job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Maintenance work in student housing runs at a different pace than conventional multifamily. PeakMade Real Estate manages off-campus student communities, and in that environment, turns happen fast, residents cycle annually, and the expectation for responsiveness is high. This Maintenance Technician role at their Murfreesboro, Tennessee community puts you at the center of all of it.

What You'll Actually Do

The daily rhythm here covers the full range of maintenance craft. Service requests come in across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliances, and you're expected to troubleshoot and complete those repairs thoroughly, not pass them up the chain. You'll work alongside the Maintenance Supervisor to keep inventory at functional levels, hold to a preventative maintenance schedule, and track pool chemistry with accurate chemical logs. Turns are a real part of the calendar in student housing, so you'll participate in make-ready events, assist with move-in and move-out processes, and help keep the punch list moving. Curb appeal, breezeway cleanliness, and exterior upkeep are daily expectations, not seasonal ones. You'll also rotate on-call for after-hours emergencies, which is an honest commitment this role requires.

PeakMade offers a facilities leadership program and technical certifications including HVAC and CPO. For a technician who wants to grow toward a Maintenance Supervisor role, those aren't minor perks. They're a structured path.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of maintenance experience, ideally in the apartment industry
  • Ability to troubleshoot and repair HVAC, plumbing, electrical systems, and appliances
  • EPA Type I and II certification preferred
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Your own hand tools (required)
  • Reliable transportation and the ability to live within 30 miles of the property
  • Availability for weekends, holidays, and rotating on-call coverage
  • Physical ability to lift up to 50 pounds, work at heights on ladders, and perform tasks outdoors in both heat and cold

The Craft This Role Develops

Student housing maintenance builds a specific kind of competence. Because lease cycles compress everything into defined windows, you'll develop real speed on turns without sacrificing quality. Working across a full system range, rather than calling out to specialists for every trade, builds the diagnostic confidence that separates strong technicians from average ones. Technicians who come out of student housing typically carry broader hands-on experience than peers from conventional multifamily, and that breadth matters when pursuing senior or supervisory roles later. The candidate who thrives here is someone who takes ownership of their work area, communicates clearly with residents even when the situation is frustrating, and treats the preventative maintenance schedule as a professional standard rather than a suggestion.

job.title: Community Manager Manufactured Housing Community Plus Housing
job.description:
Community management in manufactured housing demands a different skill set than conventional multifamily. Rent collection, delinquency follow-through, and lease enforcement matter in any asset class, but in a land-lease or home-ownership MHC, you're also coordinating with residents who have a deeper physical stake in the community. They own their homes. The relationships are longer, the grievances can be more personal, and the community dynamics require someone who genuinely knows how to build trust alongside enforcing rules.

What This Role Requires Day to Day

Alpine Vista Village is a 123-home community in Loveland, and Investment Property Group is looking for a Community Manager to run it. The core of the job involves financial oversight (rent collection, bi-monthly deposits, delinquency review, and accounting reporting), staff management (hiring, training, evaluations, and coaching), and resident relations that range from routine service requests to formal grievance processes. You'll also manage compliance with regulatory requirements, fair housing law, and company policies, and serve as the point of contact for local development agencies and law enforcement when needed.

On the leasing side, you'll oversee the application and move-in process for new residents, and you'll use marketing and sales skills to keep occupancy strong. Loveland's Front Range location means steady regional demand, but occupancy in MHC requires active management of lot availability and home inventory, so those skills carry real weight here.

Living on site is required. The position includes a two-bedroom, two-bathroom manufactured home with a fenced backyard and storage shed. This isn't incidental to the job. On-site presence is a functional part of how a community this size operates well.

Skills This Role Puts to Work

  • Delinquency management and resident account review, including understanding when to escalate to legal work-up
  • Staff leadership across a small on-site team, including performance coaching and accountability
  • Conflict resolution with residents who have long tenures and strong opinions about community standards
  • Compliance tracking for regulatory reporting to partner agencies
  • Property management software and basic accounting systems for daily operations
  • Occupancy and traffic management through active marketing of available lots or homes

Qualifications and What Sets Strong Candidates Apart

IPG is looking for at least one year of management experience at a manufactured housing or multifamily community of 100 or more units. Beyond that baseline, the candidates who tend to excel in roles like this one are the ones who can hold firm on community rules without creating adversarial relationships. In MHC, that balance matters more than in conventional apartments, because you're dealing with people who may have lived in the community for a decade or more. Patient consistency beats reactive enforcement every time.

Strong written and verbal communication skills are important here because you're regularly interfacing with residents, contractors, local agencies, and your own staff. The ability to stay organized through frequent interruptions, while keeping longer-term operational goals on track, is something IPG specifically calls out as a differentiator.

Compensation runs from $26 to $30 per hour depending on experience, plus the on-site home. Investment Property Group operates 150 properties across 13 states, which means real room for advancement for managers who perform well and want to grow within the company.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Skills This Role Puts to Work Every Day

Leasing consulting is a craft that sits at the intersection of sales, hospitality, and administration. At The Edison Apartments in Memphis, you'll draw on all three. The core skill at work here is relationship-building: converting traffic into signed leases requires genuine rapport, sharp listening, and the ability to match a prospect's needs to the right unit quickly. You'll also use written and verbal communication constantly, whether that's drafting follow-up emails, walking a prospect through lease terms, or handling a current resident's concern at the front desk.

Mathematical reasoning matters more in leasing than many candidates expect. You'll work with pricing, concessions, and occupancy figures regularly, and you need to be comfortable enough with numbers to answer questions accurately on the spot. A two-year leasing background gives you the foundation to do that without hesitation.

What the Day-to-Day Actually Develops

Beyond the skills you arrive with, this role builds others. Resident retention is a discipline on its own. Keeping an occupied unit from going on notice requires understanding what residents value, catching friction early, and following through consistently. That's a different skill set than closing a new lease, and this position asks you to practice both.

The administrative side of leasing, including file accuracy, reporting, and lease documentation, sharpens your attention to detail in ways that pay dividends if you move toward an Assistant Manager or Property Manager role later. Many strong leasing consultants treat the admin work as secondary, but the ones who advance treat it as a parallel competency. This is also where a working knowledge of fair housing law becomes non-negotiable. You'll apply it daily, and doing it well is what separates a professional leasing consultant from someone just showing apartments.

Saturday hours are part of this position. Weekends are typically when prospect traffic peaks, so Saturday availability is a practical necessity, not an afterthought.

What Makes This Role Worth Considering

Makowsky Ringel Greenberg is a Memphis-based firm with a long operating history in the local market. Working for a regional operator means you're close to decision-makers and you'll learn how a property fits into a broader portfolio rather than executing directives handed down from a national platform. That proximity can accelerate your development in ways that larger institutional environments sometimes don't allow.

The compensation structure here includes a bonus and commission program alongside base pay, which rewards performance directly. The benefits package covers medical, dental, disability, and additional insurance options, along with a 401(k) and profit-sharing plan.

  • Two years of leasing experience preferred
  • Valid driver's license, reliable transportation, and proof of insurance required
  • Strong English communication skills, written and verbal
  • Comfortable with basic mathematical reasoning
  • Saturday availability required
  • High school diploma or equivalent

If you take the craft of leasing seriously and want a role where both your sales ability and your operational attention get tested, The Edison is a reasonable place to build that record.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
It's 7 a.m. on a Monday. Two units need to turn by Friday, a vendor is arriving at nine to work on the HVAC system, and there are six open service requests from the weekend. Your job is to make sure all of it gets handled, in order, without cutting corners.

CommonPlace operates communities in Charlotte built around the idea that where you live shapes how you feel about home. The Maintenance Supervisor role sits at the center of that. You're running the maintenance operation day-to-day: scheduling your team, overseeing make-readies, managing vendor quality, and keeping the property safe and presentable. You're also the person who shows up for after-hours emergencies and makes the call when something unexpected needs immediate attention.

What the Job Covers

This is a supervisory role with a hands-on component. You'll manage a maintenance team, which means hiring, training, scheduling, and holding people accountable to CommonPlace's standards. You'll also work alongside them when the job requires it.

  • Lead unit turns and make-ready coordination to keep units move-in ready on schedule
  • Perform and oversee preventative maintenance across apartments, amenities, and grounds
  • Manage vendor work on property, including quality control and compliance
  • Handle inventory, supply orders, and tool maintenance
  • Maintain OSHA compliance, safety policies, MSDS sheets, and replacement logs
  • Assist with bidding and project planning as the Property Manager requests
  • Execute lock changes following evictions or other situations requiring rekeying
  • Participate in on-call rotation and respond to emergencies as needed
  • Manage snow and ice removal to keep the property accessible and safe

What You Need to Bring

CommonPlace is looking for someone with 3 to 5 years of hands-on maintenance experience in property management, plus 1 to 3 years leading a team. You need working knowledge of plumbing, electrical systems, HVAC, appliances, and general construction. This is a physical role: you'll regularly lift and carry up to 50 lbs and work with hand tools, power tools, and motorized equipment.

Strong communication matters here. You're the link between the maintenance team and the Property Manager. When something unusual happens on the property, you need to flag it clearly and quickly. A valid driver's license and proof of auto liability insurance are required.

One thing that separates strong candidates from average ones in this role: the ability to manage turns efficiently under schedule pressure while keeping service request response times from slipping. Those two demands compete for the same team hours. Supervisors who can sequence the work and set realistic daily priorities tend to run tighter operations than those who react to whatever feels most urgent at the moment.

CommonPlace offers medical, dental, vision, and 401(k) benefits, along with paid vacation, sick time, and volunteer time. The company emphasizes internal growth for team members who perform and want to build a career in property management.

job.title: Maintenance Tech | High-Rise Residential - Downtown Austin
job.description:
High-rise maintenance is its own discipline. Garden-style work doesn't fully prepare you for it. Vertical buildings demand coordination with freight elevators, stricter vendor access protocols, and a working knowledge of centralized building systems that a 200-unit garden community simply doesn't have. Worth Ross Management Company operates at the luxury end of the market, and this Downtown Austin property near Republic Square reflects that.

The Day-to-Day Reality

The schedule is Monday through Friday, 8 to 5, which is cleaner than a lot of maintenance positions in this industry. On-call rotation exists, so after-hours emergencies are part of the deal, but the standard week has structure. Day to day, you're running preventative maintenance on building systems and common areas, turning work orders on basic plumbing, electrical, drywall, painting, and carpentry, and keeping lobbies, hallways, and amenity spaces in the kind of condition residents paying luxury rents actually expect. You'll coordinate vendor and contractor access, which in a high-rise means managing freight elevator scheduling and making sure work is completed to spec. Move-in and move-out support is part of the rotation as well.

WRMC is specific about the resident-facing piece. This isn't a building where you can leave a half-finished repair for two days. Communication matters. If you've worked in hospitality maintenance or higher-end multifamily before, that instinct toward service quality will translate directly.

What the Role Requires

  • One to three years of maintenance experience in residential, commercial, hospitality, or property management settings
  • Working hands-on knowledge of HVAC (filter replacements and basic service), plumbing, electrical, drywall, painting, and carpentry
  • Ability to troubleshoot independently and manage competing priorities without a lot of hand-holding
  • Strong communication with residents and a professional, composed approach under pressure
  • EPA Certification preferred, or willingness to obtain it
  • High school diploma or GED required
  • Valid driver's license may be required depending on property needs

Vendor coordination experience is a genuine plus here, not just filler language. In a building this size and at this service level, contractor relationships and oversight are a real part of the job.

Benefits include medical, dental, vision, short and long-term disability, an employee assistance program, identity theft protection, pet insurance, retirement, and paid time off.

One thing worth knowing: technicians who start in luxury high-rise maintenance tend to develop a skill set that opens doors. Building systems experience, vendor management exposure, and resident service standards at this level are all credentials that carry weight if you eventually move toward a lead tech or building engineer path.

job.title: Community Administrator
job.description:
Administrative work in community association management draws on a specific mix of skills: clear written and verbal communication, the ability to keep multiple tasks organized without losing track of the details, and a steady, professional presence when residents or vendors walk through the door. This role at Taylor Management Company puts all three to work daily.

What the Work Looks Like

You'll be supporting the Community Manager for a condominium association in Little Falls Township, handling the day-to-day administrative needs that keep the office running. That means managing correspondence, tracking requests, coordinating with vendors, and serving as a first point of contact for residents who have questions or concerns. Condominium communities generate a consistent volume of owner communications, violation notices, maintenance coordination, and meeting documentation. Staying on top of that volume without letting things slip requires real organizational discipline, not just a general willingness to multitask.

The schedule is Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., and the position is fully onsite at the community. There's no travel to other properties. The salary is $50,000 annually, and the position is available immediately.

Skills That Carry Weight Here

Prior administrative experience matters here. Candidates who've worked in a condominium or HOA setting before will have a genuine advantage, because community association offices operate differently from corporate admin environments. Owners expect responsiveness. Governance documents create specific procedural obligations. Vendors need to be tracked against work orders. Someone who's already familiar with that rhythm will contribute faster.

That said, no certification is required. Strong candidates coming from other service-oriented administrative roles, such as property management support, legal offices, or healthcare administration, can transfer well if they bring genuine attention to detail and a patient, professional manner with people who may be frustrated when they walk in.

What separates strong candidates in this specific role is comfort with the repetitive-but-consequential nature of community association admin. Tracking an unresolved maintenance issue, following up on a vendor who hasn't confirmed, making sure a board meeting packet goes out on time: these tasks aren't glamorous, but letting them slip creates problems that are hard to walk back in a community where owners are also property owners with skin in the game.

The Company Behind the Role

Taylor Management Company is a New Jersey-based third-party management firm with a long history in community association management across the state. Working for a fee management company means the community's manager answers to a board of directors and to the management firm's standards simultaneously. As an administrator, you sit inside that structure and help it function smoothly. For someone interested in growing into a Community Manager role over time, this position offers direct exposure to how a professionally managed condominium operates, from financial coordination to compliance to resident relations.

job.title: Senior Vice President of Operations
job.description:
The call comes in on a Tuesday in October. A regional director flags that a mid-size student housing asset in a secondary market is running 12 points behind occupancy compared to the prior lease-up cycle, and the owner is asking questions. You've seen the T-12, you know the market, and within an hour you're aligning the regional team on a recovery plan that touches pricing, concessions, and leasing activity. That's the texture of this role.

The Scope

Yugo is a global student living brand managing communities across multiple international markets, and this SVP of Operations position sits at the top of the U.S. operating structure, reporting directly to the President. The portfolio exceeds 40 student housing communities nationally, with the expectation that it will continue to grow. Beyond direct portfolio performance, this role carries real responsibility for the third-party management business: building owner relationships, supporting new business development, and integrating incoming management assignments smoothly into the platform.

You'll lead through a layer of senior and regional operations leaders, so the ability to drive accountability through others matters as much as your own instincts. The role carries full ownership of NOI, revenue, occupancy, delinquency, and bad debt across the portfolio. You'll partner closely with Finance on budgets and forecasts, coordinate with Sales, Marketing, and Revenue Management to keep leasing strategy and execution aligned, and work with Facilities leadership on operational consistency. When assets underperform, you're the one building the recovery strategy and holding the organization accountable for executing it.

Resident experience sits alongside financial performance as a genuine measure of success here. NPS, reputation data, and service delivery standards all feed into how this role is evaluated, which reflects how Yugo positions itself in the student housing market.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • 12 or more years of progressive leadership in student housing, multifamily, or a related real estate operating environment
  • Meaningful experience managing large, geographically dispersed portfolios through regional leadership teams
  • A real track record in third-party fee management, including owner relationship development and new business integration
  • Deep financial fluency: P&L ownership, annual budgeting, forecasting discipline, and NOI performance management
  • Specific experience with student housing leasing cycles, occupancy strategy, and the timing pressures that come with academic calendars
  • Demonstrated success turning around underperforming assets, not just stabilizing performing ones
  • The credibility to represent the company externally with owners, partners, and industry audiences

Student housing operates on a leasing calendar that doesn't forgive slow decisions. The window to correct occupancy heading into the next academic year closes faster than in conventional multifamily. Candidates who've only managed conventional portfolios often underestimate how compressed the response cycle is. Experience specifically in student housing, or at minimum a clear understanding of pre-lease pacing and its relationship to annual revenue, separates strong candidates from those who need time to calibrate.

From a career trajectory standpoint, this role is a natural landing point for someone who has run regional operations at scale and wants full P&L ownership at the portfolio level. It also builds the kind of cross-functional leadership experience, finance partnership, client management, organizational development, that tends to open doors to President or COO roles over time. The third-party management dimension is worth noting specifically: executives who can grow and retain fee management clients carry a skillset that translates broadly across the industry, where fee compression and client retention are ongoing concerns for most platforms.

job.title: Apartment Leasing Sales Consultant - The Sanctuary
job.description:
Leasing at a high-performing AIR community is fundamentally a sales role, and The Sanctuary in Las Vegas makes that clear from day one. The skills this position puts to work daily are pipeline management, objection handling, consultative selling, and conversion tracking. If those words make you sharpen your pencil rather than glaze over, keep reading.

The Sales Skills This Role Runs On

This isn't a greeting-and-showing job. AIR builds tiered commission structures that reward specific behaviors: closing on longer lease terms (18 months and up), upgrading prospects to higher-rent units with better finishes or views, and consistently beating monthly leasing goals across multiple performance tiers. Base pay starts at $20.00 per hour, but total annual compensation ranges from $55,000 to well over $112,000 depending on how you perform. That ceiling is real, and the structure is transparent about how you get there.

The day-to-day mechanics look like this: you're managing a live prospect pipeline, logging every touchpoint in AIR's leasing platform, scheduling and running tours, and following up fast enough to keep warm leads from going cold in a competitive Las Vegas rental market. You're reading each prospect's priorities (budget, move-in timing, floor plan preferences, view) and matching them to the right unit. You're asking for the close. You're handling the objections that come back before you get there. Traffic matters, but conversion is the number that actually moves your performance metrics.

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

Experience in apartment leasing is useful but not required. What actually predicts performance in this role is a track record of hitting or exceeding sales goals in any environment: retail, hospitality, SaaS, car sales, insurance. The consultative piece matters more than product knowledge. Prospects choosing a home are making a significant financial and personal decision. The consultants who close consistently are the ones who listen first and present options second, then hold the conversation through to a signed lease rather than handing off a brochure and hoping.

  • At least one year of goal-oriented sales, leasing, or customer-facing experience
  • Demonstrated ability to meet or exceed conversion and revenue targets
  • Comfortable with CRM and leasing technology, or quick to learn it
  • Available to work weekends; hours shift with season and community need
  • Reliable transportation and strong written and verbal English communication

Working at AIR Communities

AIR offers a 25% rent discount at any community in its portfolio, including the option to live on-site at The Sanctuary with zero commute. The company also offers a possible extended winter break after peak leasing season, an unpaid stretch during which benefits and the rent discount remain active. Beyond compensation, the benefits package includes medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with employer contribution, up to 16 weeks of paid parental leave, and tuition assistance with full reimbursement for job-related certifications. For someone building a career in residential property management, a leasing consultant role at a portfolio operator like AIR is a legitimate launchpad: strong closers here move into senior leasing, assistant manager, and community manager tracks, where the occupancy and NOI decisions get broader.

Fair Housing compliance is a non-negotiable part of the role. Pre-employment screening includes reference checks, drug screening (marijuana excluded), and a background check.

job.title: Full-Time Senior Concierge - Morning, Mid, Evening
job.description:
Village Green has been managing multifamily communities since 1919, which means they've had a long time to figure out what resident experience actually looks like in practice. This Senior Concierge role at their Shaker Heights property sits at the center of that experience: you're the first face residents, guests, and prospects see, and a lot of what happens next depends on how that first interaction goes.

What the Day Actually Looks Like

Shifts run morning, mid, and evening, and the site operates with that full coverage in mind. Day to day, you're managing the front desk and lobby, retrieving packages, directing visitors, handling service request intake, and making sure residents feel like someone's actually paying attention. When the leasing office is closed or traffic picks up unexpectedly, you step into a leasing support role: distributing floor plans and brochures, completing guest cards, doing mini-tours, and answering prospect questions. You're not expected to close leases, but you are expected to keep warm leads warm.

Communication is a real part of this job. You'll contribute to resident newsletters and social media touchpoints, so being able to write clearly and represent the community's voice matters more than most concierge postings let on. You'll also field questions about local restaurants, transit, and neighborhood amenities. Knowing Shaker Heights helps; it's a walkable, transit-adjacent suburb with a distinct character, and residents who choose to live there tend to ask specific questions about it.

What You Bring

  • High school diploma or GED at minimum
  • Real customer service experience, ideally in hospitality, multifamily, or a resident-facing role
  • Comfort with social media and basic written communication
  • Flexibility to work any shift across any day of the week
  • Strong organizational habits and the judgment to handle minor conflicts without escalating everything
  • Team orientation. This is a shift-based role, and handoffs matter.

Where This Role Tends to Lead

Concierge roles at well-run communities are genuinely good entry points into property management. The people who move up from this position are the ones who treat it as a learning post: they watch how the leasing team handles traffic, they learn fair housing basics without being told to, and they develop a feel for resident relations that carries into assistant manager or leasing consultant roles down the line. Village Green's size (a century-old company with a national footprint) means internal movement is realistic, not just something written in an offer letter.

Pay runs $17.49 to $22.50 hourly with a bonus program. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, and a 401(k) with a company match.

job.title: Floating Maintenance Technician - Commercial Buildings
job.description:
What This Role Covers

Cirrus Asset Management manages commercial properties across Redondo Beach and LA County, and this floating technician position keeps those buildings running. Floating means exactly that: you move between retail, mall, and industrial sites based on where work orders are queued, which keeps the day varied but also demands someone who can walk into an unfamiliar mechanical room and quickly assess what's in front of them.

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, with occasional early 7 AM starts and on-call availability for emergencies. The hourly range is $23 to $25, depending on experience.

Day-to-Day Responsibilities

Work orders drive the day. You'll handle electrical maintenance (bulb and socket replacements, circuit breaker panel cleaning and repair), plumbing and heating components, and door hardware including locks, closers, and controllers. Grounds and curb appeal are part of the scope too, held to both company and client standards.

Documentation carries real weight in this role. You'll maintain records for fire extinguishers, fire suppression systems, and building alarm contacts. That paper trail matters for compliance and for client-facing reporting, so accuracy isn't optional. You'll also document work performance and materials procurement as directed.

  • Complete work orders within designated time frames across multiple properties
  • Inspect and repair mechanical systems to meet health and safety standards
  • Maintain and repair plumbing, heating, locks, doors, and entry systems
  • Track and document fire safety systems and building alarm contacts
  • Maintain grounds and exterior appearance at each site
  • Participate in ongoing technical, safety, and operational training

What Cirrus Is Looking For

At least one year of hands-on experience in retail, mall, or industrial maintenance is required. Commercial buildings have different demands than residential: tenant hours, code compliance expectations, and the pace of work orders across a portfolio all add complexity that general maintenance experience alone won't prepare you for. Relevant certifications in electrical or systems maintenance (CMRP, for example) will strengthen your application. A high school diploma is required.

You need reliable transportation. Properties span Redondo Beach and LA County, and the ability to move between sites on short notice is core to how this role functions.

Strong candidates here tend to be self-starters who don't need a supervisor on site to prioritize correctly. With a floating structure, you're often the senior decision-maker in the moment: triaging which work order is time-sensitive, spotting something on a walkthrough that wasn't on the original punch list, and communicating clearly back to the team. Attention to detail and problem-solving instincts matter more than any single technical specialty.

Cirrus offers health, dental, and vision insurance, life insurance, paid holidays, sick time, vacation, and a 401(k) plan, along with healthcare spending or reimbursement accounts.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
A tenant calls at 8:47 a.m. about an HVAC issue that's been unresolved for three days. You pull the work order, contact the vendor, and have a scheduled visit confirmed before 9:30. That kind of quiet coordination is the core of this role, and it's also where you start building the skills that carry you through a long career in commercial property management.

The Role at Stream Realty Partners

Stream Realty Partners, founded in Dallas in 1996, operates as a full-service commercial real estate firm with billions in annual transaction volume across office, industrial, retail, healthcare, and other asset classes. This Assistant Property Manager position supports Property Managers across a portfolio of commercial properties, with hands-on involvement in building operations, tenant relations, vendor coordination, and financial reporting.

Day-to-day, you'll field work order requests and route them to the right building technician or vendor, schedule move-ins and move-outs, and verify tenant insurance. On the financial side, you'll handle accounts receivable follow-up, invoice coding, and billback processing, and you'll help prepare monthly reporting packages and annual operating budgets. Operating expense reconciliations, lease compliance review, and support for insurance and electricity procurement are also part of the mix. After-hours emergency calls come with the territory, as they do in most commercial PM roles.

Stream lists experience with platforms like Yardi, MRI, Kardin, or AvidXchange as preferred, which reflects how heavily system fluency matters in commercial management. If you've worked in any of these tools, you'll have a shorter ramp-up period. If you haven't, prioritize learning the workflow logic behind them, because the software changes but the underlying processes don't.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • At least two years of experience in commercial property management
  • Solid understanding of lease types and how they affect billing and compliance
  • Experience with accounts receivable follow-up and professional tenant communication
  • Comfort with invoice coding and basic accounting processes
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and Word
  • Familiarity with real estate software platforms (Yardi, MRI, Kardin, AvidXchange, or similar)
  • A bachelor's degree is preferred but the posting doesn't treat it as a hard filter

What separates people who grow quickly in roles like this from those who plateau is the ability to read the financial side of a property, not just the operational side. Assistant managers who understand how NOI connects to owner reporting, how opex reconciliations flow through to tenant billbacks, and how budget variances get explained to clients tend to move into Property Manager seats faster. Stream's platform, with its breadth across asset classes and markets, gives you real exposure to that progression if you're genuinely curious about how the numbers work alongside the day-to-day operations.

This is a Dallas-based, on-site position at a firm that's built its reputation on a people-first culture. If you're looking to grow inside commercial real estate services rather than transition into investment or development, the APM track at a firm like Stream is one of the more practical places to start building that foundation.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
Bozzuto operates across the full property management spectrum, from development and construction to day-to-day operations at communities that tend to set the bar in their local markets. The Assistant Property Manager role at their West Harrison, NY location sits at the center of site operations. You're the connective tissue between leasing activity, resident experience, and financial performance.

Day to day, this role moves fast. You're collecting rent, working delinquency before it becomes a problem, conducting tours that close leases, and keeping the property looking the part inside and out. When the Property Manager is off-site, you run the show. That's not ceremonial. Bozzuto expects the APM to carry real operational weight.

The financial piece matters here. You'll have exposure to P&L, budgets, and revenue management. Candidates who've only leased apartments without touching the numbers side will find this role stretches them. That's a good thing if you're ready for it, but go in knowing the expectation is full-cycle accountability, not just traffic and leases.

The schedule includes one to two weekends per month. Weekend days off shift to weekdays. That's standard for residential property management, worth knowing upfront if you haven't worked that rotation before.

What Bozzuto is Looking For

  • Four-year degree or equivalent experience in property management, hospitality, or retail
  • At least two years in a relevant customer-facing or operations role
  • Comfort with P&L, budget exposure, and revenue basics
  • Yardi experience preferred; general tech competency required
  • Active use of social media platforms for community marketing
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Genuine sales aptitude, not just a willingness to try

The salary range for this position is $75,000 to $80,000, with additional bonus potential. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

For candidates thinking longer term: APM roles at well-run companies like Bozzuto are a direct track to Property Manager. The skills you build here, managing delinquency, reading a budget, coaching a team, translate cleanly into senior site leadership or regional operations. West Harrison puts you in a competitive Westchester County submarket, which gives you exposure to residents and ownership expectations at a level that sharpens your instincts faster than softer markets will.

job.title: Centralized Painter, IFM - Colorado Springs, CO
job.description:
This role lives at the intersection of speed and craft. A Centralized Painter on Cortland's Integrated Facilities Management team works across a portfolio of multifamily properties in Colorado Springs, responsible for keeping unit turns moving and finished surfaces looking sharp. The work is production-oriented, but the standard is high.

Core Skills This Role Uses Daily

Spray application is central here, not just brush and roller work. You need solid spray-prep skills, an understanding of equipment maintenance, and the discipline to keep coatings consistent across units. Texture matching matters too. Drywall patching and blending into existing finishes is a routine part of the job, not an occasional extra. The expectation is one full repaint or two touch-up units per day, so you're managing your own pace and sequencing without a supervisor directing each step.

You also need to be organized. You're maintaining a paint shop, tracking materials, logging completed work in a CMMS, and flagging anything that threatens the schedule. That administrative layer is part of the role, not optional.

What the Day Actually Looks Like

You'll drive between assigned properties, assess the day's unit turns, pull materials, and execute. Some days that means a full repaint from prep to finish coat. Other days it's a series of touch-ups, patch-and-texture work, and prep for the next day's units. You'll coordinate with service managers to stay aligned on priorities, and you'll communicate with residents or building staff when your work intersects with occupied spaces.

Exterior surfaces and elevated work come up regularly, so comfort on ladders, lifts, and scaffolding is a baseline requirement, as is working knowledge of OSHA standards and MSDS protocols.

What Makes a Strong Candidate Here

Two or more years of interior residential painting gets you in the conversation. What separates strong candidates is spray proficiency combined with genuine texture-matching ability. A lot of painters can roll a unit. Fewer can match a knockdown or orange peel finish well enough that a resident doesn't notice the patch. If you have custom home painting in your background, that attention to finish quality translates well here.

  • 2+ years of interior residential painting experience
  • Proficient with brush, roller, and spray equipment
  • Able to perform drywall patching, sanding, and texture matching
  • Valid driver's license with required vehicle insurance
  • Comfortable working at heights (ladders, lifts, scaffolding)
  • Familiar with CMMS platforms or willing to learn quickly
  • Available for weekend shifts when needed

Cortland operates at scale across its portfolio, which means the systems and support behind this role are real. Materials, equipment, and process infrastructure are in place. What they need from you is the trade skill and the reliability to execute consistently across multiple sites without hand-holding.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Commercial maintenance work pulls from a wider skill set than most people expect. You're reading equipment manuals, logging chemical consumption, interpreting fire alarm systems, adjusting HVAC controls, and occasionally crawling into a confined space to chase down a problem. This role at Stream Realty Partners in Austin asks for all of it.

What the Work Actually Covers

Stream operates across office, industrial, retail, and multifamily properties, and this technician role sits on the commercial side of that portfolio. Day-to-day, you'll handle preventive maintenance and repairs across mechanical, electrical, plumbing, and HVAC systems. That includes pumps, chillers, boilers, air handling units, and air compressors. You'll also manage the routine stuff: fixtures, appliances, plumbing repairs, and work order resolution. Where HVAC controls need adjustment, you're expected to make a reasonable call, not just escalate everything.

Accurate recordkeeping is part of the job, not a side task. Central plant operation logs, chemical consumption records, and equipment inspection reports keep the property compliant and give the engineering team the data they need. You'll also participate in water treatment chemical programs and develop working knowledge of the building's fire alarm and life safety systems.

The schedule note is worth reading carefully. Shifts can include early mornings, evenings, weekends, and holidays depending on the property's needs. Overtime happens when the building demands it. Emergencies don't wait for business hours, and this role requires a calm head when something goes sideways at 7 PM on a Friday.

Skills That Drive This Role

  • Hands-on experience with commercial building systems (HVAC, electrical, plumbing, hydraulics)
  • Comfort with power tools: pneumatic, electric, drill motors, grinders, impact wrenches
  • Ability to read and follow equipment manuals and written instructions accurately
  • Basic math for calculations tied to equipment operation or chemical programs
  • Clear verbal and written communication with building occupants and internal teams
  • Safe handling of personal protective equipment and adherence to property safety policies
  • Willingness to obtain EPA Universal Certification within 90 days of hire

A high school diploma, GED, or trade school credential is preferred. If the assigned property requires a Boiler Operating Permit, State Maintenance Electrician's License, or similar, you'll be expected to obtain those as applicable. The physical side of this job is real: expect to split time evenly between indoor and outdoor work, climb stairs and ladders, access rooftops and crawl spaces, and lift 50 pounds or more regularly.

Where This Role Fits at Stream

Stream was founded in 1996 and has grown into one of the larger full-service commercial real estate firms in the country, operating coast to coast from its Dallas headquarters. The engineering and maintenance team here carries direct responsibility for how the buildings perform and how occupants experience them day to day. That's not a small thing in commercial property management, where tenant satisfaction ties directly to lease renewals and NOI.

For technicians early in their commercial careers, this kind of role builds fast. You're working across multiple systems on properties that range in complexity, which compresses the learning curve compared to residential maintenance. A technician who develops real proficiency with central plant operations and building controls over a couple of years is well-positioned to move into a lead tech or chief engineer track. Stream's scale means that path exists internally if you want it.

Stream offers medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with company match, PTO, holiday pay, and an HSA option. Compensation varies by experience and qualifications.

job.title: Senior Revenue Manager
job.description:
It's 7:45 AM on a Tuesday and the weekly revenue call starts in fifteen minutes. One community is sitting at 88% occupied with sixty days of exposure stacking up, and the pricing model just recommended a rate increase. You already know why. You also know you're going to override it, document the rationale, and have a corrective action on the Regional Manager's desk before noon.

That's the job. Morguard is hiring a Senior Revenue Manager to own pricing discipline and revenue optimization across their U.S. multifamily residential portfolio. This is an operating role with real decision authority, not an analytics function that produces dashboards for someone else to act on.

What the Role Actually Covers

The scope here is broad and intentionally so. You'll own new lease pricing, renewal offers, concession thresholds, lease-term premiums, move-in date management, and lease expiration staggering across the full portfolio. That means translating occupancy trends, leased percentage, exposure, trade-outs, traffic, conversion, and seasonality into asset-specific actions that protect both rent growth and occupancy targets simultaneously. These two things are in tension constantly. Managing that tension is the skill.

You'll also serve as the business owner for Morguard's Revenue Intelligence pricing platform, which includes configuration, audit, vendor engagement, user adoption, and system governance. When the model's optimal-rate suggestions conflict with ground-level reality, you make the call and document why. You'll monitor recommendation adoption rates, publishing accuracy, and data integrity across the PMS and portfolio reporting stack, catching discrepancies before they contaminate budget assumptions or drive a bad pricing decision at the community level.

On the analytics side, the expectation is concise, decision-oriented reporting: what happened, why, what comes next, and what action is required. You'll forecast occupancy, leasing velocity, rental revenue, and renewal outcomes against budget and underwriting assumptions, and you'll feed defensible inputs into annual budgets, reforecasts, acquisition due diligence, and disposition planning. Renovation premium assumptions and value-add program coordination fall in your lane as well.

Market intelligence is ongoing. You'll maintain competitive sets, monitor effective rents and concessions by submarket, and build differentiated revenue strategies for stabilized assets, lease-ups, repositioning plays, and operationally challenged properties. One portfolio-wide answer doesn't fit all of those situations, and Morguard isn't looking for someone who tries to apply one.

Cross-functional leadership is a real part of this role. You'll run structured revenue-review cadences with Regional, District, and Asset Management leaders, present performance to executive leadership, and influence field execution without relying on direct authority. Site visits and competitive market tours are part of validating data and closing execution gaps, not optional add-ons.

Fair Housing compliance, rent regulation, antitrust requirements, and applicable fee and advertising rules apply to every pricing decision in every jurisdiction. This isn't a peripheral concern here.

What Morguard Is Looking For

  • Demonstrated experience in multifamily revenue management at the portfolio level, with direct ownership of pricing strategy
  • Hands-on platform experience with a recognized revenue management system (RealPage, Yardi RMS, or equivalent), including configuration and governance
  • Strong command of leasing and revenue metrics: trade-outs, loss-to-lease, exposure, leased vs. physical occupancy, concession impact, renewal conversion
  • Ability to build and defend financial models supporting budgets, reforecasts, and acquisition assumptions
  • Experience presenting revenue performance and recommendations to senior and executive leadership
  • Working knowledge of Fair Housing, rent regulation, and antitrust compliance as they apply to pricing decisions
  • Comfort operating across asset types and business plans, including value-add and lease-up situations

The candidates who tend to succeed in portfolio revenue roles like this one are the ones who understand that the model is a starting point, not an answer. Strong pattern recognition, willingness to override with documented rationale, and the ability to influence Regional Managers who don't report to you all matter more than any single technical credential.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
The assistant property manager role occupies a specific and underrated position in multifamily operations. It's where leasing competency meets financial accountability for the first time in a career, and companies like Bozzuto use it deliberately to develop people who can eventually run a property on their own. This opening at a Bozzuto community in Waltham puts you at that intersection.

What the Role Actually Covers

Bozzuto is asking for someone who can hold multiple functions at once without losing ground in any of them. On any given day, that means collecting rent, working delinquency, and keeping the financials moving, then shifting into a tour for a prospective resident that feels personal rather than scripted. You'll coach and support team members while also stepping into the property manager seat when they're out. That's not ceremonial coverage. It means knowing the building, the residents, the numbers, and the team well enough to make decisions without backup.

The weekend rotation (one to two weekends per month, with corresponding weekdays off) reflects where leasing traffic actually lives. Prospects shop on Saturdays. Being present for that traffic is part of the job, and it's worth calibrating your expectations accordingly before you apply.

Bozzuto also expects you to handle social media content creation with some real investment, not just posting floor plan photos. If you've built a following or run campaigns for a previous community, that's worth highlighting in your application.

What to Bring and Where This Goes

  • Four-year degree or equivalent experience in property management, hospitality, or retail
  • At least two years in a client-facing, operations-adjacent role
  • Comfort with P&L basics, budget exposure, and revenue concepts
  • Yardi experience is preferred; general tech fluency is required
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, and genuine sales ability

The salary range for this position is $65,920 to $70,000, with additional bonus opportunities. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401(k) with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

From a career trajectory standpoint, strong assistant property managers typically move into property manager roles within two to three years, especially at a firm like Bozzuto that promotes internally. The skills that compound fastest here are delinquency management, team coaching, and tour-to-lease conversion. Those three things, done well and consistently, build a record that translates directly to site manager credibility. If your longer-term goal is running a Class A community or moving into a regional operations role, this is a reasonable on-ramp, provided you treat the financial side of the role with the same seriousness as the resident-facing side.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
Cortland runs a vertically integrated operation, which means a Community Manager here works inside a company that controls design, construction, and day-to-day management under one roof. That structure changes the job in concrete ways: you're not chasing down a third-party maintenance vendor or waiting on a separate ownership group to approve a capital decision. You're working within a system built for speed and accountability, and that cuts both ways. The expectations are high, and the visibility is real.

The DC multifamily market is worth naming here. The District carries a mix of Class A high-rises and mid-rise product competing hard on amenities and concessions, particularly in submarkets like NoMa, Navy Yard, and Capitol Riverfront where lease-up inventory continues to absorb. Occupancy pressures have kept traffic competitive, and strong managers here know how to read pricing tools, time concessions carefully, and keep delinquency tight without letting resident relations slip. If you've managed a community in a market like this, you already understand that NOI targets don't move just because the market softens.

The role itself centers on full P&L ownership of a multimillion-dollar apartment community. You'll lead the onsite team, manage vendor contracts, conduct property inspections, and own the financial results. That means budgeting, expense control, and using community metrics to find inefficiencies before they show up on the T-12. On the revenue side, you'll set leasing goals, coach the team on conversion, and work with Cortland's marketing partners on campaigns and social media presence. Fair Housing compliance and OSHA standards are baseline expectations, not afterthoughts.

What separates strong candidates from average ones in this role is the combination of financial discipline and genuine people leadership. A lot of managers can read a budget or run a lease-up. Fewer can build a team culture that holds together through high turnover periods or a tough renewal season, and still hit NOI. Cortland's centralized support structure gives you resources, but the onsite results are yours to own.

What Cortland is looking for

  • At least two years of measurable sales leadership in a high-velocity environment, multifamily experience preferred but hospitality, luxury retail, or similar fields considered
  • Demonstrated track record hitting or exceeding occupancy and revenue targets
  • Experience leading and developing onsite teams with clear accountability structures
  • Financial acumen across budgeting, forecasting, and expense management
  • Proficiency with property management software, CRM platforms, and Microsoft Office
  • Comfort using social media as an active leasing and brand tool
  • High school diploma required; bachelor's degree preferred

Cortland is an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity and inclusion across its workforce.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
Skills That Drive This Role

This Assistant Property Manager position at Lincoln Property Company in San Rafael puts your financial fluency and tenant relationship skills to work across commercial, industrial, and retail assets. The day runs on numbers and deadlines: monthly reporting packages, CAM reconciliations, vendor invoice reviews, and budget support all demand someone who can move quickly without letting accuracy slip. If you're comfortable calculating operating expense reconciliations and translating those figures clearly to clients and tenants, you'll fit the rhythm here. Intermediate to advanced Excel is a baseline expectation, and familiarity with AP and CMMS platforms will shorten your ramp-up significantly.

Lincoln's commercial portfolio is institutional in scale, which means your reporting has to meet client-grade standards. You're not just pulling numbers together; you're helping the Property Manager deliver packages that ownership groups actually rely on for decision-making. Lease administration is another core skill set this role exercises constantly, from initial setup through changes and terminations, coordinated across applicable systems and tied closely to tenant move-in and move-out documentation.

Day-to-Day Operational Responsibilities

On the tenant side, you'll respond to service requests and coordinate building staff and vendors to resolve issues in line with lease obligations and company procedures. Vendor management includes reviewing invoices for accuracy and compliance with the management agreement before recommvals go forward. You'll also support procurement and bidding activities as the team sources contractors and service providers.

Property inspections happen monthly at minimum, so you'll spend time on-site at assigned assets, not just behind a screen. Walk-throughs with tenants, the property manager, and tenant improvement teams are part of how you track asset condition and maintain relationships. Emergency response planning is a real part of the job, including participation in drills and training. This is a fully in-office position based in San Rafael; remote or hybrid arrangements are not available for this role.

  • Bachelor's degree preferred; 1 to 2 years of commercial real estate or related experience
  • Working knowledge of financial terms and the ability to conduct basic financial analysis
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite at an intermediate to advanced level
  • Experience with AP and CMMS systems is a plus
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills across tenant and ownership audiences
  • Organizational discipline to manage multiple reporting deadlines simultaneously

What Sets Strong Candidates Apart

CAM reconciliations are where a lot of assistant managers struggle early on. Candidates who already understand how to allocate operating expenses across a tenant roster, and who can communicate those reconciliations clearly when tenants push back, tend to build credibility fast. The salary range of $80,000 to $95,000 reflects Lincoln's expectation of someone who's already past the fundamentals. Lincoln's platform spans more than 720 million square feet across asset types, so the learning environment here is broad. Strong performers in this role typically progress toward full property management responsibility on a commercial asset within two to three years, either within Lincoln's national portfolio or with the institutional-grade experience this role builds.

job.title: Regional Manager
job.description:
Asset Living runs one of the larger third-party management portfolios in the country, spanning multifamily, build-to-rent, affordable housing, student housing, and single-family rentals. This Regional Manager role sits in Orlando and covers a portfolio of communities across those categories. You'll report up through senior leadership and own everything that happens at the site level.

The job is operational and financial in equal measure. On any given week, you're reviewing occupancy and delinquency numbers, walking properties, coaching Community Managers through personnel issues, approving vendor invoices, and signing off on leasing strategy. You're also the person who catches budget drift early, writes the monthly variance explanation, and escalates capex needs before they become emergencies. Ownership reports flow through you, and accuracy is your responsibility.

Personnel management takes a real chunk of your time. You screen and hire site staff, document performance problems correctly, handle terminations when necessary, and push salary requests through the right channels. Asset Living is a third-party management company, which means your site managers are representing both Asset and the ownership group. Consistency in how you apply company policy across your portfolio matters more than it would in a single-asset role.

On the leasing side, you build out annual marketing plans, pressure-test closing rates, and make sure your teams are executing on follow-up and lease documentation with precision. Resident retention programs, complaint resolution, and move-in experience all fall under your oversight as well.

What You Bring

  • Demonstrated experience managing a multi-site residential portfolio as a regional or area manager
  • Solid working knowledge of NOI drivers, budget development, and variance analysis
  • Experience hiring, coaching, and disciplining on-site staff across multiple locations
  • Familiarity with fair housing requirements and risk management practices
  • Ability to review and approve vendor contracts, monitor capex projects, and keep maintenance programs on schedule
  • Strong written communication skills for ownership reporting and internal documentation

One thing that separates strong candidates in this role: they don't wait for site managers to surface problems. The best regional managers build reporting habits and inspection cadences that let them see issues before they show up in the T-12. If you're the type who manages by exception and only looks closely when numbers are already off, third-party management is a tough fit. Ownership clients have limited tolerance for surprises, and Asset's reputation depends on the quality of reporting and operations that regional managers deliver.

Orlando's multifamily market has stayed active with strong rental demand, but it's also seen significant new supply come online in recent cycles. That context matters for how you position your communities on concessions, set lease-up expectations, and advise ownership on pricing strategy. Experience in a competitive Sun Belt market is a practical asset here.

job.title: Assistant Manager - Aiya
job.description:
The assistant manager role at Aiya, an Olympus Property community in Gilbert, AZ, touches almost every part of daily operations. You're not just keeping files tidy or running reports. On any given morning you might reconcile rent deposits, inspect a make-ready before a move-in, coach the leasing team through traffic, and then handle a resident complaint before lunch. The breadth is real, and it suits people who like variety more than a narrow lane.

Financially, you're responsible for making sure every dollar collected gets deposited before bank close that same day. You'll track delinquency, manage final account statements on move-outs, and step into the property manager's seat during any absence. That kind of fill-in responsibility is genuinely consequential. You're not shadowing someone; you're running the show when it counts.

Olympus earned the National Apartment Association's Top Employer designation three consecutive years (2023, 2024, 2025), which at least tells you the company is paying attention to how staff experience the work. Pay for this position runs $23 to $25 per hour depending on experience, and the role includes monthly renewal incentives and quarterly bonuses on top of base wages. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer matching, short and long-term disability, life insurance, an apartment rental allowance, educational assistance, and a sabbatical program.

The honest part: the schedule is Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM as the baseline, but resident events require some evening flexibility, and the first weekend of each month is part of the gig. After-hours issues surface in property management whether you plan for them or not. If that friction is a dealbreaker, this role will wear on you quickly. If you've worked onsite before, you already know this isn't theory.

What Olympus needs from you

  • Prior onsite apartment experience as an assistant manager or a cross-trained leasing consultant
  • Comfort with RealPage, Knock, or Onesite software (strongly preferred)
  • Familiarity with rent collection procedures, deposit protocols, and move-out disposition processes
  • Awareness of the local submarket: nearby construction, hiring trends, competing properties
  • Full-time availability with first-weekend-of-month scheduling and occasional evening events

One thing worth noting about this role as a career step: assistant managers who get comfortable with financial reporting, delinquency management, and team coordination are well-positioned to move into property manager seats. Olympus promotes from within and offers formal career pathing, so the trajectory here is real if you put in the work. Gilbert's growth as a submarket also means there's ongoing leasing activity to stay sharp on, which is genuinely useful experience for anyone building toward a senior ops role.

job.title: Groundskeeper
job.description:
Bexley at Carpenter Village sits in one of the Triangle's most active suburban corridors, where apartment communities compete hard on curb appeal and resident experience. A well-kept exterior isn't just cosmetic at a property like this. It's part of what justifies renewal rates and keeps traffic converting to leases.

What the Work Looks Like Day to Day

This is a Monday through Friday, 8am to 5pm position, which gives it a more predictable rhythm than most maintenance roles. The bulk of the work happens outdoors: litter and pet waste pickup, blowing walkways and common areas, weeding, light landscaping, and keeping the community's shared spaces presentable. You'll also handle make-ready support tasks like trashing out vacant apartments and light painting when needed. The work is physical and repetitive by nature. If daily rounds of picking up litter and cleaning pet stations sounds discouraging, this role probably isn't the right fit. If you take satisfaction in visible results and a consistent routine, it tends to suit people well.

Physical demands are real. Expect prolonged walking and standing, frequent lifting up to 50 pounds or more, operating equipment like backpack blowers and power washers, and working outdoors year-round through Carolina heat and humidity. The Cary summers are no joke, and that's worth considering honestly before you apply.

What Weinstein Properties Brings to the Table

Weinstein is a family-owned company with over 70 years in the business and a portfolio of more than 60 apartment communities across the Southeast and Mid-Atlantic. That kind of ownership structure tends to mean decisions get made closer to the property level and tenure actually gets noticed. The starting rate is $16 per hour with quarterly bonuses, and there's a $1,000 stay-on bonus available at the 90-day mark for employees in good standing. Benefits include health, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k with company match, paid holidays, vacation and sick time, and a rent discount. They also include birthday time off, which is a small thing but worth noting as a signal of the culture.

Room to Grow

Groundskeeper roles at community-focused operators like Weinstein often serve as a legitimate entry point into property maintenance careers. Team members who show initiative and a willingness to pick up new skills can work toward maintenance technician positions, where the pay ceiling and scope of responsibility increase substantially. This is a company that says explicitly it trains talent from the ground up, and a 70-year track record with a family ownership structure gives that claim more credibility than it might carry elsewhere.

  • Starting pay: $16/hour with quarterly bonuses
  • $1,000 stay-on bonus at 90 days (details discussed during recruiting)
  • Schedule: Monday through Friday, 8am to 5pm
  • Benefits: health/dental/vision, 401k with match, rent discount, paid holidays, birthday time off
  • Location: Bexley at Carpenter Village, Cary/Morrisville, NC

job.title: Community Manager - 4400 Syracuse
job.description:
Most apartment communities don't struggle because the property is bad. They struggle because the person running it is stretched too thin, undersupported, or misaligned with the ownership culture. The Community Manager role exists to close that gap: one person who holds together the team, the financials, the resident experience, and the physical asset all at once. At 4400 Syracuse Apartments in Denver, MG Properties is looking for someone who can genuinely do all of that.

What This Role Requires Day to Day

This is a full operational leadership position. You're responsible for hiring and developing your on-site team, which means you'll spend real time coaching leasing staff, holding people accountable, and building a culture that keeps turnover low on your end of the building. You're also the one watching the budget closely enough to catch problems before they become a bad T-12 story, and you're driving the marketing and leasing strategy to keep occupancy where it needs to be.

MG Properties has been acquiring, developing, and managing apartment communities across the Western U.S. for over 30 years. That kind of track record usually means a company has real systems in place, and they expect their Community Managers to work within those systems while also exercising real judgment. Yardi experience will help you hit the ground running here.

The role touches almost every relationship that matters on a property: residents with concerns, vendors who need direction, ownership who wants performance, and a team that needs steady leadership. You'll feel that breadth quickly.

Who Tends to Succeed Here

The candidates who stand out for roles like this usually have a few things in common beyond the standard qualifications list:

  • Recent, hands-on experience managing a busy apartment community (not just assistant-level exposure)
  • Demonstrated supervisory experience where they've actually developed people, not just delegated tasks
  • Comfort with budget ownership, including understanding where NOI pressure comes from and what levers they can pull
  • Familiarity with Yardi or a comparable property management platform
  • A valid driver's license and proof of insurance

The honest acknowledgment worth making: Community Manager roles carry real weight. When occupancy dips, when a key team member leaves mid-month, when a resident situation escalates, it lands on you. That's not a reason to avoid the role. It's a reason to be honest with yourself about whether you're ready for it and whether you want it.

The compensation range sits at $83,000 to $86,000 annually, with monthly and performance-based incentive bonuses, company profit sharing, a 401(k) with employer match, and a standard benefits package covering medical, dental, vision, life insurance, and flexible spending accounts. PTO, paid holidays, personal days, and sick time are also included.

This position is anticipated to be filled in December 2026, so if you're planning ahead for your next move, this is worth putting on your radar now.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
The General Manager role at Luxe Belle in Columbus runs the full operation: staff, budget, facilities, leasing performance, and the annual turn. Scion operates in student housing, which means the rhythms here differ from conventional multifamily. Move-in and move-out happen in concentrated waves tied to the academic calendar, and the GM is accountable for coordinating every piece of that.

Day-to-day, this role splits time between people management and operational oversight. You're setting staff schedules, handling escalated resident issues, walking the property monthly, and keeping a close eye on NOI. During turn season, expect to be on-site and hands-on. Scion is direct about this: the GM helps move furniture, assists with punch list items, organizes high-volume resident trash, and cleans units when needed. That's part of the job description, not an edge case.

Financial accountability is real. You'll own the annual and capital budgets, manage variance reporting, handle invoice entry, and work with the regional team on capex approvals. You're also responsible for hitting revenue targets tied to market rates, leasing velocity, and concessions. If NOI drifts, it's your job to find where and fix it.

On the people side, you'll recruit through Greenhouse, manage performance through Lattice, and run scheduling and payroll through ADP. The expectation is that you develop your team, not just manage them. Scion tracks employee experience through Qualtrics alongside resident experience, so both matter operationally.

What this role requires

  • 3 or more years managing a residential community with a team of at least 3 direct reports
  • Proficiency in a property management system, Entrata preferred
  • Comfort with budgeting tools and variance reporting (Vena experience is a plus)
  • Strong conflict management and vendor management skills
  • Availability for non-traditional hours during peak periods, emergencies, and on-call coverage
  • U.S. work authorization (no visa sponsorship available)

Candidates who do well here tend to be operationally steady under pressure and comfortable shifting from a budget spreadsheet to a move-out inspection to a staff conversation, all in the same afternoon. Student housing GMs who've managed large annual turns know how compressed the timeline gets and how much coordination it demands. That experience translates directly.

The role comes with health, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, paid parental and maternal leave, a discretionary annual bonus, and learning reimbursement. The position is exempt and based on-site at Luxe Belle.

job.title: Maintenance Technician (Jessie Street Terrace)
job.description:
Maintenance Technicians at affordable housing communities carry a different kind of weight than their market-rate counterparts. The residents at Jessie Street Terrace in Santa Cruz aren't choosing between properties based on amenity packages. Consistent, safe, well-maintained housing is foundational to their stability. That context shapes everything about this role.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

MidPen Housing has managed affordable communities across Northern California since 1970, and their maintenance standards reflect that depth of experience. At Jessie Street Terrace, you'll report to the Community Manager and handle a broad technical scope: electrical repairs across appliances, fixtures, and circuits; plumbing work on water and sewage systems; rough and finish carpentry; and landscaping and irrigation upkeep. Unit turns are part of the rhythm here. When a resident vacates, you're responsible for getting that unit back to move-in ready condition within established timeframes, which means painting, flooring, fixture installation, and whatever punch list the unit demands.

You'll also carry oversight responsibilities for Maintenance Groundskeeper staff, which means coaching and training junior team members, not just completing your own task list. On the contractor side, you'll assist with bidding, scheduling, and monitoring outside vendors, so basic project coordination skills matter. Preventive maintenance schedules, work order documentation, and inventory management round out the administrative side of the position.

On-call rotation is a real part of this job. You'll cover seven consecutive days of 24/7 emergency availability on a rotating basis, including evenings, weekends, and holidays. Anyone considering this role should factor that into the decision.

Qualifications That Actually Matter Here

  • High school diploma or GED plus at least three years of maintenance experience, ideally in property management settings
  • Strong plumbing knowledge and hands-on electrical repair experience across appliances, circuits, and fixtures
  • Rough and finish carpentry skills with the ability to handle both structural and cosmetic repairs
  • Landscaping and irrigation system experience
  • Comfort with basic computer tools for work order tracking and documentation
  • Basic OSHA safety knowledge
  • Valid California driver's license, reliable transportation, and current auto insurance
  • Physical ability to lift up to 50 lbs regularly, work in all weather conditions, and handle tasks that involve climbing, bending, and confined spaces

Compensation and a Useful Detail

Pay runs from $22.50 to $25.32 per hour, based on experience. One thing worth noting: MidPen offers company-provided on-site housing availability at this property, which is rare and can be a meaningful part of total compensation in a high-cost market like Santa Cruz. Benefits include health, dental, vision, life and disability insurance, a 403(b) retirement plan, paid parental leave, education reimbursement, FSA options, an employee assistance program, pet insurance, and paid time off including wellness days and company holidays.

Technicians who do well in affordable housing maintenance often develop a well-rounded skill set faster than peers working specialized roles at larger market-rate communities. The scope here, technical repairs, unit turns, contractor coordination, and staff mentorship, covers ground that typically takes years to accumulate at properties with deeper crew structures. That breadth tends to open doors to lead maintenance or facilities management roles over time.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager (Leasing & Experience Manager I) - Villages
job.description:
Prometheus Real Estate Group has been operating in the Bay Area since 1965, and as the largest privately held apartment owner in the region, they think about real estate in decades rather than quarters. That long-term mindset shapes how they operate their communities, and it shapes how they develop their people. This Leasing and Experience Manager role at their Villages property in Cupertino sits right at that intersection.

The title signals something worth taking seriously. Prometheus doesn't call this role an Assistant Property Manager because they don't want the job done the way most companies define that title. You're running the leasing operation, coaching a team, managing resident relations, and contributing to the community's occupancy and financial performance. That's a wide scope, and it compounds fast as a career asset.

On any given weekend (and weekends are part of the regular schedule here), you might be walking a prospective resident through a unit, following up on a delinquency, reviewing concession strategy with the manager, coaching a newer leasing agent through a close, and planning a resident event. The work doesn't silo neatly. That's actually the point.
