The role also involves contributing to preventative maintenance and supporting cost-control efforts by repairing rather than replacing parts wherever possible.

Avanath emphasizes promotion from within, so this apprentice position has a clear path forward. Technicians who show initiative here typically move into full Maintenance Technician roles, then toward Lead Tech or Maintenance Supervisor over time. Hands-on experience across grounds, make-readies, and work order management builds exactly the skill set hiring managers look for at the next level.

What You Bring

  • At least 2 years of grounds or porter experience
  • Comfort operating property maintenance equipment including pressure washers and leaf blowers
  • Ability to perform minor repairs across plumbing, electrical, or general carpentry
  • Basic knowledge of Fair Housing laws and OSHA safety requirements
  • Strong attention to detail and solid time management habits
  • A professional, courteous manner with residents, staff, and vendors
  • High school diploma or equivalent

Physical demands are real here. Expect frequent standing, walking, bending, and occasional work on uneven ground or elevated surfaces. You may also travel to sister communities to provide maintenance support when needed, and as essential staff, you're expected to show up during inclement weather.

If you've been doing grounds and porter work and want a role where you can start picking up broader maintenance skills while earning a path toward a Technician title, this is a reasonable next step.

job.title: Entry Level Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Maintenance is one of the most skill-dense entry points in property management, and this role at Bigos Management's Willow Pond community in Burnsville builds a broad technical foundation fast. You're working across grounds, common areas, and apartment units, which means your hands are on almost every system a residential property runs on. That kind of cross-training compounds quickly.

What This Role Actually Builds

The core of this position is supporting daily operations at a 312-unit garden-style community, with a partial split to a second site. You'll work directly alongside experienced maintenance staff on make-readies, which means learning how to turn units efficiently from move-out to rent-ready condition. That process, furniture removal, paint touch-up, cleaning, and punch list repairs, is one of the most teachable and transferable skills in residential maintenance. Technicians who get fast and thorough at turns become indispensable quickly.

Beyond make-readies, the daily scope includes:

  • Grounds upkeep: trash removal, sweeping walks, watering, and winter ice control
  • Work order completion in apartments and common areas covering minor plumbing, electrical, HVAC, light carpentry, and painting
  • Regular property walks to catch maintenance and cleanliness issues before residents report them
  • Tool and supply inventory alongside the onsite team

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 8:00 am to 4:30 pm, with Monday and Thursday at Willow Pond and the other three days split between Hidden Valley in the morning and Willow Pond in the afternoon. Reliable transportation is required for that split.

Skills That Transfer

Entry-level maintenance roles at multi-family properties tend to sort candidates into two groups pretty quickly: those who treat every work order as a task to close, and those who treat it as a chance to understand a system. The second group ends up as lead technicians, service managers, and eventually maintenance supervisors. At a company the size of Bigos, with a portfolio that has earned Star Tribune Top Workplace recognition eleven times, there's room to grow into those positions. Getting your Certified Pool Operators license within six months of hire, which this role recommends, is one concrete early step in that direction.

The minor plumbing and HVAC exposure you get at this level is the same exposure that, over time, leads to EPA 608 certification and the ability to take on more complex systems. The time management and self-direction skills you build handling multiple open work orders daily translate directly into managing a maintenance team later. None of that is theoretical here. It's just what happens when someone pays attention.

What Bigos Offers for This Position

Pay for this role runs $18.00 to $22.00 per hour depending on experience, with monthly renewal bonuses available. Benefits start the first of the month after hire and include medical with HSA employer contribution, 401(k) with employer match, ten paid holidays with no waiting period, PTO with rollover, company-paid life insurance and disability coverage, educational assistance, and a rent discount. A Lifetime Fitness membership discount is also included.

Zero to two years of residential maintenance or assistant-level experience meets the baseline here. If you bring solid mechanical instincts, a professional attitude with residents and vendors, and the physical readiness for a hands-on outdoor and indoor schedule through Minnesota winters, this is a strong place to start building a career in property maintenance.

job.title: Roving Leasing Consultant
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is a roving leasing role, which means you won't be anchored to a single property. Bozzuto is looking for a Leasing Consultant who can move fluidly across a portfolio spanning St. Petersburg, Tampa, and the broader Greater Tampa area. On any given day, you might be touring a prospect through one community in the morning and following up with leads for a different property in the afternoon. Flexibility and organization are prerequisites, not bonuses.

The core of the work is converting interest into signed leases. That means following up with every prospect, giving tours that feel personalized rather than scripted, and staying knowledgeable enough about each community in your rotation to speak to its specific neighborhood appeal. St. Pete and Tampa have distinct identities, and residents shopping in those markets know the difference. Strong candidates will quickly learn what makes each property's location compelling, whether that's proximity to the waterfront, walkability, or access to major employment corridors.

Beyond tours and follow-up, you'll also carry social media responsibilities. That includes creating and posting content for platforms like Facebook and Instagram to generate awareness and keep prospects engaged. The weekend schedule here is real and worth understanding upfront: three weekends per month on-site, with two weekdays off in exchange. That's industry-standard for leasing, but it's a lifestyle commitment you should plan around.

What You Bring

  • Proven comfort in a customer-facing sales environment, ideally leasing or retail
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to tailor your pitch to different types of prospects
  • Hands-on experience with social media content creation, specifically Instagram and Facebook
  • Competency with property management software, CRMs, or similar platforms
  • A polished, professional presentation and genuine comfort initiating conversations
  • Reliable transportation to travel between properties across the Tampa Bay area

Context Worth Knowing

Roving roles tend to accelerate leasing careers faster than single-site positions. You'll see how multiple properties perform, understand how management adjusts concessions and traffic strategies across a portfolio, and develop a broader view of operations than most entry-level leasing consultants ever get. That exposure can lead naturally into a senior leasing role, an assistant manager position, or a portfolio-level support role with a larger operator.

Bozzuto manages properties at the upper end of the quality spectrum, so the expectations for resident experience and brand consistency are high. Candidates who thrive here typically combine genuine warmth with a structured follow-up discipline. Charm without follow-through won't move the needle on occupancy. The posted salary range runs $47,000 to $49,000, with additional bonus eligibility, plus a benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, 20 days of PTO, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

job.title: Leasing Consultant- Russellville Commons
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

Leasing at Russellville Commons means you're the first real impression a prospective resident gets of the property. You'll greet prospects, qualify applicants, walk units, and guide new residents from application through lease signing. Behind the scenes, that translates to keeping rental files current, entering data accurately, and making sure every move-in is coordinated with the maintenance team so the apartment is genuinely ready when a new resident arrives. You'll also stay in regular contact with current residents, handling complaints and following up on rent payments when needed. The administrative side of the role matters here: monthly paperwork, organized files, and clean data entry aren't afterthoughts.

MG Properties has operated across the Western U.S. for over three decades, with a focus on acquisition, development, rehab, and management. That scale means there's real infrastructure behind you, and the company has a stated track record of promoting from within.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of property management or leasing experience (preferred)
  • Genuine sales instincts paired with strong customer service follow-through
  • Comfort with leasing software and data entry, since occupancy reporting depends on accurate input
  • Professional communication skills in both in-person and written contexts
  • The organizational discipline to keep files, lease documents, and administrative tasks in order across a busy leasing cycle

Where This Role Can Take You

A leasing consultant position done well builds a specific and transferable skill set: you learn to read traffic patterns, understand what drives concessions decisions, and develop a feel for occupancy trends before they show up in a report. Those instincts are exactly what assistant managers and property managers rely on daily. Strong leasing consultants who also demonstrate comfort with the administrative side of the role, resident relations, and lease compliance tend to move into assistant manager roles faster than those who treat leasing as purely a sales function.

Portland's multifamily market has seen meaningful rent pressure over the past few years, which means leasing teams are expected to do more than just show units. Understanding traffic sources, following up consistently, and converting leads efficiently all matter more in a tighter market. If you're early in your property management career, this environment sharpens those skills in ways that translate directly to any future leasing or management role.

Benefits include monthly and quarterly bonuses, profit sharing, a 401(k) with employer match, medical, dental, and vision coverage, paid holidays, PTO, and rental discounts.

job.title: Maintenance Technician at Sugarmont Apartments & Townhomes
job.description:
Maintenance Technicians at apartment communities carry a lot of the resident experience on their shoulders. A leaking faucet or a broken AC in a Utah summer isn't just a work order. It's a person's home, and how quickly and cleanly you resolve it shapes how that resident feels about living there. At Sugarmont Apartments and Townhomes, Cottonwood Residential is looking for someone who understands that dynamic.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Day to day, you'll move through a mix of scheduled make-readies and incoming resident requests. Plumbing, electrical, general carpentry, HVAC troubleshooting. The scope is broad, which keeps the work from getting monotonous, but it also means you need a genuine foundation across trades rather than deep expertise in just one. EPA Type II or Universal certification is required before you start, and you'll need a valid driver's license. CPO certification is a plus if you have it.

The physical side of this role is real. You're on your feet for most of the day, climbing stairs and ladders, working in tight spaces, and occasionally lifting up to 50 lbs. Evenings, weekends, and on-call rotations for after-hours emergencies are part of the schedule. The Service Manager provides support during those calls, so you're not handling urgent situations entirely alone, but you need to be comfortable responding when residents need help outside normal hours.

Who Tends to Fit Well Here

Strong candidates in this kind of role share a few qualities that go beyond technical skill. They communicate clearly with residents while the work is happening. They leave the unit clean. They close the loop. A technician who fixes the problem but leaves a resident feeling brushed off hasn't fully done the job. Cottonwood emphasizes service quality and resident connection as core values, so the interpersonal side of maintenance work genuinely matters here.

  • EPA Type II or Universal certification (required)
  • Meaningful HVAC troubleshooting experience
  • Plumbing, electrical, and carpentry skills across residential repairs
  • Valid driver's license
  • Ability to work on-call and cover after-hours emergency calls
  • CPO certification (a plus, not a requirement)

Benefits and Growth

Cottonwood offers health, vision, dental, life, and disability coverage available within your first 30 days, along with a 401k with company match, HSA match, 10.5 paid holidays, and three weeks of paid time off in your first year. For a maintenance role, that's a solid package that reflects how the company values this work.

For technicians who build strong skills here, the natural path often leads toward a Lead Tech or Service Manager role. Communities like Sugarmont give you exposure to a varied unit mix including townhomes, which adds scope to your experience compared to a flat garden-style property. If you're early in your maintenance career and want to grow, that variety is genuinely useful.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance
job.description:
You're mid-turn on a two-bedroom at Craigdell Gardens, patching drywall and lining up the paint match, when a call comes in about a leaking shut-off valve in another unit. That's a normal Tuesday in this role.

Birgo is hiring a Maintenance Technician for its apartment community on Craigdell Road in New Kensington, PA. The position covers the full scope of residential maintenance work: make-readies and turns, drywall, painting, electrical, plumbing, carpentry, and HVAC repairs, along with scheduled preventative maintenance. You'll also rotate through on-call coverage for after-hours emergencies, with mileage reimbursed for travel throughout the workday. Beyond Craigdell Gardens, there's occasional opportunity to support other Birgo properties across the Western PA region.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

New Kensington sits in a market where Birgo operates workforce housing, and the residents here depend on things getting fixed right and fast. The pace of turns matters because vacant units directly affect occupancy, and occupancy affects everything else. Strong technicians in this kind of environment know how to move through a punch list without cutting corners. You're not just fixing things; you're directly affecting whether someone has a safe, functioning home.

On-call rotation is a real part of this job and worth acknowledging honestly. Emergency calls come after hours. If that kind of availability doesn't fit your current situation, this role will be difficult. If it does, the compensation and weekly pay structure reflect that trade-off.

What Birgo Needs From You

  • Eligibility to work in the United States
  • Valid driver's license and personal, insured transportation
  • Availability for on-call rotation
  • Ability to lift and carry 50 pounds without assistance
  • Comfort working in confined spaces, on ladders, and on staircases
  • Safe, competent use of power tools
  • Hands-on experience across at least several of the core trades: plumbing, electrical, drywall, painting, HVAC, or carpentry

Pay runs $24 to $27 per hour depending on experience, paid weekly. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, and life insurance with employer contribution, a 401(k) match, paid time off and sick time, a boots and uniform program, professional development reimbursement, discounted rent at Birgo properties, and a profit-sharing program. Mileage is reimbursed for work-related travel.

Technicians who grow in this kind of role often develop the breadth to move into lead maintenance or property-level facilities management. Working across multiple sites in a regional portfolio also builds exposure to different property types and condition levels, which sharpens diagnostic instincts faster than single-site work typically does.

job.title: Resident Services
job.description:
Some property roles ask you to specialize. This one asks you to cover ground. The Resident Services Coordinator position at Berkshire 15 and Central Place draws on a specific combination of skills: front-facing resident communication, leasing support, service coordination, and the kind of situational awareness that keeps a property humming when multiple departments need help at once.

The Skills This Role Runs On

Relationship-building sits at the center of everything here. Residents call because they need something, and you're the person who either has the answer or knows exactly who does. That requires genuine comfort with high-volume phone communication, the ability to shift tone quickly between a prospective renter tour and a maintenance follow-up call, and enough familiarity with leasing to step in when the leasing team needs an extra hand showing units or working renewal conversations.

Attention to detail matters more than it might appear on paper. Processing service requests sounds administrative, but the follow-through piece, confirming completion and checking in with residents, is where satisfaction scores are actually won or lost. Coordinators who track those loops closely tend to build the kind of resident trust that shows up in renewal rates.

What the Day Actually Looks Like

This is a multi-site position covering Berkshire 15 and Central Place, so reliable transportation between locations is a practical requirement, not a footnote. On any given shift, you might greet a prospective resident in the morning, field maintenance requests through the afternoon, and wrap up by supporting the team on a lease renewal outreach effort. The variety is real.

  • Supporting leasing traffic and stepping in to show units as needed
  • Handling inbound calls as the primary voice of the property
  • Coordinating service requests from submission through resident follow-up
  • Assisting with lease renewal outreach and resident retention efforts
  • Contributing ideas for resident events and satisfaction initiatives

Berkshire manages its own properties in-house, which means the teams you're working alongside, leasing, maintenance, management, are all under the same umbrella. That structure tends to make cross-departmental coordination faster and less fragmented than in third-party management environments, and it gives coordinators real visibility into how a property operates end to end.

What Makes a Strong Fit

Candidates who do well in this role usually have a natural comfort with ambiguity. The day shifts depending on what the property needs, and the ability to reprioritize quickly without losing track of open items is what separates coordinators who thrive from those who feel scattered. Prior experience in leasing or resident relations at a Class A or B community helps, but the interpersonal instincts matter as much as the resume line.

The posted hourly range runs from $24.57 to $25.96, with full benefits including health coverage, retirement, paid time off, and a 25% rent discount. Berkshire positions this role as part of a people-first culture with personal development plans built in, which is worth taking seriously if career growth in property management is on your radar. Coordinators who learn both the leasing and operations sides of a site often move into assistant manager or leasing manager roles with a stronger foundation than those who've only done one or the other.

job.title: Leasing Specialist - Part-Time
job.description:
A prospect walks in mid-afternoon, not sure if they want a one-bedroom or a two. You've got a tour starting in ten minutes, a package pile at the desk, and three resident questions in the queue. That's a normal Tuesday in leasing, and it's exactly the kind of shift this role is built around.

What the Role Covers

Redstone Residential operates more than 38,000 beds across 20 states, making it one of the larger third-party management platforms in the country. This part-time Leasing Specialist position supports a community in Provo, Utah, where Redstone is headquartered. The work sits at the intersection of leasing support and front-desk operations: conducting tours, processing applications, fielding resident questions, managing package intake, and keeping the lobby environment secure and welcoming. You're also a direct extension of the leasing team's KPI push, which means your interactions directly touch traffic-to-lease conversion, even in a support capacity.

Pay starts at $18.00 per hour with the opportunity to earn performance bonuses. A 401(k) plan with up to 6% employer matching is available.

Who Fits This Role

  • One to two years of customer service or sales experience, ideally in a front-facing environment
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills
  • Comfort with property management software; experience with Entrata is a plus
  • Ability to stay composed when multiple priorities collide
  • Basic computer proficiency for correspondence and administrative tasks
  • High school diploma or equivalent

Reliability matters more here than most leasing roles acknowledge. Part-time schedules are often the first thing that slips when life gets busy, but this position requires consistent presence. The leasing team depends on this role to keep front-desk operations steady so managers can focus on closing and compliance.

If you have any interest in growing within property management, part-time leasing is one of the cleaner entry points into the field. You build familiarity with traffic management, application workflows, and resident relations without carrying full P&L accountability. Many full-time leasing consultants and eventual assistant managers started exactly here, learning how occupancy goals translate into daily floor activity before stepping into larger roles.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
CloudTen Residential runs a genuinely varied book of multifamily assets. Hotel-to-residential conversions, high-rise lease-ups, value-add repositioning projects. For a maintenance tech, that kind of portfolio means you're not doing the same thing every shift, and that's either appealing or it isn't.

This position is based in Berkeley Heights, Kent, WA and pays $30 to $33 per hour depending on experience. There are also leasing and renewal bonuses available at the property level, which is a detail worth noting because it's not standard for every maintenance role.

The day-to-day work covers the full range: plumbing, basic electrical, HVAC, appliance repair, carpentry, pool upkeep, and keeping common areas clean and presentable. Turn work is part of the rhythm too. The expectation is that vacant units are rent-ready within three to five days, which requires you to prioritize quickly and work without a lot of hand-holding. Service requests get a 24-hour resolution window, and when parts are on order or something creates a delay, you're expected to communicate that clearly to both the community manager and the resident.

On-call emergency response is real here. This is worth stating plainly: you'll carry availability for after-hours calls, evenings, and weekends. If your personal schedule doesn't flex easily, that's worth thinking through before applying. The properties need coverage, and the expectation is responsiveness when something goes wrong at 10pm.

Preventive maintenance is a consistent part of the role too, not an afterthought. Monthly PM directives cover lighting, fire safety, pool and spa systems, and life-safety checks. You'll also track inventory, maintain MSDS records for chemicals on site, and document vacant unit status. The documentation side of this job is real, and candidates who treat paperwork as secondary tend to create problems down the line.

What this role generally requires

  • 1 to 2 years of hands-on maintenance experience across plumbing, electrical, HVAC, carpentry, and painting
  • Valid driver's license in good standing
  • Comfort with a mobile device and basic computer tasks (work orders, communication, documentation)
  • Ability to work independently and manage your own time without constant supervision
  • Strong communication skills, including with residents who are frustrated or in a difficult situation
  • Flexible availability including weekends, evenings, and holidays

The candidates who tend to do well in roles like this are the ones who already know what they don't know and ask good questions rather than guessing on unfamiliar systems. CloudTen's portfolio spans property types that range in complexity, so intellectual curiosity and a willingness to learn specific systems actually matters here. The tech who shows up with confidence, documents their work cleanly, and communicates proactively when something's off is the one who earns trust quickly.

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, company-paid life insurance, FSA access, paid vacation and sick leave, and paid holidays. CloudTen is an equal opportunity employer and maintains a drug-free workplace policy.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Villa Del Mar
job.description:
Multifamily maintenance is fundamentally a craft role with a service layer on top. The technician who understands both sides of that equation, fixing the problem correctly the first time while keeping the resident informed throughout, is the one who genuinely moves a property forward. At Sunrise Management's Villa Del Mar community in Oceanside, CA, that's exactly the balance this position asks you to strike.

Sunrise operates with a resident hospitality focus, and the maintenance function is central to delivering on that promise. Your work directly protects NOI by keeping turns tight, reducing delinquency pressure from dissatisfied residents, and preserving curb appeal at a coastal California asset where first impressions carry real weight.

What the Role Actually Covers

This is a full-scope technician position, not a specialty trade role. Day to day, you'll handle service requests across plumbing, basic electrical, HVAC, appliance repair, carpentry, and painting. You'll also carry responsibility for pool and spa maintenance, common area upkeep including laundry rooms and recreation areas, and grounds cleanliness. Make-readies are a core deliverable: Sunrise expects units to be rent-ready within three to five days of vacancy, so you need to manage a punch list efficiently without cutting corners on quality.

Beyond reactive work, the role includes structured preventive maintenance rounds covering fire safety systems, lighting, pool and spa equipment, and life-safety checks. You'll track tool and supply inventory, maintain MSDS documentation for on-site chemicals, and participate in move-in and move-out inspections. On-call emergency response is part of the schedule, so flexibility on evenings, weekends, and holidays is a real requirement.

Pay runs $25.00 to $27.00 per hour depending on experience, and the position is eligible for leasing bonuses at this property.

What You Bring and What You'll Build

The role requires one to two years of hands-on maintenance experience across the core trades listed above, plus at least two years of familiarity with property management software such as Yardi, Entrata, or Onesite. You need to be comfortable working from a mobile device, because work orders, unit status updates, and communication with management all flow through digital systems at most modern multifamily operations.

Strong candidates in a role like this tend to separate on two things: turn speed and resident communication. Technical competency is the baseline. What distinguishes a technician who advances to a lead or supervisor position is the habit of closing the loop, updating residents proactively when a part is on order, flagging a recurring issue to management before it becomes a capital problem, and documenting vacant unit status consistently. Those habits, practiced here, translate directly to supervisory readiness.

  • Trade experience: plumbing, electrical, HVAC, carpentry, painting (1 to 2 years required)
  • Property management software familiarity: Yardi, Entrata, Onesite, or equivalent (2 years minimum)
  • Mobile device proficiency for work order management
  • Ability to respond to after-hours and weekend emergency calls
  • PPE compliance and adherence to safety and hazardous materials policies
  • Customer service skill in handling difficult situations professionally

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, company-paid life insurance, an FSA option, and paid vacation, sick leave, and holidays. Sunrise Management is an equal opportunity employer and maintains a drug-free workplace.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager - Inkwell at Baseline ~ Broomfield, CO
job.description:
Assistant property manager roles at luxury communities ask a lot. You're handling leasing one hour and chasing delinquency the next. At Inkwell at Baseline, a Davis Development community in Broomfield, CO, the expectation is that you can shift between those two modes without losing composure in either one.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

The leasing side is active: greeting and touring prospective residents, walking them through qualifications, preparing files, and helping close renewals. You'll also support marketing efforts and resident events aimed at pushing occupancy to target. The operations side is where the real depth lives. You'll manage applications, track rents, and handle delinquency including the legal non-payment process when it comes to that. Yardi accuracy is your responsibility, so if you're sloppy with records, this role will make that apparent quickly. You'll do property walk-throughs, follow up on work orders, and keep the community looking and functioning at a level consistent with a luxury standard.

Resident issues will land on your desk too. Some of those conversations are straightforward. Some aren't. Davis specifically calls out maintaining a calm demeanor, and that's not filler language. It reflects the reality that you'll handle conflict regularly, and how you handle it reflects directly on the community's reputation.

What Davis Development Looks For

  • At least one year of assistant property manager experience
  • Lease-up experience at luxury communities is a plus
  • Proven sales, marketing, and customer service background
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Comfortable working across teams and with people at different levels of the organization
  • A bachelor's degree in a related field is preferred but not required
  • Proficiency with or willingness to learn Yardi

Candidates who stand out in roles like this are the ones who don't need reminding to follow through. Leasing skills get you in the door, but it's the operational discipline, keeping files clean, staying on top of delinquency before it compounds, catching problems on walk-throughs before residents do, that separates a strong assistant manager from one who's just passing through.

The Company Behind the Property

Davis Development is a privately owned luxury developer and management company with more than 25 years building and operating multifamily communities across the country. Their model is in-house management, meaning the people running these communities work directly for Davis, not a third-party firm. They describe their on-site teams as owner-operators, and that framing is meaningful. You're expected to make decisions that matter, not wait for someone else to call the shot.

Benefits include health coverage (medical, dental, vision, and behavioral health) starting the first of the month after 30 days, a 401(k) with a 4% employer match that vests immediately, company-paid life insurance, paid time off with a carryover provision, and access to a company apparel store allowance. Training and development are part of the package as well, which matters if you're thinking about a path toward property manager or beyond.

Davis Development is an equal opportunity employer. No third-party recruiter inquiries, please.

job.title: Community Manager - Portland
job.description:
The Skills This Role Runs On

Community management at an affordable housing portfolio pulls on a specific combination of skills: financial oversight, compliance knowledge, and genuine people work. At Avanath, all three carry equal weight. You'll read budget comparisons and rent rolls with the same attention you give a resident concern at the front desk. LIHTC and Tax Credit compliance isn't background knowledge here. It shapes daily decisions around eligibility, file management, and subsidy voucher submissions.

Strong interpersonal skills matter in every property management role, but affordable housing puts that skill set under real pressure. Residents often face housing instability, and you function as a resource hub connecting them to services and agencies beyond what the property itself can provide. That requires listening without judgment, communicating clearly under stress, and knowing when to escalate and when to handle something directly.

Day-to-Day Responsibilities

Operationally, you own the full scope of on-site management. That includes:

  • Monitoring delinquency and driving toward 0% through consistent rent collection systems
  • Managing accounts payable, vendor relationships, and contractor performance
  • Preparing monthly financials and reports accurately and on time
  • Partnering with your Regional Manager on the annual operating budget
  • Overseeing capex projects and coordinating across departments when needed
  • Maintaining occupancy goals through leasing of new and turned units
  • Ensuring curb appeal and physical presentation stay at a high standard

On the people side, you lead and develop a full on-site team. You set schedules, give direct feedback, run performance reviews, and handle the day-to-day challenges that come with managing staff in a high-contact environment. Resident events and retention programs also fall to you, and you'll be expected to build relationships with regulatory agencies and social service partners in the community.

What Sets Strong Candidates Apart

Avanath specifically needs someone with 5 to 7 years in property management, including at least 2 years in a manager seat, and verified LIHTC experience. That last point is non-negotiable. Tax credit compliance has meaningful legal and financial consequences, and the learning curve matters.

What actually separates strong candidates in this type of role is the ability to hold both sides of the job at once. The managers who struggle tend to be strong on either the financial side or the resident relations side, but not both. Affordable housing community managers need to run tight books and still show up for residents as a genuine advocate. Avanath's model is built around that balance, and their reputation in workforce housing reflects it.

If you've worked in LIHTC communities, built real relationships with housing agencies or social services, and led teams through high-occupancy, compliance-heavy environments, this role fits the skills you've already developed.

job.title: Concierge (16 Hour Part-Time)- 181 Fremont
job.description:
High-rise HOA concierge work is a specific kind of service job that most people outside of property management don't fully understand. It's not a hotel front desk. It's not a leasing office. It's a fixed-schedule, relationship-driven role inside a residential community where the same residents walk past you every day and hold you to a high standard because they live there.

Action Property Management, the largest privately owned HOA management company in the West, operates over 300 communities out of nine offices. Their portfolio runs toward luxury and they've built a reputation over four decades on professionalism and follow-through. 181 Fremont is one of their flagship San Francisco properties, and they're bringing on a part-time concierge for 16 hours per week.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

At a luxury high-rise like 181 Fremont, the concierge is often the first person a resident or guest encounters. You're managing package intake, handling access control, fielding questions from residents, and keeping a close eye on who comes and goes. The building has standards, and your job is to uphold them consistently, not just when it's easy.

Part-time in HOA concierge often means fixed shifts, so your schedule is predictable. But the nature of the work means you need to stay sharp for the full duration of your shift. A quiet lobby can shift quickly, and residents at a property like this expect a professional, calm response regardless of what's happening behind the scenes.

Who Fits This Role

  • Someone who's comfortable working independently without constant supervision
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, especially under pressure
  • Experience in hospitality, residential property management, or a related service role
  • A professional demeanor that holds up when residents are frustrated or demanding
  • Attention to detail for access logs, package tracking, and incident reporting

The honest part: residents at luxury HOA communities can be exacting. You'll occasionally deal with complaints that feel disproportionate, requests that fall outside your actual scope, and moments where you have to hold a firm but polite line. That's part of the job. If that dynamic sounds manageable rather than exhausting, you're probably the right fit.

For candidates thinking about where this kind of role leads, HOA concierge experience at a high-profile property is a genuine resume asset. It demonstrates you can operate inside a structured, professional environment with high resident expectations. People who do this work well often move into assistant community manager or community manager positions within HOA management companies.

job.title: PT Concierge (Weekends) - Downtown Dallas
job.description:
Concierge roles at luxury high-rise and mid-rise communities tend to look simple from the outside. In practice, they're the front line of resident experience, and at a downtown Dallas high-rise, that means holding a lot of the building's reputation in your hands on a Saturday morning when management isn't around.

The Role at Victory Park

Worth Ross Management Company runs HOA and residential operations across Texas, and this part-time weekend position covers Saturday and Sunday mornings, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., at their Victory Park property in downtown Dallas. The pay is $17 to $17.50 per hour.

You're the first person residents and guests see when they walk in. That means controlling access, logging vendors, handling packages through BuildingLink, and knowing residents by name. The expectation isn't just to check IDs at the door. It's to anticipate needs, field complaints before they become escalations, and keep everything documented and organized so the Lead Concierge and AGM have clean handoff notes when the week starts.

Package management is a bigger part of this than people expect. Coordinating deliveries, logging them accurately, and getting them to residents in a timely way takes real attention to detail, especially on weekends when volume can spike. Emergency response is also part of the job. You need to recognize alarms, react without hesitation, and follow building protocols correctly.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • Prior concierge or front desk experience in a hotel or residential setting
  • Comfortable working independently on weekends without a manager on-site
  • Proficient in MS Office and adaptable to building management software (BuildingLink experience is a plus)
  • Ability to lift 30 to 50 pounds and move through the building quickly when needed
  • Multilingual ability is a genuine advantage in a downtown Dallas high-rise environment
  • Steady under pressure, especially when residents are frustrated or an emergency is developing

Worth Knowing Before You Apply

Weekend morning shifts at high-density residential buildings have a particular rhythm. Resident traffic picks up early, vendor scheduling requests come in fast, and you're expected to handle it all without someone looking over your shoulder. The candidates who do well here tend to have a hospitality background where they learned to stay calm, stay organized, and actually remember people's names. That last part sounds small. It isn't.

Worth Ross has a track record in the HOA management space and tends to promote from within when concierge staff demonstrate reliability and service quality. For someone building a career in residential property management, a concierge role at a well-run downtown property is one of the cleaner paths toward a front office or assistant manager position.

job.title: Property Manager
job.description:
Founders Hall is a student housing community in Tempe, Arizona, which puts it squarely in the orbit of Arizona State University, one of the largest universities in the country by enrollment. Managing student housing at that scale means your leasing calendar is dictated by academic timelines, your turns are compressed and intense, and your resident base turns over in ways that traditional multifamily doesn't. The Property Manager role here carries the full operational weight of that reality.

Yugo operates nearly 40,000 beds across 88 U.S. properties, so this position connects to a genuinely global organization. The reporting line is to a Regional Property Manager, and you'll be expected to communicate property performance clearly: occupancy trends, delinquency, budget variance, operating expenses. That means knowing your numbers well enough to explain them, not just read them off a report.

Day-to-day, the role covers the full spectrum of property operations. You'll lead the on-site team, oversee rent collection and delinquency management, coordinate leasing and marketing activity, manage vendor relationships, and handle the turn process when the academic year wraps. Student housing turns tend to be high-volume and time-compressed. Getting hundreds of units ready in a narrow window before move-in requires tight coordination between leasing, maintenance, and outside contractors. That's a meaningful part of this job, and candidates who've run turns at student or university properties will feel the difference immediately.

Financial oversight includes reviewing T-12 performance, contributing to annual operating and capex budgets, and identifying opportunities to improve NOI. You'll also monitor local market conditions, track competitor pricing, and help keep Founders Hall positioned competitively in the ASU-area market.

What you'll bring

  • At least three years of supervisory experience in residential property management or a related operational role
  • Hands-on experience running a property, with student or university housing experience a strong differentiator
  • Proficiency in Entrata, Yardi, RealPage, or a comparable property management platform
  • Working knowledge of Fair Housing regulations and applicable federal, state, and local compliance requirements
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to manage both team performance and resident relations effectively
  • A bachelor's degree in business or a related field, or equivalent residential management experience

Compensation is $70,000 to $75,000 annually, plus a fully compensated two-bedroom apartment on-site. The total package also includes health, dental, and vision benefits, 401(k) with 4% employer match, three weeks of PTO, paid parental leave, and eleven paid holidays.

The candidate who does well in this role typically has enough operational range to move fluidly between a budget conversation in the morning and a resident complaint in the afternoon without losing focus on either. Student housing rewards managers who can build real culture within a community, keep their team motivated through a demanding leasing cycle, and hold occupancy without letting delinquency creep up. Those three things together are harder than they look, and the operators who get all three right tend to advance quickly in this segment of the industry.

job.title: Daytime Concierge
job.description:
High-rise and mid-rise communities in markets like Silver Spring run on relationships just as much as they run on operations. The leasing team closes deals, the maintenance team keeps things working, but the concierge desk is where residents actually feel whether they made the right decision moving in. Bozzuto understands this, which is why the Daytime Concierge role carries real weight in how the community performs and how residents talk about it to others.

What This Role Actually Looks Like Day to Day

This is a Monday through Friday position, 10AM to 7PM, which means you're covering the heart of resident activity: move-ins, deliveries, afternoon arrivals, evening returnees. You're the face people see when they walk through the door, and Bozzuto takes that seriously enough to make it a dedicated role rather than a front-desk add-on.

A typical day might start with organizing the package room and checking overnight logs, shift into fielding questions from a prospective resident who wants to know about the neighborhood, then pivot to coordinating details for a resident event you're planning for later in the week. You'll know residents by name, their pets by name, and probably their routines. That kind of familiarity doesn't happen by accident; it happens because you genuinely enjoy people and you pay attention.

Social media is also part of the role. You'll contribute to community awareness by posting content that's authentic to the community's character, and you'll encourage satisfied residents to share their experiences through reviews. In a competitive rental market like Silver Spring, those reviews move the needle on traffic and occupancy.

What Bozzuto Is Looking For

  • At least two years in a hospitality, hotel, retail, or travel-facing role
  • Strong written and verbal communication, the kind that works equally well in a quick hallway conversation and a formal email
  • Comfort with software, apps, and digital tools used to manage front desk operations
  • Attention to detail in package management, reservation logs, and freight elevator scheduling
  • A professional appearance and a natural instinct for anticipating what someone needs before they ask
  • Ability to lift up to 25 pounds (the holiday package volume is real)

The hourly rate is $23.08, with bonus opportunities on top of that. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

One thing worth knowing if you're considering this role: concierge work in a luxury residential community tends to create a strong foundation for broader property management careers. People who do this job well develop resident relations skills, operational awareness, and vendor coordination experience that translate directly into leasing, assistant manager, and community manager paths. It's a genuine entry point into the industry for people with hospitality backgrounds who want to build something longer-term.

job.title: Leasing Manager - Olympus Corsair
job.description:
It's a Tuesday morning and three prospects are scheduled back-to-back, your leasing team needs a coaching moment before the first tour, and you're also fielding a renewal question from a long-term resident who got a competing offer down the street. That's a pretty normal hour at the Corsair.

The Role

Olympus Property is hiring a Leasing Manager for Olympus Corsair in San Diego. This position sits between the leasing team and property leadership. You're responsible for driving occupancy, but you're also the person who shapes how your team presents, follows up, and closes. Expect to spend time on the floor alongside consultants, not just reviewing their numbers from behind a desk.

Day-to-day responsibilities include leading and developing the leasing staff, holding them accountable to follow-up standards (calls, emails, handwritten notes to prospects), and tracking traffic reports, lease counts, move-ins, and move-outs on a weekly and monthly basis. You'll conduct market surveys, show and lease apartment homes yourself, and prepare lease paperwork through move-in. Resident retention is part of the job too: planning and attending resident events, handling concerns before they escalate, and visiting locators and local businesses to keep traffic coming in. You'll also work out of RealPage/Knock/OneSite, so familiarity with that stack matters.

The schedule is Monday through Friday, 9 to 5, with flexibility for resident events and rotating weekends. San Diego's rental market is competitive enough that strong follow-up cadence and locator relationships genuinely move the needle here. If you've worked lease-up or high-traffic Class A communities, you already know how much consistency in prospect follow-up affects closing ratios.

What Olympus Is Looking For

  • At least 3 years of experience as an apartment leasing consultant
  • Demonstrated ability to lead, train, and motivate a leasing team
  • Hands-on experience with RealPage, Knock, or OneSite strongly preferred
  • Comfort closing leases directly while also coaching others to do the same
  • Availability for after-hours resident events and periodic weekend coverage

Olympus has been recognized as a National Apartment Association Top Employer from 2023 through 2025. Compensation runs $25 to $27 per hour depending on experience, plus monthly leasing commissions and resident renewal bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, pet insurance, an apartment rental allowance, and a sabbatical program.

What tends to separate strong candidates in this specific role: the ability to build and actually run a follow-up system, not just describe one in an interview. Prospects in a market like San Diego are shopping multiple properties simultaneously. Teams that follow up consistently and personally win more of those decisions. If you've built that habit into a team before, that experience will show up quickly here.

job.title: Leasing Manager
job.description:
Student housing leasing runs on a different clock than conventional multifamily. Pre-lease cycles start months before a bed turns, traffic spikes hit hard in late fall and early spring, and closing a college student often means closing their parents too. PeakMade Real Estate is hiring a Leasing Manager for their Reno community to own that cycle from the top of the funnel down to a signed lease.

What This Role Actually Covers

This is an onsite leadership position, which means you're building the team as much as you're working the traffic. You'll hire, onboard, and develop both full-time and part-time leasing staff, then set the standard for how the desk runs day to day. Customer service, tour quality, closing ratios, lease renewal execution: all of it runs through you.

On the digital side, PeakMade expects real fluency with social platforms. Instagram and Facebook content, graphics built in Canva, photo editing in Lightroom or VSCO, and active reputation management through platforms like Reputation.com and JTurner are part of the weekly rhythm here. A property's online presence directly influences traffic, and traffic drives occupancy. That connection is real and measurable.

You'll also collaborate with the property manager on the annual marketing plan, coordinate lease-up events and renewal programming, and maintain accurate prospect data so the team can track where leads are dropping off and adjust. Occupancy targets, closing ratios, and retention goals are the scorecard.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • At least 2 years of leasing experience in off-campus student housing specifically. Conventional multifamily experience doesn't transfer cleanly to this model.
  • Prior leadership or supervisory experience, even informal mentoring or shift lead responsibility counts here.
  • Comfort working some evenings and weekends, particularly during peak traffic periods.
  • Hands-on proficiency with social media content creation and property management software.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills that connect with 19-to-22-year-olds and their parents in the same conversation.

One honest note on what separates good from great in student housing leasing: the ability to manufacture urgency without pressure tactics. College renters are price-sensitive, heavily influenced by peers, and often deciding in groups. Managers who understand that dynamic and build genuine rapport consistently outperform those who rely on scripted closes. If you've tracked your own traffic-to-lease conversion and improved it, that story will matter in an interview for this role.

Compensation is set at $52,000 annually, with monthly, quarterly, and annual commission and bonus opportunities available on top of base. PeakMade also offers a housing discount, 401(k) match, up to 12 weeks of paid parental leave, 15 days of PTO plus two additional wellbeing days, and access to a mentorship program for those looking to grow within the organization.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager Affordable Apartment Community
job.description:
It's Tuesday morning and a resident stops by the office with a late rent concern while the phone rings about a maintenance request and a prospective tenant waits near the leasing counter. That kind of overlap is the normal operating rhythm at a 120-unit affordable community, and it's exactly the environment this role is built for.

Investment Property Group, headquartered in Park City, Utah, owns and operates more than 150 properties across 13 states, spanning multifamily, manufactured home, and RV communities. This Assistant Community Manager position supports Antelope Valley Apartments in Lancaster, California, a tax credit and project-based Section 8 community where compliance isn't optional and resident relationships carry real weight. The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 8am to 5pm, with hourly compensation ranging from $24.00 to $28.00 depending on experience and qualifications.

What This Role Actually Involves

You'll work directly alongside the Community Manager to keep daily operations moving. Rent collection, delinquency follow-up, and ledger accuracy are core functions, as is coordinating any necessary eviction proceedings. On the leasing side, you'll assist with new move-in applications, renewals, and waitlist management, all of which carry heightened compliance requirements in a tax credit environment where income certifications and regulatory documentation have to be handled precisely.

Daily property walks keep you connected to the physical condition of the community. Common area inspections, unit inspections, and documented punch lists are part of the routine. Resident concerns get addressed directly and professionally, and you'll also participate in regulatory meetings or agency inspections as needed.

What You'll Bring and What You'll Build

The role requires at least one year of assistant manager experience at a multifamily community of 100 units or more. Strong delinquency management skills, conflict resolution experience, and comfort handling administrative detail are all necessary from day one. Spanish fluency is preferred given the Lancaster market and the community's resident demographic, though it's listed as a bonus rather than a hard requirement.

  • Demonstrated experience with rent collection and delinquency workflows
  • Solid written and verbal communication skills across residents, vendors, and local agencies
  • Organizational ability to manage competing priorities without things slipping
  • Valid driver's license
  • A straightforward, professional approach to difficult conversations

What this role builds is equally worth naming. Affordable housing operations develop a compliance fluency that transfers directly to tax credit specialist roles, regional compliance positions, or community manager seats at affordable or mixed-income properties. Candidates who learn to manage a waitlist, coordinate with housing authorities, and maintain accurate resident files in a regulated environment develop skills that are genuinely scarce and increasingly valued as affordable housing inventory grows. If you're a strong assistant manager looking for a path toward a full community manager role, the affordable housing side of the industry offers clear progression for people who take the compliance piece seriously.

IPG offers medical, dental, and vision coverage, life insurance, a health savings account, an employee assistance program, a 401k with company match, and four weeks of accrued PTO.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
Where You'll Be Working

Midtown Place Apartments in Memphis sits in one of the city's most active residential corridors, a neighborhood with genuine walkability and consistent rental demand. For an assistant property manager, that kind of location means steady traffic, a mix of resident profiles, and the opportunity to develop your leasing and operations skills on a property that stays busy year-round. Makowsky Ringel Greenberg is a well-established regional operator, and this role reflects their preference for hiring people who already understand how residential communities function.

What the Role Covers

This is a full-cycle leasing and operations position. On the leasing side, you'll handle all stages of the apartment rental process, from initial contact through closing. You'll track daily traffic, which matters more than it sounds. Consistent traffic logging feeds into occupancy projections and tells the property manager how the property is performing against its leasing goals.

On the operations side, you'll collect and record rental payments, process service requests from residents, and conduct daily inspections of the model unit, common areas, and amenities. You'll also assist with vacant apartment inspections, which ties directly into the make-ready cycle. Knowing what a unit needs before a turn gets started saves time, cuts costs, and keeps move-in dates realistic.

When the property manager is unavailable, you step into that role. That's standard for this position level, but it means you need to be comfortable making decisions, not just executing tasks.

Saturday availability is required. That's part of the job and worth knowing before you apply.

Skills This Role Requires vs. Skills It Builds

You'll need one to two years of residential leasing or management experience coming in. Familiarity with property management software is also expected. OneSite and Yardi are the preferred platforms here, so experience with either one will reduce your ramp-up time. You'll also need reliable transportation, a valid driver's license, and proof of insurance, along with the physical ability to walk the property and climb stairs during inspections.

What this role develops is your operational range. Leasing professionals who take on assistant manager responsibilities build fluency in the administrative and financial side of property management: payment processing, delinquency tracking, maintenance coordination, and daily reporting. These are the skills that distinguish a strong leasing consultant from someone ready to manage a property independently. If you're looking to move toward a property manager role in the next few years, this kind of position is where that transition happens.

  • 1 to 2 years of residential leasing or property management experience
  • Proficiency with OneSite or Yardi preferred
  • Weekend availability, including Saturdays
  • Ability to walk the property and navigate stairs
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Valid driver's license, reliable transportation, and proof of insurance
  • Must clear credit, background, and drug screening

MRG offers a competitive salary with a performance bonus program, full medical, dental, and vision coverage, short and long-term disability, company-paid life insurance, an apartment discount, paid holidays and PTO, and a 401(k) with profit-sharing. That's a meaningful benefits package for a role at this level in the market.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This position covers two Louisville communities, Devonshire and Lyndon Crossings, with a combined unit count of more than 470. Your day runs across work orders, preventive maintenance, and apartment turns. That means HVAC troubleshooting, plumbing repairs, electrical fixtures, appliance issues, drywall, and light paint work. You'll also manage equipment and supply inventory, keep up with grounds care, and handle seasonal tasks including snow removal. Pool maintenance may be part of the mix depending on the community.

After-hours on-call is part of the job. Peak pays an on-call premium for it, but set your expectations accordingly: some nights and weekends, you'll get a call.

With 470-plus units split across two properties, the work volume is real. Strong candidates know how to triage. A clogged drain and a non-functioning furnace in January are both urgent, but they're not equal. The technicians who perform well here move efficiently, communicate clearly with residents, and don't let a full work order queue turn into a backlog.

What You Bring

  • Prior maintenance experience at an apartment community or comparable residential setting
  • Hands-on familiarity with HVAC systems, plumbing, electrical, and basic appliance repair
  • Ability to troubleshoot problems independently without waiting on a supervisor to direct each step
  • HVAC certification is preferred but not a hard requirement
  • Physical readiness: ladder work, confined spaces, lifting up to 50 pounds, outdoor work in all weather
  • Professionalism with residents. You're often the only person from the company they see face-to-face

Compensation and Context

Pay ranges from $17 to $27 per hour depending on experience. The package includes medical, dental, and life insurance, paid time off (plus your birthday), a 401(k) with employer match, an on-call premium, and a sign-on bonus.

Peak Management operates across multiple communities, so strong technicians here have a clear path toward senior tech or lead maintenance roles as they build tenure and skills. If you want to grow within a multi-property company rather than stay in a single-site dead end, the structure is there.

job.title: Community Manager | Rambler Atlanta - Atlanta, GA
job.description:
Rambler Atlanta is a student housing community, which means this role comes with rhythms that standard multifamily doesn't. Lease-up pressure concentrates around academic calendars. Turnover hits hard and fast in summer. Residents are often living on their own for the first time, which shapes how you handle everything from delinquency conversations to maintenance requests. If you've managed in that environment before, you already know what that means. If you haven't, it's worth being clear-eyed about it before you apply.

LV Collective is looking for a Community Manager to run day-to-day operations at Rambler Atlanta. The scope is full-cycle: budget ownership, team leadership, leasing oversight, resident relations, vendor management, and financial reporting. You'll carry the P&L, manage on-site staff across leasing and maintenance, and serve as the connection point between what's happening on the ground and what corporate leadership needs to know. Monthly variance analysis, delinquency tracking, occupancy reporting, and rent collections all fall on this role.

Resident engagement at a student property carries real weight. It's not a nice-to-have. Retention at this asset type depends on whether residents feel connected to the community, and that work falls to the manager as much as anyone. You'd be planning and executing programming, fielding concerns directly, and keeping the brand experience consistent across every touchpoint.

The evenings and weekends piece is real. This isn't a five-days-and-done position. Student housing communities have activity that doesn't stop at 5pm, and a manager here needs to be reachable and willing to show up when something needs them.

One thing that separates strong candidates in this role: comfort with financial statements that tell a complicated story. Student housing occupancy can look healthy on paper while delinquency or concessions erode NOI quietly. Managers who catch those variances early and adjust strategy before month-end are the ones who actually hit their targets.

LV Collective uses Entrata, and familiarity with it matters. If you've built reporting in Entrata or used it to track traffic and leasing velocity during a lease-up cycle, that's a real advantage here.

What the role requires

  • 4 or more years in property management, with student housing or multifamily experience
  • Demonstrated experience managing budgets, analyzing financials, and driving NOI
  • Experience leading on-site teams and holding people accountable to performance
  • Proficiency in Entrata (preferred), Microsoft Office, and Google Workspace
  • Strong communication skills across resident, staff, vendor, and corporate relationships
  • Experience with lease-up or new development openings is a plus

If you've built a team culture at a property that was underperforming and left it in better shape, or managed a summer turn without losing your mind, that experience is exactly what this role is built for.

job.title: Property Manager
job.description:
It's August, and move-in weekend is two days away. You're walking the property with a punch list in hand, confirming turns are complete, coordinating with your maintenance supervisor on a handful of last-minute work orders, and fielding a call from your leasing team about a question on a new resident's account. That's the rhythm at The Soto, Yugo's student housing community in Eugene.

The Role

Yugo operates nearly 40,000 beds across the U.S., and The Soto is one of 88 properties in that portfolio. As Property Manager, you report to the Regional Property Manager and carry full operational accountability for the community. That means staffing, financials, leasing performance, maintenance oversight, and resident experience all sit in your lane.

On the financial side, you'll manage accounts receivable and payable, own delinquency and eviction processes, and work through budget prep and variance analysis. You'll review occupancy trends and operating performance regularly, and you'll look for ways to strengthen NOI, whether by growing revenue or trimming unnecessary expense. Capital projects and vendor contracts are part of the job too, from bid coordination through completion.

Leasing and marketing aren't just a support function here. You'll oversee retention initiatives, track competitor pricing, and keep the community positioned competitively in the market. You'll ensure the leasing office and model units stay sharp and ready, because student housing traffic moves fast and first impressions close leases.

On the people side, you'll recruit, train, and develop your team, hold regular staff meetings, and manage performance when needed. You'll also handle resident complaints, disturbances, and policy violations, which in student housing means maintaining clear boundaries while keeping the community atmosphere positive.

What You Bring

  • At least three years of supervisory experience in residential property management or a closely related field
  • Direct experience managing a student or university residential community is a strong plus
  • Comfort with property management platforms such as Entrata, Yardi, or RealPage
  • Solid grounding in Fair Housing regulations and compliance requirements
  • A bachelor's degree in business or a related area, or equivalent hands-on experience
  • Carbon Literacy Certification, or willingness to complete the training

The salary range for this position is $70,000 to $75,000, with bonus eligibility and a benefits package that includes health, dental, and vision coverage, 401k with 4% employer match, three weeks of PTO, paid parental leave, and eligibility for comped on-site housing.

One thing worth knowing if you're considering this role: student housing runs on an academic calendar, and the weeks around lease-up and move-in are genuinely demanding. Strong candidates for this type of position have usually built their instincts for managing surge periods, keeping a team focused under pressure, and recovering quickly when things don't go according to plan. That adaptability carries directly into broader multifamily leadership roles over time.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Meadow Creek
job.description:
Meadow Creek sits in Boulder, a market where quality renters have real options and maintenance responsiveness is one of the sharpest differentiators between a community that retains residents and one that bleeds them. AIR Communities knows that. Their tech stack and shop organization reflect it. This role is a real maintenance technician position at a well-run Class A community, and the day-to-day reflects that expectation.

The work divides roughly into two streams: turns and service requests. Turns mean following a structured make-ready process so that every unit hitting the market is genuinely move-in ready, not just passable. Service requests mean troubleshooting whatever the day brings, plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliances, building systems. AIR uses technology to route and prioritize work orders, which keeps techs moving efficiently rather than burning time triaging at the shop. The shop itself is fully stocked, which sounds like a minor detail until you've spent 45 minutes hunting down a part that should've been on the shelf.

On-call is part of the job. At least one week per month, you'll need reliable transportation and the ability to respond to emergency calls outside business hours. That's the honest part of this role that doesn't get softened: Boulder residents in Class A units expect fast response, and on-call nights are real. Budget for that when you're thinking about fit.

Pay runs $25 to $28 per hour depending on your actual skill set and trade depth. There's also a quarterly customer service bonus of up to $1,500 for techs who consistently earn strong resident satisfaction scores. That number isn't trivial. The 50% rent discount at any AIR community is a genuine benefit if you're open to living onsite or nearby.

AIR's internal development program, Ascend, is designed around individual growth paths rather than a one-size training module. For a tech who wants to move into lead or maintenance supervisor territory over the next few years, that kind of structured development is worth paying attention to. Multifamily maintenance careers tend to advance through demonstrated trade depth and resident service scores, and this environment rewards both.

What you'll bring

  • At least 2 years of maintenance experience in multifamily, facilities, or building maintenance
  • Proficiency in at least two trades: plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliance repair, or carpentry
  • Availability for flexible scheduling including evenings, weekends, and on-call rotation
  • Reliable transportation for emergency response during on-call shifts
  • Physical ability to handle equipment and machinery as the work requires

Strong candidates in this type of role tend to be thorough on turns, not just fast. A punch list that's actually complete before a move-in beats a quick turn with callbacks every time, and the best techs know the difference.

job.title: Maintenance Manager
job.description:
Village Green has operated residential communities since 1919, which means this Maintenance Service Manager role carries real institutional weight. The team has systems, history, and standards. Your job is to keep a San Antonio apartment community running at a level that protects asset value and keeps residents renewing.

The Skills This Role Runs On

HVAC and mechanical systems knowledge sits at the center of this position. You'll field work orders spanning EPA Universal-level refrigerant work, boiler and chiller maintenance, plumbing systems, water heaters, electrical, and appliances. That breadth matters because you're not just turning wrenches. You're triaging, prioritizing, and deciding what gets done today versus what goes on the capex list. Identifying capital improvements and pulling bids is part of the job, as is preparing the maintenance portion of the annual budget. Monthly energy management reports land on your desk too, which means you're reading consumption trends and putting recommendations in writing.

Team leadership is the other core skill set. You'll supervise maintenance staff directly: distributing work orders, managing schedules, and keeping the make-ready pipeline moving so turns don't stall occupancy. You'll also be involved in interviewing candidates when the team needs to grow. Mentoring existing staff is just as important as recruiting them. A preventative maintenance program only works when the whole crew understands it and executes it consistently.

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

Two years of supervisory experience in apartment, hotel, or similar facilities maintenance is the baseline. What separates a strong hire from an average one is the combination of mechanical depth and genuine coaching instincts. Technicians who got promoted because they were the best at repairs sometimes struggle to delegate and develop others. This role needs someone who can diagnose a complex HVAC issue at 8 AM and run a productive team huddle at 8:15. Customer service matters too. Residents interact with maintenance staff more directly than any other department, and every completed work order is a retention moment.

Proficiency with maintenance software is required. Work order documentation, completion rates, and aging reports are all tracked, and you'll need to stay on top of that data to run an efficient operation.

Working at Village Green

Village Green holds multi-year recognition from Great Place to Work and Best Workplaces in Multifamily, both of which reflect how the company manages its people internally. The company's approach is to invest in associates with training and tools rather than just filling seats. For a Maintenance Manager, that tends to mean real support on capital projects and access to resources rather than being stretched thin and expected to improvise. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, a bonus program, and a 401(k) with a company match.

San Antonio's multifamily market has stayed active, with steady demand keeping occupancy pressure real across the metro. Keeping turns tight and preventative maintenance current directly affects NOI here. This is a role where your operational decisions show up in the numbers.

job.title: Property Manager (Class A Office)
job.description:
It's 8:45 a.m. and you're already cross-referencing a vendor invoice against the GL, fielding a tenant call about HVAC response times, and mentally flagging an expense variance you'll need to explain in this month's ownership report. That's a Tuesday. At Stream Realty Partners, the Property Manager role for their Class A office portfolio in Dallas runs at the intersection of financial discipline and tenant-facing service, and it rewards people who can move between both without losing precision.

What This Role Actually Covers

Stream operates as a full-service commercial firm, and this position sits on the fee management side, serving third-party owners. That distinction matters. You're accountable not just to building operations but to client relationships and the management agreement governing everything you do. Day-to-day, that means accounts payable and receivable, monthly rent edits, general ledger review, and financial reporting tailored to each client's requirements. You'll write expense variance comments that actually explain what happened, not just what the numbers show.

Beyond the financials, you're coordinating the full operating cycle of the property: vendor contracts, service agreements, capital projects, and tenant improvement applications through to accounting submission. You'll conduct routine inspections and follow up on punch list items before they become exposure. You'll set up leases in the accounting system, own the CAM reconciliation process, and manage the real estate tax review for your portfolio. After-hours emergency calls are part of the role, and supervisory responsibility for your team means performance conversations and PTO approvals are yours to manage as well.

You'll work alongside Stream's Construction, Leasing, Marketing, and Accounting teams regularly. The "Stream Team" model is collaborative by design, so strong internal communication is as important here as the client-facing work.

What You Bring vs. What You'll Build Here

Three or more years in commercial property management with some supervisory experience is the baseline. CAM reconciliations, annual budget preparation, and ownership reporting should already be familiar territory. Yardi or MRI proficiency matters, and comfort with Excel goes beyond basic spreadsheet use. A CPM or RPA designation, or active pursuit of one, signals the kind of professional seriousness Stream is looking for.

What the role develops is harder to list but worth naming. Managing a portfolio for third-party owners sharpens your ability to translate operational decisions into client-ready financial narratives, a skill that transfers directly to senior PM roles, portfolio director positions, or eventually asset management. You'll get repetitions with ownership reporting at a level of detail that builds genuine financial acumen, not just operational coordination.

  • Bachelor's degree preferred
  • 3+ years of commercial property management experience, with supervisory responsibility
  • CPM or RPA designation preferred (or in progress)
  • Experience with Yardi, MRI, Kardin, AvidXchange, or similar platforms
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills across clients, tenants, and vendors
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word, and Teams
  • Analytical mindset with the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously

Stream is headquartered in Dallas and has built a reputation as one of the faster-growing commercial services firms in the country. This role is onsite and full-time.

job.title: Cortland Duluth Maintenance Hiring Event - 11/10/2026
job.description:
What's Happening and What You'll Do
