  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Bilingual in English and Spanish (required, not preferred)
  • Background in property management, leasing, or residential customer service
  • Comfort with Microsoft Office, property management software, and social media platforms
  • Strong organizational habits and the ability to shift between tasks without losing track of details
  • Professional presence and communication skills across in-person, phone, and written channels
  • Ability to lift up to 25 lbs. and walk the property regularly
  • Reliable local transportation for occasional errands or marketing runs

Who Tends to Thrive Here

Candidates who do well in roles like this one usually have a genuine comfort with variety. On a given day you might be walking a prospective resident through a model unit in the morning, coordinating a vendor request before lunch, posting a community update to social media, and wrapping up by supporting an afternoon youth club session. People who need a tightly defined lane tend to find that exhausting. People who get energy from switching context and seeing immediate impact on the people around them tend to find it rewarding.

The bilingual requirement reflects the real demographics of the community you'd be serving. Residents who speak Spanish as a primary language aren't a niche population here. Your ability to communicate with them directly, without a workaround, shapes their experience in ways that matter. That's worth stating plainly because it's not a checkbox. It's a daily functional need.

Compensation includes a competitive base plus performance-based bonuses. This is an on-site, full-time position in Apopka, Florida.

job.title: Entry-Level Accounts Receivable Administrator
job.description:
Multifamily ownership at scale creates an operational layer that on-site teams simply can't manage alone. When a company like AIR Communities runs apartment communities across multiple major markets from a centralized platform, someone has to own the financial accuracy that keeps those properties running cleanly. This accounts receivable role sits at that intersection: corporate discipline applied to the messy, real-world details of resident ledgers, lease lifecycles, and delinquency management.

The Day-to-Day Work

This is a five-day, in-office position based at AIR's corporate offices in the Denver Tech Center. The team here provides centralized AR support across AIR's national portfolio, which means your work touches communities you'll never visit in person but still affects directly. On a given day, that looks like auditing resident account activity, working through a shared support mailbox, coordinating with on-site teams to make sure leasing-related transactions post correctly, and helping move non-payment files through the eviction support process when needed.

The delinquency piece is worth understanding before you apply. Supporting eviction-related files is a routine part of accounts receivable in multifamily, and at a portfolio this size, it's a consistent part of the workload. It requires steady communication, accurate recordkeeping, and the ability to follow policy precisely, especially when timelines are legally sensitive.

The schedule is a genuine asset here: consistent Monday through Friday, with evenings and weekends free. That's not the norm across all PM roles, and it's a meaningful quality-of-life factor for people building a career rather than burning through one.

What AIR Is Looking For

  • One to two years of experience in customer service, administrative work, retail, hospitality, or a comparable field
  • High accuracy in data entry and a track record of catching your own errors
  • Comfort picking up new software quickly (you'll work across multiple systems)
  • Strong written communication, since a significant portion of coordination happens through a centralized inbox
  • Self-directed work habits and the ability to prioritize without constant direction
  • Property management background is a plus, but the team will train someone who comes from outside the industry

Pay runs $24 to $27 per hour depending on experience. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, HSA/FSA options, company-paid short and long-term disability, a 401(k) with up to 6% employer match, paid parental leave up to 16 weeks, tuition assistance, and a 25% rent discount at any AIR community.

For someone who wants a foothold in corporate real estate operations, this role builds skills that transfer broadly: ledger reconciliation, delinquency workflows, cross-team communication, and systems fluency. Those are the same foundations that feed into property accounting, asset management support, or centralized operations leadership as a career develops.

job.title: Property Manager | Lease-Up | Pay $65k + Bonus & Lease Up Commissions
job.description:
Lease-up property management is a different job than stabilized asset management. You're building occupancy from zero, setting the tone for a new community, and handling the operational chaos that comes with a brand-new building. Village Green is hiring a Property Manager to do exactly that at a new construction property in Wentzville, MO.

What the Role Covers

You'll run the full operation: leasing, marketing, maintenance coordination, resident relations, and financials. During lease-up, that means heavy traffic management, pushing conversion, and keeping the team focused on velocity without letting service quality slip. Once the property stabilizes, the job shifts toward NOI performance, collections, and tightening operations.

Day-to-day, you're supervising both office and maintenance staff, managing reporting up to an Area Director, and staying on top of accounting and delinquency. Village Green expects their managers to own their numbers and hit budget objectives, not just pass along reports.

The compensation reflects the scope. Base pay is $65,000, with a quarterly bonus program and lease-up commissions on top of that. For a manager who can drive occupancy quickly, the commission structure makes this materially more than a standard PM salary.

What You Need to Bring

  • At least 2 years of multi-family property management experience, including supervising a team
  • Background managing luxury apartment communities
  • Strong financial and analytical skills, including budget accountability
  • Creative marketing ability and comfort with social media
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite
  • Flexibility to work evenings, weekends, and holidays as the lease-up demands
  • A bachelor's degree, or equivalent experience in lieu of one

The candidates who perform well in lease-up roles are the ones who can hold structure when everything around them is still being figured out. Construction punch lists, systems not fully set up, vendors still onboarding. If you've managed a lease-up before, you know this. If you haven't, this probably isn't the right entry point.

The Company Behind the Role

Village Green has been in property management for roughly 100 years. That kind of tenure means established systems, training, and institutional knowledge that newer operators often lack. For a manager stepping into a high-pressure lease-up, working under a company with deep operational infrastructure is a real advantage.

Benefits include medical, dental, vision, and a 401(k) with employer match. Pre-employment drug screening and background checks are required. Village Green participates in E-Verify.

job.title: Property Administrator
job.description:
Commercial property management runs on paperwork, relationships, and financial accuracy in equal measure. When a portfolio falls behind on AP coding, COI tracking, or AR follow-up, the Property Manager loses hours they don't have. The Property Administrator role exists to close that gap, keeping the back office sharp so the front-facing work can happen on time.

Stream Realty Partners, a full-service commercial real estate firm founded in 1996 and operating coast to coast across office, industrial, retail, and other asset types, is hiring a Property Administrator for its Phoenix operations. This is an onsite, hands-on position supporting the day-to-day management of a commercial portfolio.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

A significant portion of this role lives inside the financials. On the payables side, you'll code and verify invoices against the approved budget before routing them to the Property Manager for sign-off. On the receivables side, you'll run monthly AR reviews and help prepare late notices and default notices when tenants fall behind. You'll also support the preparation of monthly and quarterly financial reports, which means you need to be comfortable reading numbers and understanding what they represent, not just entering them.

Beyond the ledger, you'll manage vendor and tenant Certificates of Insurance, a detail that sounds routine but creates real liability exposure when it slips. You'll draft and coordinate service contracts, log work order requests, schedule move-ins and move-outs, and help plan tenant events. The front desk function is part of this role too: phones, visitors, deliveries, and message routing all run through this position.

Yardi experience is a plus. Microsoft Excel and Word proficiency is expected from day one.

Who Fits This Role Well

  • A bachelor's degree (preferred) with coursework or work experience touching accounting, finance, business administration, or real estate
  • Basic accounting fluency. You should understand debits, credits, and how an invoice moves through an approval workflow
  • Strong attention to detail, particularly when working across multiple tenants, vendors, and budget line items simultaneously
  • Clear written and verbal communication. You'll interact with tenants, vendors, and internal teams regularly
  • Genuine interest in growing inside commercial property management, not just filling a coordinator seat

One honest note on career trajectory: Property Administrator roles in commercial real estate are well-established pipelines into Property Manager positions. Candidates who treat the financial reporting and vendor management components as learning opportunities rather than administrative chores tend to move up faster. The AP/AR experience here maps directly to what a PM handles at the portfolio level, and firms like Stream promote from within when the fundamentals are strong.

job.title: Apartment Service Technician (HVAC/EPA Certified)
job.description:
Morguard operates as a fully integrated real estate investment and management company, and their onsite maintenance teams carry real weight in how communities perform. At the technician level, this kind of role is where hands-on skills get sharpened into genuine expertise. The person who excels here builds a reputation across every trade, and that reputation travels.

The Work Itself

This is a full-time position running Sunday through Thursday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM, at a multifamily community in Aurora, CO. You'll work under the Lead Maintenance Technician and Community Manager, handling the daily flow of resident work orders, participating in preventative maintenance programs, and contributing to unit turns when apartments go vacant. Make-ready work is a core part of the job. Turning a unit well, closing the punch list clean, and getting it leased-ready on schedule directly affects occupancy and the community's overall performance.

Daily property walks are part of the rhythm here. You'll know your grounds, your buildings, and the mechanical systems running beneath them. When work orders come in, the expectation is thorough diagnosis, not surface fixes. Communicating proactively with your supervisor when something runs longer than expected is treated as professionalism, not a weakness.

You'll also participate in the on-call rotation, splitting after-hours emergency coverage with your teammates. Each on-call week earns a $100 stipend paid directly to you, regardless of whether you're called out.

What You Bring

  • HVAC Type I and Type II certification, or EPA Universal. This is a firm requirement, not a preference.
  • Working knowledge across plumbing, drywall, painting, carpentry, appliance repair, and basic electrical troubleshooting
  • Prior experience in a multifamily setting, specifically closing work orders and completing unit turns
  • Comfort responding to after-hours emergencies as part of a shared rotation
  • High school diploma required; technical school background is a plus

Pay, Benefits, and Where This Role Leads

The hourly rate runs $25 to $26, with quarterly bonuses of up to 5% of annual salary based on performance. Morguard offers employer-provided medical insurance, a 401(k) with dollar-for-dollar matching and immediate vesting, paid time off including summer hours, and an education reimbursement program. There's also an employee housing discount within their portfolio, subject to availability.

From a career standpoint, a technician who consistently closes work orders cleanly, communicates well, and handles turns efficiently is the natural pipeline for Lead Maintenance Technician roles. From there, the path to Maintenance Supervisor or Regional Facilities positions is straightforward in companies of Morguard's scale. The HVAC certification you already hold is the credential that distinguishes you at every step. Technicians who also build fluency in capex projects and vendor coordination tend to move fastest into supervisory tracks.

What separates strong candidates here is less about the breadth of certifications and more about the quality of follow-through. A technician who documents accurately, communicates without being prompted, and treats each work order as a direct reflection on the resident's experience is the one who earns expanded responsibility. Morguard invests in that kind of person.

job.title: Leasing & Sales Consultant- Cortland Chisholm Trail
job.description:
Leasing is a skill set that doesn't always get the credit it deserves. At its core, it's persuasion, empathy, and organization working together at the same time. The Leasing and Sales Consultant role at Cortland Chisholm Trail in Fort Worth calls on all three, often within the same conversation.

What This Role Actually Demands

Your days will center on people: prospects calling to ask about availability, walk-ins who showed up on a whim, and current residents who stop by the office with questions. What separates strong leasing consultants from average ones here isn't just charisma. It's the discipline behind the charm. Following up with a lead the same afternoon, keeping CRM notes accurate after every interaction, tracking conversion rates without being asked, and adjusting your pitch when something isn't working. The consultative side matters, too. You're listening for what someone actually needs and matching it to what the community offers, not running through a script.

Beyond the one-on-one sales work, you'll manage the community's social media presence and help plan resident events that build real connection among people who live there. That's a broader scope than many leasing roles carry, and it means your work touches both occupancy and retention.

The Relationships You'll Manage

You'll spend most of your time with prospects and residents, but the internal dynamics matter just as much. Cortland operates as a vertically integrated company, meaning design, construction, and management run through the same organization. That structure gives you more internal resources to draw on than you'd find at a third-party management shop, but it also means brand standards are taken seriously. How you present the community, how you handle a complaint, how you show up on a tour: these things reflect a company with real brand investment. You'll get coaching on all of it, and the expectation is that you act on it.

Cortland is one of the ten largest multifamily owners and operators in the country. Working inside that scale means you're not figuring things out from scratch. There are systems, processes, and performance benchmarks already in place. Your job is to execute within that structure and push your own numbers.

A Good Fit for This Role

  • At least six months of experience in sales, customer service, or a role where you were held to measurable goals
  • Comfort with CRM tools, or a genuine willingness to learn them quickly
  • Organized follow-up habits. Leads go cold fast, and timeliness is part of the job
  • A coachable disposition. Feedback here is specific and frequent, and it's meant to help you hit your targets
  • A polished, professional presence that fits a premium brand environment

Fort Worth's rental market has stayed competitive, with steady population growth and continued apartment development along the southwest corridor near Chisholm Trail Parkway. That means traffic exists, but so does competition. The consultants who perform well in this market are the ones who close on the first visit when possible and nurture prospects who need more time rather than letting them go quiet.

For someone building a career in multifamily, a leasing consultant role at a company like Cortland is a real starting point. The skills you develop here, pipeline management, objection handling, resident relations, CRM fluency, all carry directly into roles like assistant manager, leasing manager, or community manager down the line.

job.title: Administrative Assistant
job.description:
The Skills This Role Runs On

Administrative work at a large real estate firm demands a specific combination of organizational precision and communication fluency. This role at Lincoln Property Company's Humble, TX office puts both to work every day. You'll manage calendars and coordinate meeting logistics for a team, which sounds straightforward until competing deadlines and shifting priorities require you to make judgment calls without being asked. You'll draft and proofread correspondence and memos, process invoices and expense reports, maintain filing systems, and handle department purchase orders. The throughline across all of it is accuracy. Errors in data entry, invoice processing, or correspondence reflect directly on the team you support.

Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Word, Excel, and Outlook, is a real requirement here. Calendar management and internal coordination run through Outlook. Reports and correspondence go through Word. Expense tracking and departmental data often live in Excel. If you can move fluidly across all three without friction, you'll spend less time on mechanics and more time on the actual work.

What the Day-to-Day Looks Like

On a typical morning, you might reconcile a purchase order, confirm room bookings for two afternoon meetings, and route a memo for signatures before noon. Onboarding support for new team members adds another layer when it's active. Order and supply tracking for the office is an ongoing task with no clear finish line. The role is fully in-office during standard business hours, so the rhythm is consistent and structured.

Lincoln operates across a broad portfolio including multifamily, commercial, industrial, and mixed-use assets. That scope means the team you're supporting may work across multiple asset types or client relationships simultaneously. Background in commercial real estate is a genuine advantage here because the vocabulary and workflow expectations differ from general corporate admin. You'll encounter terminology related to property operations, client reporting, and leasing activity. Familiarity with that context reduces the learning curve.

What Sets Strong Candidates Apart

Two years of administrative or clerical experience is the baseline. What separates candidates who do well in this environment is the ability to manage a varied workload without waiting for someone to sequence it for them. Lincoln describes its culture as encouraging an entrepreneurial mindset, and even in an administrative function, that means taking ownership of your workload and flagging problems early rather than waiting for direction on every task.

  • High school diploma or equivalent required
  • 2+ years of administrative or clerical experience
  • Commercial real estate experience preferred
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook)
  • Ability to prioritize independently across multiple concurrent tasks
  • Must be authorized to work in the United States without visa sponsorship

Lincoln offers a full benefits package including medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with traditional and Roth options, flexible time off, paid sick leave, and company-paid life insurance and long-term disability coverage.

job.title: Assistant Manager - Montair at Somerset Hill
job.description:
Tumwater sits in a quieter pocket of the South Sound, but it draws steady renter demand from state government employment, the nearby JBLM workforce, and residents priced out of Olympia proper. Montair at Somerset Hill operates in that kind of market, where occupancy holds well but retaining residents through renewal cycles matters just as much as putting new traffic through the door. The Assistant Manager role here is built around both.

The Day-to-Day

This position covers the operational and financial core of the property. You'll handle rent collection and daily deposits, maintain resident files with accuracy and confidentiality, track delinquency, and step into the property manager role when the Business Manager is out. Alongside that, you're inspecting make-ready apartments before move-ins, reviewing final account statements at move-out, and staying close enough to the sub-market to flag anything that might affect occupancy or income.

You'll also carry a share of leasing responsibility. When traffic is heavy or the team needs coverage, you're showing units. You're participating in resident retention events and community programming. And when residents have complaints, you're the one addressing them directly, not routing them through a queue.

Olympus uses RealPage and Knock (Onesite), so familiarity with that stack is a real advantage coming in. Candidates who've managed collections, coordinated move-out dispositions, or handled liability referral protocols in a prior onsite role will get up to speed faster.

What the Schedule Looks Like

  • Full-time, Monday through Friday, generally 9 AM to 6 PM
  • Flexibility for resident events after hours
  • First weekend of each month required
  • Prior onsite experience as an Assistant Manager or a cross-trained Leasing Consultant is required

Growth and Culture

Olympus has earned the National Apartment Association's Top Employer recognition three consecutive years (2023, 2024, 2025). That kind of consistency usually reflects something real about how the company runs internally, and in this case the emphasis is on internal mobility and recognition. The Assistant Manager title is a well-worn path to a Business Manager seat, and Olympus has formal career pathing to support that progression. Compensation is experience-based with monthly renewal incentives and quarterly bonuses on top of base pay, plus a benefits package that includes an apartment rental allowance and tuition reimbursement.

If you've built solid financial habits onsite, know how to run a leasing office with attention to detail, and want to work toward running a property on your own, Montair at Somerset Hill is a reasonable next step.

job.title: Leasing Consultant - Part Time
job.description:
Part-time leasing roles tend to attract people who want steady hourly work without the full 40-hour grind. What makes this one worth a closer look is the company behind it. Weinstein Properties has been family-owned for over 70 years, operates more than 60 communities across five states, and runs a hands-on model that puts real weight on customer experience rather than just occupancy numbers.

The position is at Bexley at Heritage in Wake Forest, NC. Starting pay is $18/hour, with increases based on experience, quarterly bonuses, and a 10% rent discount. The schedule runs about 20 hours per week, with most or all Saturdays required and flexible weekday hours negotiated around your availability.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

You're the first person a prospect talks to, and often the last touchpoint before they decide to sign or walk. That means touring units, answering questions by phone and email, following up on leads, and helping current residents feel heard when they have concerns. But this isn't a pure sales role. Administrative tasks, property walks, inspecting make-ready units, and pitching in on community appearance are all part of the job. Weinstein is upfront: everyone does a little bit of everything.

Some days will be interrupted constantly. A prospect walks in while you're mid-task, a resident has a complaint, and your to-do list shifts on the fly. That's not unusual for leasing work at any property. Knowing it going in makes it easier to handle.

Who Does Well Here

Weinstein explicitly welcomes people without leasing experience, and they mean it. Their training program is built for that. What they're actually filtering for is reliability, warmth with strangers, and a genuine interest in helping people find a home. Strong candidates for this specific role tend to come from retail, hospitality, or customer service backgrounds where they've handled high-interaction environments without losing their composure.

  • Comfortable talking to people in person and in writing
  • Organized enough to manage follow-ups and administrative tasks alongside tours
  • Available most Saturdays without it being a recurring conflict
  • Able to take direction during training and apply it independently afterward

For the right person, this is a legitimate entry point into property management. Weinstein promotes from within, and leasing is the traditional starting point for site managers, assistant managers, and eventually community director roles. A part-time leasing position that gives you real training and Saturday traffic exposure builds the foundation faster than many full-time roles that keep consultants siloed in one task.

job.title: Leasing Consultant - 3300 Tamarac
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

The Leasing Consultant role at 3300 Tamarac Apartments puts you at the center of the community's daily traffic. You'll greet and qualify prospective residents, walk units, and convert interest into signed leases. That means understanding fair housing compliance well enough to screen applicants correctly and consistently, preparing lease packages, and coordinating with the maintenance team to make sure move-ins go smoothly from a punch list standpoint, not just a paperwork one.

Day-to-day, you're also maintaining rental files, entering data accurately into property management software, and helping with the monthly administrative close. When residents come to you with complaints or maintenance concerns, you handle those conversations professionally and follow them through to resolution. Rent collection and delinquency follow-up are part of the rhythm too. This is front-line leasing work: visible, fast, and detail-dependent.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of property management or related leasing experience (preferred)
  • Sales instincts and customer service habits that hold up under pressure
  • Comfort with leasing software and accurate data entry
  • Professional communication skills, written and verbal
  • The organizational discipline to keep files current and paperwork clean
  • A team orientation. MG Properties promotes from within, which means your coworkers today are often your future peers at higher levels

Where This Role Fits in the Craft

Leasing Consultant roles build a specific skill set that transfers directly into senior leasing, assistant manager, and eventually property manager positions. You develop fluency in the full prospect-to-resident lifecycle: traffic generation, conversion, application processing, lease execution, and move-in coordination. If you're early in a property management career, this is one of the cleaner paths toward understanding how occupancy decisions affect NOI at the property level.

MG Properties has been acquiring and operating apartment communities across the Western U.S. for more than 30 years. Denver is a competitive multifamily market, and 3300 Tamarac sits in that context. Strong candidates here will know how to handle objections during a tour, recognize when a concession conversation is appropriate, and understand that consistent occupancy is built through dozens of small interactions done well, not just the occasional great tour. If you've worked a leasing office and learned to treat every walk-in as a real opportunity, this role will use that skill immediately.

job.title: Leasing Consultant, Full-Time
job.description:
Student housing leasing runs on communication skills, and this role uses them constantly. At The Vue in Fayetteville, The Scion Group is hiring a full-time Experience Team Member (ETM) to handle the leasing and resident engagement work that keeps a student community occupied and functioning.

The Skills This Role Draws On Daily

The ETM role sits at the intersection of sales, marketing, and front-line customer service. You'll give community tours, field objections from prospective residents and their parents, and relay patterns in those objections back to your management team. That feedback loop matters. If the same concern keeps coming up, leadership needs to hear it. You'll also contribute to local marketing efforts and support social media content, which means you have to understand who you're talking to: students who are choosing where to live, often for the first time, with parents frequently involved in the decision.

Property administration rounds out the day. Package management, office upkeep, maintenance request follow-up, and helping keep the clubhouse and amenities in presentable shape are all part of the job. None of it is glamorous, but it's what keeps a property running between the more visible leasing moments.

What the Schedule Actually Looks Like

Daytime business hours cover most of your schedule, but the role includes an after-hours on-call rotation. Lockout calls happen. You need to be reachable and available when they do. Turn periods (when hundreds of students move out and back in over a short window in late summer) require full availability and sustained energy. That's when the whole team earns it. If you've never worked a student housing turn, expect it to be fast, physical, and demanding. It's also the period that teaches you more about property operations than any other stretch of the year.

What Scion Is Looking For

  • A customer-first mindset, with real interpersonal range across a diverse resident population
  • Reliability and self-discipline, especially during high-traffic leasing seasons
  • Flexibility when priorities shift quickly, which they will in a collegiate environment
  • Availability during summers, holidays, and turn periods
  • Eligibility to work in the United States (visa sponsorship is not available)

Scion operates student communities across the country and has built a recognizable operational model in that niche. For someone early in a property management career, an ETM role at a professionally managed student housing property is solid footing. The leasing skills, resident communication habits, and operational exposure you build here carry directly into assistant manager or leasing manager roles, either within student housing or conventional multifamily.

The position comes with health, dental, and vision insurance, 401k matching, paid time off, paid parental leave, a discretionary annual bonus, and learning reimbursement. The work is located on-site at The Vue, 1111 W Stadium Dr, Fayetteville, AR.

job.title: Community Manager (Celestina Garden Apartments)
job.description:
Celestina Garden Apartments sits in Sonoma County, one of the more expensive housing markets in Northern California. The residents MidPen serves here have limited options and real stakes in stable housing. That context shapes this role in ways a conventional property management job doesn't.

What You'll Actually Do

Day to day, you're running the full operation at Celestina Garden. That means rent collection, delinquency follow-up, security deposit accounting, and bank deposits handled correctly and on time. You'll process applications, certifications, and re-certs under HUD, TCAC, and Fair Housing requirements. Affordable housing compliance isn't paperwork for its own sake. A missed re-cert or a documentation error can affect a resident's housing eligibility, so accuracy here carries real consequences.

You'll lead a small site team, which means performance reviews, coaching, and being the person who sets the tone when things get difficult. You'll manage unit turns within established timeframes, keep a preventative maintenance schedule, and walk the property regularly to stay ahead of curb appeal and repair issues. When emergencies happen, and they will, you're the one coordinating the response.

MidPen's model pairs property management with onsite resident services. You won't run those programs, but you'll work closely with that team. Building that relationship matters. A community where property staff and services staff operate in silos is harder to manage and harder to live in.

What You Bring

  • At least three years of multi-family residential management experience, with two of those years in affordable housing specifically
  • One year of supervisory experience, with a track record of developing staff rather than just directing them
  • Tax Credit Specialist (TCS) or Certified Occupancy Specialist (COS) certification, or the ability to obtain one within six months (MidPen covers the cost)
  • Working knowledge of Fair Housing laws and the ability to pass the FHA test within your first 60 days
  • Comfort with RealPage and the Microsoft Office Suite
  • An associate degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience

A Few Things Worth Knowing

Affordable housing management is a different discipline than conventional Class A or B work. The compliance layer is heavier. Resident populations often include seniors, families, and individuals with special needs who bring more complexity to the community dynamic. Difficult conversations with residents happen, and they require patience and clear judgment. The paperwork load is real. So is the impact when the operation runs well.

Company-provided on-site housing is available, which is a meaningful benefit in a market where Sonoma housing costs are significant. Pay ranges from $25.62 to $28.82 hourly based on experience, with a full benefits package that includes health, dental, vision, 403(b), paid parental leave, and tuition reimbursement. Candidates who move from this role into senior property management within nonprofit affordable housing often find the compliance depth they built here travels well across LIHTC portfolios anywhere in the state.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
A prospect calls at 5:45 PM, fifteen minutes before closing, interested in a two-bedroom. You pull up availability, schedule a tour for tomorrow, and follow up with a lead card before you leave. That's a normal Tuesday at Hawthorne Northwest.

The Role

Hawthorne Residential Partners ranks among the 50 largest multifamily management companies in the country, with a portfolio rooted in the Southeast. The Assistant Community Manager at their Greensboro property on Brigham Road carries real operational weight. This position spans leasing, resident relations, and financial administration, with the expectation that you can step into the Community Manager's seat when needed and keep things moving without missing a beat.

On the leasing side, you'll conduct tours, work your lead pipeline, process applications and renewals, and manage the community's social media presence to drive traffic and keep residents engaged. Occupancy and retention both live in this role.

The financial piece is equally substantive. You'll post payments, scan checks, review ledgers for accuracy, monitor delinquency, make weekly collection calls, and coordinate eviction procedures when they become necessary. You'll also assist with financial reporting up to regional leadership. This is the kind of financial exposure that separates candidates who later become strong Community Managers from those who stay perpetually in support roles.

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, and Saturdays from 10 AM to 4 PM, with one weekday off to keep the week at 40 hours. Evening and weekend availability may come up for resident events.

What Hawthorne Is Looking For

  • High school diploma or GED equivalent
  • Two years of property management experience preferred
  • At least six months in an assistant community manager capacity, ideally
  • Valid driver's license
  • CALP designation is a plus

The candidates who do well here aren't just personable leasing agents. They read a delinquency report and act on it. They de-escalate a frustrated resident and document the interaction cleanly. They can hold the office together on a Saturday when the Community Manager is out. Financial comfort, conflict resolution, and organizational follow-through matter just as much as a warm handshake.

Hawthorne offers monthly leasing and renewal commissions, quarterly performance bonuses, and an hourly base. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, 401k with employer match, paid time off (including your birthday), paid sick leave, parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, company-paid life insurance, telehealth access, and health and wellness incentives. Their internal Career Path Program is active, meaning this role has a defined track toward Community Manager for candidates who perform.

Greensboro's rental market has held relatively steady occupancy, and the Hawthorne Northwest location on Brigham Road puts this community in an established corridor with consistent demand. For someone looking to build serious multifamily operations experience in a mid-size Southeast market, this is a solid entry point with room to grow.

job.title: Leasing Consultant (Broadlands)
job.description:
Leasing at a residential community is a relationship job wrapped inside a sales job. The consultant who thrives here isn't just closing applications. They're the person residents call when something feels off, the one who remembers names, and the one whose follow-up actually gets returned. Van Metre's Broadlands Apartments in Ashburn, VA is hiring a Leasing Consultant to fill that role.

What the Job Looks Like Day to Day

You'll spend a meaningful chunk of each shift on traffic: greeting walk-ins, answering calls, scheduling tours, and following up with prospects by phone and email until an application comes in or the lead goes cold. Grassroots marketing falls in your lap too, so expect some outreach activity beyond the leasing office walls.

The rest of your time splits between current residents and property upkeep. That means checking in on service request status, keeping residents in the loop, handling renewals, and helping plan community events. You'll also run three exterior inspections per week and inspect vacant units before they're shown, logging anything that needs attention from the maintenance team. The make-ready process depends on consultants catching issues early, and Van Metre expects that discipline here.

Weekend availability is required. Bilingual candidates have an advantage given the Northern Virginia market.

Compensation and What Van Metre Offers

  • Base pay: $20.00 to $21.00 per hour, based on experience
  • Annual bonus potential up to $5,000, paid quarterly
  • Leasing and renewal commissions on top of base
  • 11 paid holidays, 10 vacation days, 10 sick days, plus personal days, volunteer days, winter break, a birthday day off, and a day for your annual physical
  • Comprehensive parental and bonding leave
  • Company-matched 401(k) with access to retirement planning coaches
  • Annual wellness reimbursement up to $900
  • Tuition reimbursement, company-paid certifications, and mentorship programs
  • Rental discounts and Van Metre home purchase discounts

Van Metre has operated in the DC metro area since 1955, and Broadlands sits in one of Loudoun County's more established planned communities. Ashburn has seen sustained demand from tech sector growth tied to data center expansion and the Silver Line extension, which gives leasing staff here a concrete story to tell prospective residents about the location.

Candidates with backgrounds in hospitality, retail sales, or customer-facing service tend to translate well into leasing. The skills that separate strong performers are straightforward: consistent follow-up, comfort on the phone, and the ability to build trust quickly with someone making a significant housing decision. If you treat every tour like it matters, that compounds over time into strong occupancy and retention numbers.

job.title: Helper A - Residential Maintenance Technician Local 399
job.description:
This is a union maintenance position at The Belmont, a residential property at 3170 N Sheridan Rd in Chicago's Lakeview neighborhood. You'd be working Tuesday through Saturday, 2pm to 10pm, under Local 399 at a starting rate of $29.39 per hour.

The shift matters here. An evening schedule means you're the person residents reach when something goes wrong after work hours. Service requests, water infiltration reports, after-hours calls when you're on rotation. You'll work under and alongside the Building Engineer, handling work orders, assisting with apartment turns, running preventative maintenance tasks like HVAC filter swaps and sewer rodding, and coordinating vendor access when repairs go beyond the scope of in-house work. Janitorial and grounds duties are also part of the job, including snow removal when Chicago winters demand it.

Reside Living expects EPA certification and at least one year of full-time maintenance experience. Plumbing, electrical, HVAC, and hot water systems are the core mechanical skills they want. You'll document your work through a mobile app, so comfort with a smartphone and basic computer literacy matters.

Qualifications

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • EPA certification (current)
  • Minimum one year of full-time maintenance or related field experience
  • Familiarity with mechanical systems: plumbing, electric, HVAC, hot water heaters
  • Proficiency with Outlook and Microsoft Suite
  • Ability to lift up to 75 lbs regularly; occasional heavier loads with assistance
  • Comfortable on ladders, stairs, and on your feet for the majority of your shift

Benefits come through Local 399 and include full health coverage. Reside also offers free employee parking, a $50 monthly phone stipend, and a 25% rent discount after 90 days, which carries real weight given Lakeview rental prices.

One thing worth knowing about this shift: the 2pm to 10pm window is quieter for coordinating vendors and project work, but busier for resident interaction. Most residents are home by then. That means your customer service manner shows up constantly, not just when you choose to engage. Strong candidates in this type of role understand that how you talk to a resident in the hallway is as much a part of the job as fixing what brought you there.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager at Cottonwood Ridgeview Apartments
job.description:
Cottonwood Residential operates a growing national multifamily portfolio, and the Assistant Property Manager at Cottonwood Ridgeview in Plano sits right at the center of how that portfolio actually performs. This is an operational role with real financial responsibility, real people dynamics, and regular moments where you'll need to step up and own decisions without the Property Manager in the room.

Day to day, you're covering a wide range: posting rent, processing applications, staying current on unit availability and pricing, walking the property, coordinating with vendors, and responding to residents who need answers quickly. You'll also support leasing efforts directly, which means you need to be comfortable talking with prospects, understanding what moves people to sign, and following through on the administrative side of the application process. The community uses Self-Guided Tours, so part of keeping that running smoothly falls to you too, including unit readiness and daily inspections.

The team support piece carries genuine weight here. You'll assist with onboarding new hires, help set expectations for consistent performance, and occasionally need to deliver hard feedback. When the Property Manager is out, you're not just holding down the fort. You're making the calls, fielding escalations, and keeping the community running. That's a real leadership expectation, and candidates who've only observed that kind of responsibility from the sidelines will feel the difference quickly.

One dynamic worth knowing: Plano sits in a competitive DFW submarket where Class A communities have trained renters to expect a polished, responsive experience. Residents here aren't comparing you to the budget complex down the street. They're comparing you to every other well-amenitized option they toured last weekend. That raises the bar on follow-up speed, communication quality, and how move-ins are handled. Candidates who've worked in competitive lease-up or stabilized Class A environments will recognize that pressure immediately.

What separates strong candidates from average ones in this role isn't just experience with property management software (Entrata experience is a plus here) or familiarity with the basics of leasing. It's the ability to hold multiple threads at once without dropping the resident-facing ones. When you're mid-way through a delinquency report and a vendor is waiting on an invoice approval and two residents have open service requests, the ones who thrive prioritize without being prompted and communicate without being asked.

What you'll bring

  • At least 2 years of multifamily property management experience, with 1 or more years specifically in an assistant manager capacity
  • Solid understanding of leasing fundamentals, rent posting, and basic financial reporting
  • Strong organizational habits and accurate record-keeping
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office; experience with Entrata or similar platforms preferred
  • Confident communicator with residents, vendors, and team members alike
  • Comfortable with a schedule that occasionally requires early starts or extended hours
  • Physically able to walk the property regularly, climb stairs, and handle light lifting up to 25 lbs.

Cottonwood Residential offers competitive compensation and a real path to growth within an expanding organization. If you're the kind of person who notices what needs doing before someone points it out, this role gives you a lot of room to show that.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Northglenn, CO
job.description:
Maintenance Technicians at the right company build a toolkit that compounds over time. A year spent at a well-managed, owner-operated community like Carrick Bend in Northglenn, CO teaches you more than repair work. It teaches you how a property breathes: what deferred maintenance costs in NOI, how curb appeal connects to traffic, and why make-ready speed matters to occupancy. Berkshire Residential Investments owns and manages its own assets, which means the maintenance team operates with real accountability and real visibility into how the work connects to the bigger picture.

The day-to-day here is genuinely varied. You might start the morning walking punch list items from a recent turn, shift to a plumbing call mid-morning, then spend part of the afternoon helping audit shop inventory or checking out equipment condition. The role touches appliance repair, electrical, carpentry, and basic building systems. Curb appeal is part of the job too, not an afterthought. Technicians who treat the property's exterior with the same attention as an interior unit tend to stand out quickly in this kind of environment.

Berkshire's in-house structure means you're not a contractor cycling through multiple sites. You're embedded in one community, which lets you develop relationships with residents and get to know the property's quirks, its recurring issues, and its seasonal demands. That familiarity builds the kind of institutional knowledge that makes a technician genuinely irreplaceable over time.

What you bring

  • At least one year of hands-on maintenance experience in a residential community setting
  • Working knowledge across plumbing, electrical, appliances, carpentry, and general building maintenance
  • Comfort using computers and related software for work orders or communications
  • Strong written and verbal English communication skills
  • A service mindset that extends to residents and teammates alike

From a career trajectory standpoint, a solid run as a Maintenance Technician in a company like Berkshire typically positions you well for a Lead Tech or Maintenance Supervisor role. The technicians who move up fastest are the ones who treat inventory control and safety compliance as seriously as the repair work itself. Those habits signal readiness for supervisory responsibility, and companies that own their assets tend to promote from within when they can.

Berkshire offers a rent discount, three weeks of vacation, personal development planning, and a benefits package. The team culture leans toward high performance without pretense. If quality workmanship and consistent service are things you take pride in, this is a good place to build on that.

job.title: Regional Real Estate Manager - San Diego Region
job.description:
Third-party fee management at the regional level is a different animal than in-house work. You're not just accountable to your company's performance standards. You're accountable to owners who have their own return expectations, their own timelines, and their own tolerance for variance. Sunrise Management operates in that space, and this role sits at the center of it.

The Regional Real Estate Manager position covers a portfolio of multifamily properties across the San Diego region, reporting to a Regional Vice President or Regional Asset Director. The scope includes everything from on-site team supervision to budget preparation to owner communication. You're the connective tissue between what's happening at the property level and what ownership needs to see at the portfolio level.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

A meaningful portion of this role is financial. You'll prepare annual budgets, run monthly variance analyses, and identify where NOI is slipping and why. That might mean expense creep on a mid-renovation asset, delinquency trending the wrong direction at one property, or a marketing spend that isn't converting traffic to leases. You're expected to spot those problems and move on them, not wait for a directive.

Team management takes up the other major share of your time. You're supervising property managers and property administrators across multiple sites, which means performance reviews, hiring decisions in partnership with HR, and the kind of ongoing coaching that builds accountable site teams. Some of those conversations will be easy. Some won't.

Client relationship work is real and ongoing. In fee management, clients can and do move their assets. Keeping owner confidence means proactive communication, accurate reporting, and showing up when something goes sideways, not just when results are good.

Requirements Worth Taking Seriously

  • Active California Real Estate License, in good standing. This is a hard requirement, not a preference.
  • At least five years of multifamily property management experience with direct oversight of multiple properties
  • Demonstrated ability to read and act on financial performance data, including budget-to-actual analysis
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel for financial work
  • Strong communication skills across audiences: site staff, regional leadership, and property owners

Candidates who tend to stand out in regional roles like this are the ones who've already carried a portfolio through something difficult. A lease-up, a transition from a prior management company, a capex cycle that ran long. The technical skills matter, but the judgment that comes from having managed through pressure is what separates candidates who can describe the job from those who can actually do it.

The salary range is $120,000 to $150,000, combining base pay and supplemental wages. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, FSA options, company-paid life insurance, and paid time off.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is a full-scope maintenance technician role at a Griffis Residential community in San Diego. You'll work under the Service Manager handling the work that keeps a luxury apartment property running: make-readies, service requests, preventive maintenance, and the occasional emergency that doesn't care what time it is. The 30-minute response expectation on emergency calls is written into the job, so if quick pivots aren't your operating mode, that's worth knowing upfront.

Day to day, you're turning units, working through punch lists, and fielding resident requests across plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliances, and carpentry. You'll also carry pool and spa maintenance responsibilities, which means keeping chemical logs current and the CPO license current with them. Inspections, litter rounds, and grounds upkeep are part of the rotation too. The unglamorous stuff matters at a property that positions itself in the luxury tier.

On the financial side, you'll work with the Service Manager to manage parts inventory and keep spend in line. At this level, that mostly means not over-ordering and knowing when to repair versus replace.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of hands-on maintenance experience in multi-family housing, hospitality, or a closely related setting
  • Working knowledge of HVAC, plumbing, electrical systems, and appliance repair
  • CPO license and EPA 608 certification preferred; both required within the first six months if not already held
  • Physical ability to lift up to 75 pounds and work outdoors across weather conditions
  • Basic computer proficiency for work order systems and maintenance records
  • Strong communication and resident-facing professionalism
  • Bilingual English/Spanish is a genuine asset in San Diego's rental market

Context Worth Having

San Diego's rental market runs competitive and Class A product here gets scrutinized by residents who expect fast response and clean finishes. Deferred maintenance shows up quickly in online reviews, and at Griffis, reputation scores are tied directly to the bonus structure, so the tech who takes pride in a clean punch list and zero callbacks tends to do well both in performance reviews and in their quarterly bonus numbers.

Pay runs $25.00 to $28.50 per hour. The benefits package is genuinely substantial: 50% rent discount, a 401(k) with up to 4% company match, three weeks of PTO accruing from day one, 11 paid holidays, paid parental leave, tuition reimbursement up to $5,250 annually, and multiple bonus programs tied to occupancy and online reputation. For a maintenance role, the total compensation picture here is worth looking at seriously.

Technicians who build strong diagnostic skills and develop vendor relationships often move into Service Manager roles within a few years. Multi-family maintenance experience translates well across property types, and the preventive maintenance exposure here builds the kind of documentation habits that matter at the next level.

job.title: Leasing Professional - RedPeak, Denver
job.description:
Leasing is one of those roles where three distinct skill sets have to work together at the same time: sales instincts, customer service patience, and operational follow-through. When all three click, you close leases. When any one of them lags, prospects slip, paperwork stalls, and occupancy drifts. This position with RedPeak at their 423-unit, 12-building portfolio in Denver demands all three, and it rewards people who've learned to balance them well.

What This Role Trains You to Do

The work centers on lead development and conversion. You'll manage the full funnel: answering inbound calls and online inquiries within required response windows, qualifying prospects based on their timeline and needs, building value through phone and email before the tour even happens, and then following through consistently after showings to keep deals moving. RedPeak sets specific weekly and monthly goals, and you'll work with a Sales Manager to understand where the pipeline stands and what marketing initiatives the community is running to drive traffic.

On the operational side, you'll handle lease paperwork from reservation through signing, run credit and background checks, and update prospect and resident records in Yardi. You'll walk units before move-in, coordinate make-ready punch checks, and prepare move-in gifts and key sets. You'll also compile weekly comp surveys and shop competing properties on a regular basis. That last responsibility is worth noting: consistent comp awareness sharpens your pricing instincts in ways that stay with you throughout a PM career.

Retention carries its own weight here. Roughly 15 percent of the role involves securing renewals, resolving resident issues quickly, and maintaining the kind of community feel that keeps people from looking elsewhere when their lease comes up.

Skills That Compound Over Time

Leasing consultants who pay attention to the full cycle, from traffic ratios to occupancy targets to renewal rates, build a genuinely useful mental model of how a property performs. You start to see how your close rate connects to NOI, how concession decisions affect the T-12, and how delinquency often traces back to weak screening earlier in the process. That systems-level understanding is what separates leasing professionals who move into Assistant Manager or Leasing Manager roles from those who stay in a pure leasing seat for years.

RedPeak is a Denver-focused owner-operator with 25 years in this specific market. They're not a national REIT managing assets from a distance. That focus means you're working with a team that has real institutional knowledge of Denver neighborhoods, and you'll develop local market fluency that carries weight whether you stay with RedPeak long-term or move into a broader multifamily career.

What Fits Well Here

  • Demonstrated sales track record, in property management or in any customer-facing sales role
  • Comfort managing multiple active leads simultaneously without letting follow-up fall through
  • Attention to leasing paperwork accuracy (Yardi experience is a plus)
  • High School diploma required; Bachelor's degree preferred
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • Ability to be on your feet during tours and at a desk for administrative work

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9am to 6pm, with a base pay range of $21 to $23 per hour plus bonuses. Benefits include full medical, dental, and vision coverage, employer-paid short-term disability, and a 401(k) with company match that vests on day one.

job.title: Grounds Specialist - Silas at Springwoods - Spring, TX
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

The Grounds Specialist at Silas at Springwoods is the person who sets the first impression every single day. You're out walking the property from early on, clearing litter, debris, and pet waste from breezeways, pool areas, common spaces, and grounds before most residents have had their morning coffee. That consistency matters more than it might sound. A clean, well-kept exterior tells residents they made the right choice, and it tells prospects the same thing before they ever step inside a unit.

Beyond the daily walks, you'll be checking and logging pool chemical levels, vacuuming the pool weekly, and keeping the grills and amenity areas in safe, working order. That means checking timers and knobs, not just wiping surfaces. You'll also keep trash areas organized on schedule and support the Maintenance Supervisor and Property Manager with general labor tasks as needs come up. Some weeks that's routine. Some weeks it's more demanding. The role requires flexibility and a willingness to put in more than 40 hours when the property needs it.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of general labor experience. Multifamily background is a plus but not required.
  • High school diploma or equivalent, preferred.
  • Certified Pool Operator (CPO) certification is preferred. If you don't have it yet, it's worth pursuing.
  • Comfortable using hand tools, cleaning equipment, and supplies across different tasks.
  • Able to lift up to 50 lbs and work outdoors in varying Texas weather conditions.
  • Good verbal and written communication. You'll interact with residents, team members, and occasionally vendors.
  • Strong time management. You're often moving independently through a daily routine without someone checking in on every step.

The Team and the Company

Davis Development is a privately held luxury apartment developer and property management company with over 25 years in the business. Their model is in-house and hands-on. They don't outsource the day-to-day; they put real decision-making in the hands of on-site teams. That means the people you work alongside, including your Maintenance Supervisor and Property Manager, are genuinely invested in how the property runs. There's a family-culture element here that isn't just marketing copy. It does mean expectations are real and consistent, though. The "work hard, take care of the details" ethos applies to this role as much as any other on the team.

One honest note: grounds work in Spring, TX means heat. Summers are long and humid, and a significant portion of this role happens outside. If you thrive working in that environment and take pride in physical, visible results, that's a genuine fit signal. The right person for this role finds satisfaction in a property that looks noticeably better because of their effort.

Benefits kick in on the first of the month after 30 days of employment and include medical, dental, vision, and behavioral health coverage. The 401(k) comes with a 4% employer match that vests immediately, plus company-paid life insurance, paid time off with carryover, a company apparel allowance, and access to training and development. Davis Development positions this role as a place to grow, not just a job to fill.

job.title: Leasing Professional, J. Coopers Row
job.description:
The Navy Yard submarket in Washington, DC has absorbed a significant amount of new high-rise inventory over the past decade, and it remains one of the city's most competitive lease-up corridors. J. Coopers Row sits directly next to Nationals Park at South Capitol Street, which means the leasing conversation here is as much about lifestyle and location as it is about floor plans. Jefferson Apartment Group is staffing this 312-unit, 12-story property with a Leasing Professional who can convert traffic into signed leases while representing the community well from day one.

The Property and the Role

J. Coopers Row carries a mix of studios, one-, two-, and three-bedroom apartments alongside ground-level rental townhomes with private entrances. That unit diversity means you'll be qualifying prospects across a wide range of budgets and lifestyle needs, and matching the right resident to the right product type. Day to day, you're walking units, showing models, processing applications, explaining lease terms and addenda, and posting availability across listing platforms. You'll also accept rental payments and handle notices to vacate, which means this isn't a pure sales role. Resident relations and basic administrative accuracy are part of the job from the start.

Jefferson Apartment Group operates as a fully integrated real estate firm across acquisition, development, construction, and property management, which gives the company unusual depth compared to a pure third-party management shop. That integration tends to show up in how decisions get made at the property level: there's generally more continuity between the development vision and how a community is actually managed and leased.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • Genuine comfort with a sales-oriented leasing process, including following up on leads and closing on the spot when the opportunity is there
  • Attention to leasing paperwork detail. Errors in applications or lease addenda create downstream problems for collections and renewals
  • Weekend availability. Saturdays especially tend to drive the highest walk-in traffic at urban high-rises, and this role requires it
  • Familiarity with listing platforms and online marketing, including Craigslist and ILS posting
  • Customer service experience in any fast-moving environment, retail, hospitality, or residential leasing all translate well here

A high school diploma is the minimum requirement. Additional education or vocational training is preferred but the real differentiator at this level is someone who can read a prospect, communicate clearly, and keep their paperwork clean under volume. The Navy Yard draws a mix of young professionals and federal-adjacent renters who typically do their research before visiting. Knowing the neighborhood's walkability, transit access, and entertainment options gives you a real edge in the leasing conversation.

Pay runs $24.00 to $26.00 per hour. Full-time employees receive medical, dental, and vision coverage for themselves and eligible family members, paid time off, performance-based bonus potential, and potential rental discounts. This is an in-office, on-site position.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
Affordable housing operations run on tighter margins and stricter compliance requirements than conventional multifamily. An Assistant Community Manager at an affordable community carries a heavier compliance load than the title might suggest, particularly when LIHTC certification and regulatory file maintenance are part of the daily rhythm.

Avanath, a recognized affordable housing provider, is hiring an Assistant Community Manager for its community in Willowbrook, IL. This is a hands-on operations role that spans rent collection, delinquency management, leasing support, compliance oversight, and full property leadership when the Community Manager is out.

The Operational Picture

Day to day, you're moving between the front desk and the back office. You'll handle rent posting, chase outstanding balances, and run delinquency procedures with an eye on keeping the ledger clean. You'll inspect vacancies and make-ready units, flag punch list items, and make sure models are show-ready for traffic. You'll pull monthly projection reporting and sit in on performance conversations with the Community Manager and Regional Manager. When the Community Manager is away, the property runs through you.

On the compliance side, this role requires working knowledge of the Low Income Housing Tax Credit program. File maintenance under LIHTC isn't optional or occasional. It's a core accountability here, and errors carry real consequences for the property's regulatory standing. If you've managed compliance files before, you understand the difference between a clean file and a costly audit finding.

Resident relations at an affordable community also require a different kind of patience. Residents may be navigating financial hardship, and part of this role is functioning as a resource center connecting people to information that helps them maintain housing stability and pay on time. That's a meaningful distinction from conventional lease-up or Class A operations.

What This Role Requires

  • At least 2 years of experience as an Assistant Community Manager
  • LIHTC and Tax Credit program knowledge (required, not preferred)
  • Demonstrated bookkeeping and rent collection track record
  • Working knowledge of Yardi Voyager
  • Solid understanding of Fair Housing and landlord/tenant law
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, and standard office tools
  • Strong interpersonal skills across diverse resident and staff populations

Candidates who stand out in affordable housing ops tend to be precise with paperwork and calm under pressure. Delinquency conversations require tact. Compliance errors require attention to detail before they happen, not after. If your background includes both the financial side of property management and hands-on resident engagement in an income-restricted environment, this role fits that profile well.

Avanath emphasizes culture and purpose alongside performance. The Willowbrook location gives you a suburban Chicago market with genuine community ties. This role can reasonably lead toward a Community Manager seat, particularly for someone who builds a track record on NOI protection, compliance accuracy, and team stability.

job.title: Maintenance Field Tech - Columbia, South Carolina
job.description:
The single-family rental sector has grown fast enough over the past several years that operational infrastructure is now the differentiator. Institutional SFR platforms live or die on how efficiently they turn homes, handle occupied maintenance, and keep residents from churning. The field technician role exists precisely because that work can't be done remotely. Evergreen Residential, a Dallas-based SFR and build-to-rent platform founded in 2021, is building out its Columbia, South Carolina presence and needs a Maintenance Field Technician who can own the on-the-ground work across a scaling residential portfolio.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

This is a mixed-bag field role, and that's what makes it worth understanding before you apply. On any given week, you might complete minor post-renovation punch list repairs on recently turned homes, troubleshoot smart home technology installations, and perform pre-move-in inspections 72 hours ahead of a resident's keys date. You'll also conduct move-out walks with residents, complete occupied maintenance work orders, run HOA violation checks, handle in-person eviction and lockout coordination, and perform recurring occupancy checks. Marketing yard sign placement and removal is also part of the scope.

The KPI review piece matters here. You'll check your progress against performance metrics weekly with the Head of Construction, which means this isn't a role where work disappears into a queue. There's accountability built into the cadence, and you'll need to communicate with residents professionally and promptly on outstanding violations or service issues.

Who Fits This Role

  • At least two years of hands-on residential maintenance experience in a related position
  • Comfortable working in Microsoft Office (Outlook, Excel, Word) and familiar with resident or property management software
  • HVAC certification is preferred and will differentiate your application
  • Self-directed and comfortable operating with ambiguity as the portfolio scales
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, particularly with residents

The smart home troubleshooting piece is worth calling out specifically. SFR platforms at institutional scale are increasingly standardizing smart locks, thermostats, and access systems across their portfolios. Technicians who can diagnose and resolve those issues independently become genuinely valuable, and that skill compounds quickly into a differentiator as more operators adopt connected-home technology at scale. If you've got exposure there already, lead with it.

From a career trajectory standpoint, field technicians who perform well in SFR platforms tend to move into market-level maintenance lead roles or construction coordination as portfolios grow. The reporting relationship to the Head of Construction at Evergreen signals that this company tracks and develops field talent rather than treating the position as purely transactional. For someone two to four years into a maintenance career, that kind of visibility is worth more than the title suggests.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Leasing at a 245-unit property like Willow Creek in Plymouth requires a specific set of skills working simultaneously: sales instincts, organization, and genuine people skills. This role uses all three from the moment the phone rings in the morning to the last tour of a Saturday afternoon.

What This Role Actually Demands

The core skill here is sales, but not the pressure-heavy kind. You're converting phone inquiries into visits, visits into applications, and applications into signed leases. That means listening well, matching prospects to the right unit, and following up with people who went quiet. If you let leads sit without follow-up, occupancy slips. The job rewards consultants who are organized enough to track their pipeline and personable enough to make prospects feel at home before they sign anything.

You'll also handle the administrative side of the leasing cycle. Qualifying applicants, preparing lease documents, walking new residents through their move-in inspection, and later handling move-outs the same way. These aren't glamorous tasks, but they protect the property and the resident relationship. Getting paperwork right matters.

Renewal conversations are part of the job too. You're not just filling vacant units; you're keeping current residents from leaving. That takes a different approach than initial leasing, and consultants who do it well add real value to NOI by reducing turn costs.

Skills That Travel Well

Leasing consultants who perform well in this kind of role tend to move into assistant manager positions within a few years. The combination of sales, resident relations, and lease administration builds a foundation for broader property operations. At a company like Bigos, which has ranked as a Star Tribune Top Workplace twelve times, internal development paths tend to be real rather than theoretical.

The Schedule and Setup

This is a Tuesday through Saturday position. Hours vary slightly by day, with some earlier starts. Weekend availability is a firm requirement, since Saturday is typically a high-traffic day for prospective renters.

Pay runs $17 to $22 per hour depending on experience, with leasing commissions and renewal bonuses on top of base. Benefits start the first of the month after hire.

What Bigos Is Looking For

  • High school diploma or GED
  • One to two years in customer service or sales
  • Prior leasing experience is a plus but not required
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Basic computer literacy: email, web-based tools
  • No active real estate license while in this role
  • Ability to travel occasionally for company meetings and training

Candidates who stand out tend to combine genuine follow-through with organized habits. Plenty of applicants can give a good tour. Fewer consistently follow up with every prospect, track their pipeline, and close renewals without prompting. That's where the difference shows up in occupancy numbers.

job.title: Assistant General Manager- West Ocean (Long Beach, CA)
job.description:
A homeowner calls about a noise complaint, a vendor is waiting at the front desk, and the access control log shows a discrepancy from last night's shift. Before 9 a.m., you've already touched three different parts of this job. That's West Ocean on a typical morning.

The Role

Action Property Management is hiring an Assistant General Manager for West Ocean, a high-rise community in Long Beach, CA. You'll work directly alongside the General Manager to keep daily operations running. That means handling resident communications, supporting front desk and access control staff, and acting as the go-to contact for community information and member services.

This is an on-site, hands-on position. Residents interact with this office constantly, and your responsiveness shapes their experience directly. You'll help train and supervise front-line staff, so you need to be comfortable giving direction and holding people accountable without escalating everything to the GM.

What You Bring

  • Experience in HOA management, hospitality, or a similar resident-facing operations role
  • Strong communication skills, both written and verbal, for working with homeowners and staff
  • Comfort managing multiple priorities without losing track of the details
  • Supervisory experience or clear readiness to step into that responsibility
  • Familiarity with access control systems and building operations is a plus

Action Property Management has operated since 1984 and manages over 300 communities across nine offices in the West. They're the largest privately held HOA management company in the region. West Ocean is the kind of community that reflects that reputation, so they need someone who takes resident service seriously and doesn't need to be reminded twice.

Strong candidates for this role tend to have a hospitality mindset, people who read a situation quickly and respond without waiting for a script. HOA work at a high-rise property involves a lot of small moments that add up to how a building feels to live in. The AGM is central to that.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
The delinquency report hits your inbox Monday morning and three residents are past due. By 10 a.m., you've already made contact, documented the calls, and started the paper trail your Community Manager needs to make a decision. That's the rhythm of this role.

The Work

Havenpark Communities operates more than 100 manufactured home communities across the country, with over 30,000 homesites in the portfolio and active acquisition underway. The Assistant Community Manager in Swartz Creek, MI keeps day-to-day operations moving alongside the Community Manager: resident relations, collections follow-up, leasing support, and work order tracking. You're the first point of contact when something goes sideways, and the person making sure the details don't fall through.

Collections is a real part of this job. Staying on delinquency, keeping records clean, and knowing when to escalate matters. So does leasing: fielding traffic, showing homes, moving prospective residents through the process. And when a resident has a maintenance concern, you're tracking that work order from submission to close, not just forwarding the email.

Occasional travel may be required on a semi-annual or annual basis, likely for company training or regional meetings.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • Experience in property management, manufactured housing, or a resident-facing operations role
  • Comfort handling collections conversations directly, professionally, and with follow-through
  • Organizational habits that hold up under volume: multiple open work orders, active leases, and daily resident requests at once
  • A customer-first approach that doesn't require a script
  • Alignment with the core values Havenpark operates by: Respect, Grit, Collaboration, Stewardship, and Boldness

Manufactured home communities run differently than conventional multifamily.
