Residents often own their homes and lease the land beneath them, which shifts the dynamic of both leasing conversations and collections. The most effective ACMs here understand that distinction and build trust with residents accordingly. That relationship-first mindset, combined with clean administrative habits, is what separates candidates who thrive in this environment from those who struggle with the pace.

Havenpark is in an active growth phase, which means ACMs who perform well have visible paths toward Community Manager roles as new properties come into the portfolio. The skills built here, occupancy management, delinquency tracking, leasing, and resident communication, carry directly into site management and beyond.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
A resident submits a work order at 8 a.m. reporting a leak under the kitchen sink. By 9 a.m., you've already triaged three other requests, assigned your team for the day, and you're on your way to handle it yourself. That's the pace of this role.

PeakMade Real Estate is hiring a Maintenance Supervisor for one of its off-campus student housing communities in Davis, California. This is a working supervisor position. Expect to spend the majority of your time, roughly 60 to 70 percent, doing hands-on repair work alongside your team. The rest goes toward scheduling, vendor oversight, inspections, and coordinating with the Property Manager to keep the asset running efficiently within budget.

Day-to-Day Responsibilities

You'll own the service request queue: prioritizing, assigning, and following up until items are closed. Daily grounds and building inspections keep liability and curb appeal in check. You'll also run the preventative maintenance program, manage shop inventory, maintain OSHA-compliant safety standards, and oversee the hazard communications program. During turn season, you'll direct your team and any outside contractors through make-ready work on vacant units, keeping the process on schedule and inside budget. Unit inspections, key control, and supporting residents through move-in and move-out are all part of the job. For capital projects, you'll work directly with the National Facilities Director to obtain bids.

Repair competencies expected include HVAC, intermediate plumbing, intermediate electrical (where no license is required), major appliances, general carpentry, sheetrock, painting, pool care, roofing, gutters, landscaping, and irrigation. You'll need your own reliable vehicle and basic hand tools.

What You'll Need

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • 2+ years of maintenance supervisory experience; multifamily background strongly preferred
  • EPA Type II certification required; CPO preferred
  • Valid driver's license and current auto insurance
  • Must live within 30 miles of the property
  • Ability to lift up to 50 pounds, work at height, and perform physical tasks in both extreme heat and cold
  • Other licenses or certifications as required by local, state, or federal law

Student housing runs on a tight seasonal calendar. The summer turn between academic years is compressed and high-volume. Supervisors who thrive here are comfortable managing contractor relationships, holding a punch list to standard under time pressure, and adjusting priorities mid-day without losing track of what's still open. If your background is in conventional multifamily, that experience carries well, but the turn intensity in student housing tends to be sharper.

PeakMade offers a benefits package that includes paid parental leave, PTO, 401(k) match, wellness programs, technical training, certification support (HVAC and CPO), and renewal bonuses. Anticipated pay starts at $28.00 per hour, with final compensation based on experience and qualifications.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
The assistant property manager role tends to be where PM careers either accelerate or plateau. The difference usually comes down to whether someone treats it as a support position or a genuine ownership role. At Makowsky Ringel Greenberg's Signature at Schilling Farms in Collierville, Tennessee, this is a full-cycle position carrying real leasing and administrative responsibility, with direct exposure to day-to-day operations across a residential community.

What the Role Actually Covers

You'll own the leasing process from initial traffic contact through move-in, including rent collection, payment entry, and keeping occupancy data current. Service request coordination sits in your lane too, either handling it directly or working alongside maintenance to close out tickets. Daily inspections of the model, common areas, and amenities are part of the rhythm here, as is assisting with vacant unit inspections. When the property manager is out, you step up. That's written into the job, and it's worth taking seriously as preparation rather than just a coverage obligation.

Weekend availability is a real requirement. Collierville's suburban renter traffic skews heavily toward weekend tours, so this isn't a formality in the posting. You'll also need to be mobile on the property, including stairs, and have reliable transportation and a valid license with current insurance.

What MRG Is Looking For

  • One to two years of residential leasing or property management experience
  • Working knowledge of OneSite or Yardi (OneSite preferred)
  • Comfort handling both leasing conversations and administrative tasks in the same shift
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Weekend availability, reliable transportation, valid driver's license and proof of insurance

MRG offers a competitive salary with a bonus and commission component, medical, dental, disability, and other insurance options, a 401(k) with profit-sharing, and paid training. The working environment is described as pleasant, which in this industry is less a given than it sounds.

One thing that separates strong candidates at this level: the ability to shift cleanly between guest card follow-up, a delinquency call, and a maintenance coordination conversation without losing the thread on any of them. That context-switching is the job, and people who are good at it tend to move into property manager seats faster than those who prefer one lane.

job.title: Part-Time Violations Inspector - Brick, NJ
job.description:
You're rolling out on a Kubota utility vehicle at 8 a.m., working through an 804-unit condo community in Brick, cataloguing what you see: an improper satellite dish here, a parking violation there, a fence that doesn't meet the community's architectural standards. By the end of the shift, your notes become the paper trail that keeps the community's rules enforceable and its curb appeal intact.

What the Role Involves

Taylor Management Company, a New Jersey-based community association management firm, is hiring a Part-Time Violations Inspector for one of its larger condominium communities in Brick Township. The schedule runs three days per week, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., and pays $20 per hour. No certification is required to start.

The core of the job is straightforward: walk or drive the property, observe conditions against the community's established rules and regulations, and document what you find with enough accuracy and detail that management can act on it. That documentation function matters more than most candidates expect. A vague inspection report creates ambiguity when violations need to be addressed; a precise one gives the management team what they need to notify residents and track compliance over time.

You'll also flag maintenance and appearance concerns beyond formal violations. A cracked sidewalk, a burned-out light in a common area, debris near a dumpster enclosure: these aren't always rule infractions, but they affect how the community looks and functions, and management needs eyes on them.

What Makes a Strong Candidate

  • Comfortable working outdoors across a large property in varied weather conditions
  • Observant and consistent: the ability to apply the same standard from unit to unit without letting familiarity cause you to overlook things
  • Clear, organized written communication for documenting findings
  • Professional demeanor when residents are present. Inspectors regularly encounter homeowners who want to discuss what you're noting, and how you handle those moments reflects on the management company.

Brick Township's condo communities tend to draw a mix of year-round residents and seasonal owners, which means occupancy patterns shift and absentee ownership is common. An inspector who knows how to document conditions thoroughly on a quiet Tuesday in January gives the management team just as much useful information as one working during peak season when residents are around to flag things themselves.

For candidates considering where a role like this can lead: violations inspection builds familiarity with HOA governing documents, community standards enforcement, and the inspection reporting workflows that community managers rely on daily. It's a natural entry point for anyone interested in moving toward a full association management role over time.

job.title: Administrative Assistant
job.description:
What This Role Actually Covers

Administrative support at a firm like Lincoln Property Company means keeping a commercial real estate team running smoothly across a wide range of operational details. On any given day, you're managing calendars and coordinating meeting logistics, drafting and proofreading correspondence, processing expense reports and purchase orders, and making sure filing systems stay organized and accurate. Onboarding logistics for new team members, office supply management, and data entry into company systems round out the picture. The work is varied, the pace is consistent, and the expectation is that you handle competing priorities without waiting to be told what comes first.

This position is fully in-office in El Segundo, five days a week during standard business hours. If you've worked remotely and prefer that flexibility, this one's probably not the right fit.

What You Bring to the Role

  • A high school diploma or equivalent, minimum
  • At least two years of administrative or clerical experience; commercial real estate exposure is a genuine differentiator here
  • Solid command of Microsoft Office, particularly Word, Excel, and Outlook
  • Clear written and verbal communication, the kind that doesn't need editing before it goes out
  • Strong organizational instincts and real attention to detail
  • The ability to manage a shifting workload independently

Where This Role Can Take You

Administrative roles at large commercial real estate firms are a genuine entry point into the industry. Lincoln manages over 720 million square feet of commercial space across asset types ranging from office and industrial to life science and data centers. Working inside an organization of that scale exposes you to how real estate operations, asset management, and client reporting actually function at an institutional level. Assistants who learn the vocabulary of the business, how leases get structured, how reporting cycles work, how internal teams coordinate across asset types, tend to move into coordinator, analyst, or operations specialist roles faster than those who treat the administrative layer as a holding pattern.

The skills you'll build here, specifically the ability to manage complex scheduling across senior team members, produce clean professional correspondence, and maintain accurate records under pressure, transfer directly into transaction coordination, property management support, and real estate operations roles. Lincoln's stated commitment to mentorship and internal training means the development pathways are real, not just recruiting language.

Compensation for this position is posted in the $65,000 to $75,000 range, with a standard benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, 401(k), and paid time off.

job.title: Community Manager- Tupelo Alley
job.description:
It's 9 a.m. on a Tuesday and you're already triaging: a leasing consultant has a question about a concession, maintenance flagged a unit that won't make the scheduled move-in, and the delinquency report is sitting in your inbox waiting for you to actually look at it. That's the job, and at Tupelo Alley in Portland, MG Properties needs someone who doesn't flinch at that kind of morning.

What This Role Actually Covers

MG Properties has been acquiring, developing, and managing apartment communities across the Western U.S. for over three decades. Tupelo Alley is one of their Portland assets, and they're looking for a Community Manager to run it. That means full operational ownership: budgets, occupancy, marketing, leasing performance, and the team doing all of it. You'll build out and lead your on-site staff, oversee the make-ready process, manage the property's financial performance, and keep the asset moving. This role touches everything from traffic and T-12 review to vendor relationships and resident retention. If you've been managing a property where someone else handled the hard parts, this probably isn't the right fit.

MG Properties also participates in profit sharing, which is worth noting. It means when the portfolio performs, the people running the properties see some of that upside. Combined with monthly and performance-based bonuses, the comp structure is tied to outcomes, not just hours logged.

What They're Looking For

  • Recent, hands-on experience managing an apartment community. Not five years ago. Recent.
  • Demonstrated supervisory experience. You've hired, coached, and when necessary, made hard calls about staff.
  • Yardi experience is preferred. If you've been running a property without it, be ready to get up to speed quickly.
  • Real operational range: budget management, marketing, sales, leasing metrics. You should be comfortable in all of these, not just one or two.
  • Valid driver's license and proof of insurance.

Portland is a market with real regulatory complexity around evictions and tenant protections, and that context matters here. Community Managers operating in Oregon need to stay current on local landlord-tenant law, and operators who treat that as an afterthought tend to create expensive problems. If you've been managing in the Portland metro already, that familiarity with the local compliance environment is a genuine advantage.

MG Properties offers medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer match, paid holidays, PTO, sick time, and rental discounts. Background check and drug screening required prior to hire.

job.title: Market Property Manager II
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role covers two Milton, MA properties: 4 Franklin and Residences at Quarry Hills. Day to day, you're the operational anchor for both sites. That means your mornings might start with a delinquency report and a call to legal, and your afternoons might shift to reviewing a capex proposal or walking a unit with a maintenance lead. The work moves fast and the scope is genuinely broad.

You'll supervise administrative, leasing, and maintenance staff across the properties, which means hiring decisions land on your desk, as do performance conversations when someone isn't meeting the mark. You'll work directly with owner representatives on property strategy and performance goals, so comfort presenting to stakeholders matters as much as comfort on the floor.

On the financial side, you'll ensure timely rent collection and authorize corrective or legal action when accounts fall behind. You'll also develop a working knowledge of the competitive landscape in the South Shore and Greater Boston markets, feeding recommendations to the Senior Property Manager on rental rates, renewal pricing, and marketing direction. Annual property audits, internal reviews, and external inspections are also part of the role's rhythm.

One detail worth noting: affordable housing proficiency is listed as a hard requirement. If you've worked with affordable programs and understand their compliance layer, that background will matter here more than general market experience alone.

What You Bring

  • At least five years of property management experience, with time spent actually leading a team
  • Demonstrated experience in affordable housing programs and their compliance requirements
  • Fluency in Yardi and Microsoft Office
  • Genuine comfort with budgets: reading them, defending them, and flagging problems early
  • Experience managing vendor contracts and monitoring capital improvements
  • The ability to hire and develop staff, not just manage them

The strongest candidates will bring a track record of proactive communication with ownership. Knowing when to escalate and how to frame a problem before it becomes a crisis is the kind of judgment that separates effective property managers from reactive ones in this type of role.

The Team and the Company

John M. Corcoran and Company has been operating in New England real estate since 1951. It's a firm with real tenure on its team, the kind of place where people tend to stay. That kind of retention usually signals something about internal culture, and it also means institutional knowledge runs deep. You'll be working alongside people who know these properties and this company well, which is both a resource and a standard to meet.

The schedule is Monday through Friday, 9 to 5. The pay range runs from roughly $73,500 to $98,800 depending on experience, with a $2,500 sign-on bonus. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, life insurance, PTO, and a 401k with company match.

If you've been managing properties where your input on strategy rarely made it past your supervisor's inbox, this role offers a different dynamic. The connection to owner representatives is direct, and the expectation is that you'll come with opinions, not just reports.

job.title: Floating Leasing Specialist
job.description:
Hillpointe builds and operates market-rate workforce housing across the Sun Belt, and they do it with a fully integrated model: land acquisition, construction, asset management, and leasing all run in-house. That context matters for this role. When you support a community as a Floating Leasing Specialist, you're working inside a system where decisions happen quickly and the people around you understand every phase of a property's life cycle.

The Skills This Role Runs On

Leasing is the core skill in play here, but the floating structure puts a premium on adaptability in a way that a site-based leasing position does not. You'll step into communities during lease-ups, high-traffic periods, and team transitions, which means you need to read a room quickly. Each property has its own prospect pool, its own tour path, its own pace. Strong candidates already know how to conduct a compelling tour, match community features to a prospect's stated needs, and follow up across phone, text, and email without letting leads go cold. You bring those habits with you from day one.

Customer service instincts matter just as much as leasing technique here. Prospects often arrive with real questions and real concerns. Your ability to listen, address objections honestly, and keep the conversation moving toward a decision is what converts traffic into signed leases.

What the Role Builds

Because you'll move across multiple communities, you'll develop a portfolio-level view of leasing performance that most site-based consultants take years to acquire. You'll see what concessions are working in one market, how a lease-up community's traffic patterns differ from a stabilized asset, and how to calibrate your pitch for different price points and renter profiles. That breadth is genuinely useful if your career path leads toward leasing manager, property manager, or regional leasing roles.

The role also sharpens your instincts around fair housing compliance, since you'll encounter diverse prospects across multiple sites and need to apply consistent standards regardless of location or team culture.

What to Know Before You Apply

  • Frequent travel between properties is a core requirement, not an occasional ask. A valid driver's license and a flexible schedule including weekends are necessary.
  • Temporary or permanent relocation may be required based on where Hillpointe needs coverage.
  • Free rent at an assigned Hillpointe community is part of the compensation structure, subject to company policy.
  • Prior experience in leasing, hospitality, or sales is preferred, though strong customer-facing experience in adjacent fields is considered.
  • A high school diploma or equivalent is required.

What separates strong candidates in a floating role is the ability to get up to speed without hand-holding. You won't always have a seasoned team member walking you through the property. The people who thrive here are the ones who can walk into a new leasing office on a Monday morning, learn the floor plan, review the availability, and be ready to tour by noon.

job.title: Leasing Consultant - Madamore Apartments
job.description:
A prospective resident walks in on a Tuesday afternoon, a little uncertain, maybe comparing three communities across the city. You're the first person they meet, and the impression you leave matters more than any floor plan or amenity photo ever could. That's the core of this role.

The Position at Madamore Apartments

Ackermann Group, a Midwest real estate and property management company with roots going back to 1938, is adding a full-time Leasing Consultant to the team at Madamore Apartments, a 312-unit community in Cincinnati. The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, with rotating Saturdays from 9 to 4.

Day to day, you'll be the primary point of contact for both prospective and current residents. That means handling inbound inquiries by phone, email, and in person, converting those conversations into tours, and guiding interested prospects through to a signed lease. You'll complete all the administrative work that comes with leasing: guest cards, lease preparation, move-in documentation, fair housing compliance records. Accuracy and timeliness matter here because errors in that paperwork have real consequences.

The role extends beyond the leasing office. You'll walk units and community common areas regularly to confirm they're showing well, handle small corrective tasks yourself, and loop in the maintenance team when something needs their attention. Being comfortable on your feet, observant about your surroundings, and communicative with colleagues you don't always share a desk with makes a real difference at a community this size.

Ackermann expects this person to own the resident experience, not just the leasing funnel. That includes anticipating issues before residents escalate them, documenting service requests clearly, and participating in resident events and community outreach. If you've worked in a customer-facing role and found that you genuinely enjoy problem-solving for people, this structure will feel natural.

What Makes a Strong Candidate Here

Qualified applicants will have:

  • A high school diploma or equivalent
  • Prior customer service experience (required)
  • Leasing or sales experience (strongly preferred)
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and property management software; Yardi Voyager, Rent Café, and CRM experience are a plus
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to build rapport quickly
  • Comfort working in a team environment alongside a Community Manager and maintenance staff

The candidates who tend to stand out in roles like this aren't necessarily the ones with the most leasing experience. They're the ones who track their follow-ups without being reminded, notice when a model unit needs attention before a tour, and communicate problems to management clearly rather than letting things drift. CRM discipline and genuine curiosity about what a prospect actually needs tend to separate good leasing consultants from average ones at the occupancy level.

Ackermann offers competitive hourly pay plus commission on new and renewed leases, health benefits, 401k with company match, paid time off (including your birthday), an employee rent discount at any Ackermann community, and career development support. Cincinnati's multifamily market is competitive enough that a consultant who learns to read local traffic patterns and adjust their pitch accordingly builds skills that transfer well across any future property they work at.

job.title: Leasing Consultant - Lincoln Park
job.description:
Leasing Consultants at growing Chicago operators wear a lot of hats. On a given Thursday morning, you might be following up on weekend traffic leads, walking a vacant unit with your punch list notes to flag touch-ups for maintenance, and then turning around to host a tour for a prospect who found the property on Google. That rhythm, sales-forward but grounded in daily operations, is exactly what this role at Reside Living looks like.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

Reside Living manages roughly 3,000 apartments across Chicago's neighborhoods, and this position is tied to their Lincoln Park portfolio. Your core job is keeping occupancy healthy: converting leads to signed leases, following up consistently through the CRM, and making sure prospects feel genuinely welcomed from the first call to move-in day. You'll also keep a pulse on the local market, run monthly audits of online marketing presence, and bring ideas to your Property Manager when you spot opportunities to improve traffic or resident satisfaction.

Day-to-day responsibilities include:

  • Responding to prospect inquiries via phone, text, and email, and tracking all communication in the CRM (Yardi experience is a plus)
  • Conducting tours and guiding prospects through the leasing process in compliance with fair housing, ADA, and all applicable state and federal regulations
  • Physically inspecting vacant units and common areas, flagging service needs to maintenance staff
  • Preparing daily and weekly leasing reports
  • Helping plan and host resident events that support retention

The schedule runs Thursday through Monday, 9 AM to 5 PM, with Tuesdays and Wednesdays off. That's worth noting upfront because it's a real differentiator for some candidates and a dealbreaker for others.

Compensation and What Comes With It

The base is $22.00 per hour, and with commission and quarterly bonuses, total compensation typically lands between $65,000 and $75,000 annually. Beyond that, Reside Living offers medical, dental, and life insurance, a 401(k) match, paid time off, a commuter benefit, and a 25% monthly apartment discount. There's also a $100 monthly student loan assistance contribution, a $50 monthly phone stipend (you'll use your personal cell), and a $1,000 career apparel allowance for new hires.

Who Tends to Succeed Here

At least one year of leasing experience is required. Strong candidates come in already comfortable with the full leasing cycle and fluent enough with Microsoft Office to handle reporting without hand-holding. What separates good consultants from great ones in a role like this is honestly the follow-through. Generating traffic is one thing; tracking every prospect touchpoint, staying organized across a busy weekend of tours, and still bringing a genuine warmth to the hundredth showing of the month is a harder skill to screen for. If you find the sales side energizing rather than draining, and you care about the product you're representing, you'll fit the culture Reside Living describes.

Reside Living emphasizes an open environment with room to grow. For consultants who perform well, the natural path forward in property management runs toward Assistant Property Manager and eventually Property Manager roles, particularly within a portfolio that's still expanding.

job.title: Groundskeeper at Cason Estates Apartments
job.description:
It's 7 a.m. at Cason Estates and the parking lot already needs a sweep before the first resident heads to work. That's where you come in, before most of the office staff has even logged on.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Cottonwood Residential is hiring a Groundskeeper for Cason Estates Apartments in Murfreesboro, Tennessee. The role covers the physical upkeep of the property grounds and common areas. Day to day, that means trash and litter removal throughout the community, sweeping and pressure washing walkways and building exteriors, basic gardening and weed control, and cleaning windows and common area furniture. You'll also handle general maintenance tasks tied to grounds and building upkeep as they come up. It's a full-body job. Expect long stretches on your feet, regular lifting up to 50 lbs, and working across varied terrain, including stairs, ladders, and scaffold access when needed.

On-call availability for nights, weekends, and company events is part of the deal. Curb appeal doesn't take days off, and a property's first impression lives or dies in the grounds.

One thing worth noting for candidates who haven't worked multifamily before: groundskeeping on a residential community is different from landscaping a commercial site. Residents notice everything. A cigarette butt near the mailboxes, overgrown beds along a building entry, a pressure-washed walkway that dried with streaks. The work is visible in a way that directly affects how residents feel about where they live, and that shows up in retention. Good groundskeepers understand that without being told.

What Cottonwood Is Looking For

  • Ability to read, write, and speak English well enough to process company paperwork and follow safety and operating procedures
  • Physical capability to lift, carry, and reposition items up to 50 lbs
  • Comfort working on your feet for extended periods, on varied terrain, in multiple physical positions (kneeling, crouching, climbing)
  • Availability for on-call shifts including nights, weekends, and company events

Cottonwood Residential offers competitive pay with full health, dental, vision, life, and disability benefits available within the first 30 days. The 401k and HSA both carry a company match. First-year PTO comes in at 120 hours (three weeks) plus 10.5 paid holidays. That's a solid benefits package for a grounds role, and it's worth saying plainly.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
A Saturday morning at a multifamily community in Daytona Beach looks different than most people expect. You're fielding a renewal question from a long-term resident, checking in with maintenance on the make-ready schedule, and reviewing delinquency notes before the Community Manager arrives. By 10 a.m., the leasing team needs a quick coaching moment. That's the pace this role runs at, and for the right person, it's genuinely energizing.

What You'll Be Doing

Waypoint Management Services is hiring an Assistant Community Manager at their Daytona Beach property. The role puts you at the center of daily operations, working closely with the Community Manager on everything from leasing performance and staff development to financial oversight and resident relations. You'll monitor occupancy and recommend pricing adjustments based on market surveys. You'll track renewals and make-ready schedules. You'll help manage rent collection, delinquencies, and evictions when it comes to that, and you'll make sure lease files and rent roll records stay accurate.

On the leasing side, you'll support the team's training and operational consistency, and contribute to marketing and sales strategies aimed at attracting and retaining residents. Part of that means staying current on what competitors are doing nearby, which in a coastal Florida market like Daytona Beach is genuinely useful work because the rental landscape shifts with seasonal traffic and tourism cycles. Weekend availability is part of the rotation here, so that's worth factoring into your decision.

What You'll Bring

  • At least two years of experience in leasing, sales, or a hospitality setting where managing people and expectations was a daily reality
  • Comfort with financial reporting, delinquency tracking, and the administrative side of community operations
  • Strong communication skills across residents, vendors, and team members
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office; Yardi experience is a real plus here
  • A valid driver's license and willingness to work weekend rotations
  • A high school diploma or equivalent; additional education is welcome but not required

The candidates who tend to thrive in ACM roles are the ones who've actually worked the leasing floor long enough to coach others through it. Financial fluency helps, but it's the ability to hold a team accountable while still being the person residents trust that separates a strong assistant manager from one who's just performing the job title.

Waypoint offers monthly leasing and renewal bonuses, an employee housing discount, medical, dental, and vision coverage starting on day one, 120 hours of PTO in the first year, two floating days annually, a 401(k) with company match, commuter benefits, and an employee referral program. Professional development training is also part of the package, which matters if you're thinking about where this role leads. Assistant Community Manager experience builds the financial and operational foundation that most Community Manager roles require, and companies that invest in training tend to promote from within.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor ($2,000 hiring bonus)
job.description:
A unit goes down on a Friday afternoon: AC out, resident escalating, and two techs waiting on direction. That's the moment this role earns its pay. As Maintenance Supervisor at BAM Companies in Waukee, Iowa, you're the person who keeps that situation from turning into a weekend crisis.

What the Job Looks Like

BAM Companies, founded in 2010, manages residential properties with an emphasis on team culture and operational quality. In this role, you supervise and develop the on-site maintenance team while taking ownership of HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and general property upkeep. That means hands-on work alongside your crew, not just directing from the office.

Preventative maintenance is a core part of the job. You'll schedule and oversee regular inspections designed to catch problems before they become work orders. You'll also manage supply purchasing and keep operations within budget, so an eye for cost-effective decisions matters as much as mechanical know-how.

Curb appeal and common areas fall under your watch too. Residents notice the details, and your team sets the standard for how the property looks and functions day to day.

A $2,000 hiring bonus comes with this position, and pay runs between $27 and $32 per hour depending on experience.

What BAM Is Looking For

  • 2 to 3 years of property maintenance experience; supervisory background is a plus
  • EPA Type II or Universal Certification (required)
  • Valid driver's license and a reliable vehicle
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills
  • Genuine ability to coach and develop technicians, not just assign tasks

The candidates who stand out here aren't just technically solid. They know how to read a team: when someone needs more training, when morale needs attention, when a process needs tightening. A good supervisor at a property like this raises the skill level of everyone around them over time, and that's exactly what BAM is hiring for.

Benefits include medical, dental, vision, and life insurance, along with 15.5 paid holidays plus PTO that kicks in after 90 days. BAM also offers housing discounts at their properties for employees who want to live on-site or nearby.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Founders Village
job.description:
Founders Village is a residential community in Williamsburg, VA managed by LivCor. This maintenance technician role covers the full range of day-to-day upkeep: work orders, make-readies, emergency response, and keeping amenity spaces functional and presentable.

What You'll Actually Do

Most of your time splits between active work orders and unit turns. You'll diagnose and repair appliances, plumbing, HVAC systems, electrical issues, gates, and pool equipment. When a unit vacates, you run through the punch list to get it rent-ready on schedule. You'll also handle on-call rotation, which means responding to urgent repairs evenings, weekends, and holidays when needed.

Beyond wrench-turning, you'll log service requests, track vendor work, keep the shop stocked and organized, and communicate directly with residents when addressing complaints or delivering notices. This role requires solid interpersonal skills, not just technical ones.

What You Bring

  • 1 to 3 years of maintenance experience, preferably in apartment communities
  • Type II or Universal refrigeration certification (required within 90 days of hire if not already held)
  • Valid driver's license and clean driving record
  • Physical capability to lift 50 lbs independently, move appliances and equipment up to 300+ lbs on wheels, and work comfortably at heights up to 40 feet
  • Comfort working in varied conditions across both interior units and exterior common areas

Compensation and Benefits

Pay runs $22 to $25 per hour depending on your experience relative to the role's requirements. Benefits include a generous PTO program, 13 paid holidays plus 3 floating holidays and a paid volunteer day, comprehensive medical coverage, company-paid dental and vision, a 401k with strong employer match, an associate apartment discount, and tuition and certification assistance. Mental health and wellness programs are also company-paid.

One thing worth knowing going in: on-call rotations are a real part of this job. If a water heater fails at 9 PM or a resident is locked out due to a gate malfunction on a holiday weekend, you're expected to respond. Technicians who thrive here treat that responsibility as part of the role, not an exception to it. The support structure, pay, and benefits reflect that expectation.

job.title: Bilingual Screening & Applications Specialist - Sandy Springs, GA
job.description:
Cortland runs one of the largest multifamily portfolios in the country, and their centralized contact center in Sandy Springs handles application volume that most on-site teams never see. This Bilingual Screening and Applications Specialist role sits inside that contact center, focused on one specific stretch of the leasing cycle: the period between application submission and move-in.

What You'll Actually Do

Your day revolves around applications. You'll review them for completeness, verify supporting documentation, and keep applicants informed as they move through the process. A good portion of your time is spent on inbound communication, calls, emails, and chat, answering questions, chasing missing documents, and keeping multiple files moving at once. When an applicant is confused, frustrated, or escalating, you're the one who steadies the conversation.

You'll work inside platforms like RealPage, OneSite, and Funnel, so comfort with property management software matters. Fair Housing compliance isn't an afterthought here. It's built into every interaction.

Spanish fluency is a genuine requirement for this role, not a nice-to-have. A meaningful portion of applicants communicate primarily in Spanish, and you'll handle those conversations end to end without escalating to a translator.

What You Bring

  • At least two years of customer service experience, preferably in a high-volume contact center or multifamily setting
  • Bilingual fluency in English and Spanish (spoken and written)
  • Hands-on experience with RealPage, OneSite, or Funnel is a strong differentiator
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Demonstrated ability to handle confidential applicant information with care
  • Strong organizational skills and comfort managing competing priorities without losing accuracy
  • Availability for weekends and extended hours when volume requires it

Context Worth Knowing

Centralized leasing operations are expanding across institutional multifamily ownership, partly to standardize the applicant experience and partly to take pressure off on-site teams. Working inside Cortland's contact center puts you at the center of that model. You'll process high application volume across multiple properties rather than supporting a single community, which means the pace is real and the variety of situations is broad.

Candidates who perform well here tend to have one specific skill that separates them from others: they can maintain accuracy on paperwork while simultaneously managing a live conversation with an anxious applicant. Both halves matter equally. If your background is heavy on customer interaction but light on document review, or the reverse, this role will push you to strengthen the weaker side quickly.

job.title: Affordable Housing Compliance Specialist
job.description:
A new resident file lands in your queue at 9 a.m. The application looks straightforward until you notice an income discrepancy that could put the property's LIHTC compliance at risk. You flag it, document your reasoning, and loop in the site team before noon. That kind of catch, repeated across a portfolio, is what this role is actually about.

The Work

Asset Living, one of the country's largest third-party management firms, is hiring a Compliance Specialist to support its affordable housing portfolio. This is a file-review and regulatory oversight role with real stakes. You'll evaluate resident applications and existing tenant files for eligibility under applicable affordable housing regulations, with a turnaround standard of 24 hours from receipt. Speed matters, but accuracy matters more.

Beyond the day-to-day review work, you'll track changes in LIHTC requirements and help implement updates to internal procedures as regulations shift. When outside entities conduct tax credit reviews, you'll be an active participant, which means you need to be comfortable fielding questions and presenting documentation under scrutiny. Annual TDHCA training attendance is part of the job, and if you don't already hold the Housing Credit Certified Professional (HCCP) designation, you'll be expected to pursue it and pass the exam within your first two years.

Travel runs approximately 50% of the time. That's a meaningful commitment. Expect property visits, conferences, and training sessions spread across the year, particularly if the portfolio spans multiple states or Texas markets.

Who Fits This Role Well

  • Experience reviewing LIHTC or HUD resident files, with working knowledge of income qualification and eligibility standards
  • Hands-on experience with RealPage OneSite Tax Credit module (or comparable affordable housing compliance software)
  • HCCP designation already earned, or a clear willingness to pursue it on a defined timeline
  • Strong written communication skills, since your file notes and compliance decisions need to hold up under external audit review
  • Comfort working semi-independently, given the remote and travel components of this hybrid role

HUD program knowledge is a plus, though not a hard requirement. What separates strong candidates from adequate ones in this kind of role is the ability to stay current on regulatory updates without waiting for someone to hand them the information. LIHTC rules shift at both the federal and state level, and a specialist who proactively monitors those changes protects the portfolio in ways that reactive compliance work simply cannot.

If you've built a career in affordable housing compliance and want to bring that expertise to a firm operating at scale, this position offers genuine scope and a defined credentialing path if you're still building toward HCCP.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
It's 7:45 AM on a Monday and your on-call phone already logged two emergency calls over the weekend. Before the leasing office opens, you're walking units, confirming your team's work order queue, and coordinating a vendor for a scope of work that came in Friday afternoon. That's the rhythm here.

The Role

Weinstein Properties, a family-owned operator with more than 70 years in the business and over 60 apartment communities across the Southeast and Mid-Atlantic, is hiring a Maintenance Supervisor for their Cedar Park area communities outside Austin. This is a hands-on position where you'll both lead the service team and work alongside them. The expectation is that you're turning wrenches as often as you're assigning work orders.

Your team handles the full range of in-house repairs: HVAC, plumbing, electrical, pool, carpentry, drywall, appliances, and exterior structural. You'll diagnose issues, complete repairs, coordinate vendor work, and keep turns moving efficiently. A slow make-ready process affects occupancy, and occupancy affects everything downstream. Weinstein owns and manages all its properties in-house, so there's no third-party management layer between the field team and ownership decisions. That structure tends to produce faster approvals and cleaner accountability.

Standard schedule runs Monday through Friday, 8 to 5. On-call rotation is shared with teammates, and there's a bonus attached when you carry the on-call phone.

What Qualifies You

  • Minimum 4 years of trade experience across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and general building systems
  • At least 1 year of supervisory, lead, or assistant maintenance experience in apartment communities specifically
  • EPA/CFC certification required (Type I and II, or Universal)
  • Comfortable using property management or work order software to assign tasks, schedule turns, order supplies, and communicate with the office team
  • Valid driver's license, reliable transportation, and your own tools
  • Background check and DMV review required

Compensation is experience-based with quarterly and annual bonus opportunities. Benefits include health, dental, and vision insurance, 401k with company match, PTO, paid holidays, birthday time off, an Employee Assistance Program, and a rent discount.

One thing that separates strong candidates in this role: the ability to read a unit quickly and triage accurately. Supervisors who know the difference between a repair that can wait for a vendor and one that needs to be done today keep turn times tight and keep residents from escalating. That skill is harder to teach than most technical trades, and Weinstein's hands-on culture means you'll be tested on it regularly.

job.title: Community Manager - Artesia Apartments
job.description:
Community Manager roles at Western U.S. operators like MG Properties tend to run closer to full P&L ownership than people expect from the title. You're not just supervising leasing staff. You're accountable for the budget, the team, the physical asset, and the revenue performance, all at once.

What the Role Covers

Artesia Apartments in Everett, WA needs a Community Manager who can handle the operational breadth that comes with a multifamily property at this level. That means building and developing your on-site team, keeping occupancy and delinquency numbers where they need to be, executing the marketing strategy, and holding the budget line month to month. MG Properties has been in the acquisition, development, and management business across the Western U.S. for over 30 years, so there's an established operational framework behind you, but you're still expected to run your property.

Yardi is the platform of record here, and comfort with it matters. Candidates without recent, hands-on experience managing an apartment community won't be well-positioned for this one. The posting is explicit about that, and it's not a placeholder requirement.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • Demonstrated supervisory experience with a track record of developing leasing and maintenance staff
  • Budget management experience: building it, defending it, and adjusting when actuals drift
  • Working knowledge of Yardi (preferred, not optional in practice)
  • Marketing experience relevant to driving traffic and closing leases
  • Valid driver's license and proof of insurance

The candidates who tend to thrive in this kind of role are the ones who can read a T-12 and spot the story in it, keep NOI moving in the right direction without letting the physical asset slip, and coach a leasing consultant through a tough month without micromanaging them. The ones who struggle usually have strength in one area, either operations or people, but not both.

Compensation and Growth

Base salary runs $83,000 to $85,000 annually depending on experience, with monthly and performance-based incentive bonuses on top of that. MG Properties also offers company profit sharing, a 401(k) with employer match, full medical, dental, and vision coverage, and rental discounts. PTO starts at 10 days per year, plus 10 paid holidays, 2 personal days, and 52 hours of paid sick time.

Everett's multifamily market sits in a submarked that's seen consistent renter demand driven by its proximity to Seattle and a relatively more affordable cost of living. That context matters operationally: traffic sources, concession strategy, and renewal retention all look a little different here than they do in a downtown Seattle high-rise. A Community Manager who understands that dynamic will move faster than one who's treating it like a generic lease-up.

For the right operator, a well-run community at a company like MG Properties tends to open doors toward regional or portfolio-level roles. They promote from within where performance supports it, which is worth noting if that trajectory is on your radar.

job.title: Leasing Consultant (The Dean)
job.description:
Where People Skills Drive Property Performance

Leasing at a well-run apartment community draws on a specific combination of abilities: reading people quickly, staying organized under volume, and knowing when to close. At The Dean in Mountain View, Prometheus Real Estate Group puts all three of those skills to work daily. This is an entry point into residential property management that trains you across leasing, customer relations, and community operations at the same time.

Mountain View sits in one of the most competitive rental corridors in the Bay Area. Proximity to major tech employers keeps traffic consistent, but it also raises resident expectations. People touring here have options, and they know it. Your ability to create a genuine connection during the leasing experience carries real weight in an environment where occupancy is earned, not assumed.

What the Day-to-Day Actually Requires

Prometheus uses the title Neighbor Ambassador rather than Leasing Consultant, and that distinction reflects how the role is structured. You're not just processing applications. You're guiding prospective residents through the full decision process, building comfort and trust before they ever sign. Once residents move in, you remain a point of contact. That continuity is part of what keeps a community's reputation intact.

On the administrative side, you'll prepare rental agreements, run market surveys, produce property reports, and manage apartment advertising. These tasks build the operational foundation that makes everything else run smoothly. Strong candidates treat the paperwork side of leasing with the same attention they bring to a prospect tour, because inaccurate or delayed admin work creates real downstream problems for the team.

Weekend availability is a firm requirement. That's when traffic peaks, which means it's also when your leasing skills matter most. Your regular days off fall during the week in exchange.

What Sets Strong Candidates Apart

Prometheus hires across industries, so prior property management experience isn't required. What does matter is a demonstrated track record in customer-facing roles where you had to manage multiple priorities, stay personable under pressure, and represent a brand consistently. Sales instincts help, but coachability and self-direction tend to predict success here more than raw sales experience.

This role often leads to a Senior Leasing or Assistant Manager track for people who develop their administrative fluency alongside their leasing performance. The companies that invest in both paths tend to promote from within, and Prometheus's compensation structure, which includes per-lease incentives, semi-annual bonuses, and occupancy contests, is structured to reward that development in real time.

  • Hourly rate of $25.00 to $26.25, plus a $200 incentive per lease signed
  • Weekend shift premium pay on top of base hourly rate
  • Discretionary semi-annual bonus plan
  • Company-paid medical, vision, and dental coverage including eligible dependents
  • 401(k) with employer matching
  • Tenure-based housing discounts and tuition reimbursement
  • 12 paid holidays including your birthday, plus 9 sick days annually

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
The Community Manager role at a Southeast-focused multifamily company carries real weight. You're not just running day-to-day operations at a single property. You're the person ownership, residents, and your own team all look to when performance slips, a lease-up stalls, or a vendor drops the ball. Hawthorne Residential Partners operates over 50 multifamily communities and has built a reputation around service culture, which means this position asks you to lead both the business and the people simultaneously.

What the Role Demands

This is a full-cycle community management position covering financial oversight, leasing, team leadership, and resident relations. You'll own the budget, track delinquency, manage deposit accounting, and pull reporting through Yardi. On the leasing side, you'll guide your team on traffic conversion, renewals, and pricing strategy to protect occupancy. You'll also jump in on tours and prospect follow-up when the volume calls for it.

Vendor management and property inspections are part of your weekly rhythm. So is partnering with maintenance on work orders and preventive care to protect curb appeal and reduce costly turns. You'll hold weekly team meetings, handle escalated resident concerns, and manage the community's online reputation by responding to reviews and keeping communication consistent with ownership and regional leadership.

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, with Saturdays from 10 to 4, and one weekday off each week. Resident events and community needs can pull you in outside standard hours, so flexibility is part of the job.

What You Bring vs. What You Build Here

Hawthorne is looking for candidates with at least two years of multifamily experience, including time as a Leasing Consultant and Assistant Community Manager. Six months of direct community manager experience is strongly preferred. Yardi and Knock familiarity will make your first 90 days much smoother. A CAM, CAPS, or real estate license is a plus but not a hard requirement.

The skills this role builds are worth naming clearly. Managing a full P&L, coaching a mixed office and maintenance team, and owning occupancy outcomes develops the operational fluency that regional management requires. Hawthorne runs a formal Career Path Program with a stated goal of promoting community managers into regional roles, so this isn't a lateral move disguised as an opportunity. The infrastructure for growth is genuinely in place.

What Separates Strong Candidates

The managers who perform well in this type of role tend to share a few traits that go beyond the basics:

  • They can read a T-12 and connect the numbers to operational decisions, not just report what's on the page
  • They hold their teams accountable without losing the trust that makes daily coaching work
  • They respond to a difficult resident situation with the same professionalism they'd bring to an ownership call
  • They treat retention with the same urgency as new leasing, understanding that a renewal saved is a turn avoided

If you've grown through the leasing and assistant manager levels and you're ready to own the full operation, this is the kind of platform that rewards that progression with real commission upside and a clear path forward.

job.title: Traveling Leasing Manager
job.description:
Leasing is a skill set that compounds. The fundamentals you build closing a lease at one property, reading what a prospect needs mid-tour, recovering a wavering applicant through follow-up, transfer cleanly to assistant manager work, community manager work, and beyond. This role at Redstone Residential is structured to accelerate that compounding.

What This Role Actually Builds

As a Traveling Leasing Manager, you'll move between Redstone's apartment communities across the Salt Lake City area, stepping in where leasing support is needed and taking direct ownership of occupancy performance at each stop. That variety is the point. Most leasing consultants spend a year or two at a single property, absorbing one team's habits and one property's traffic patterns. You'll move faster than that. You'll see how different sites handle lead follow-up, how renewal conversations change depending on the resident base, and how Entrata gets used across communities with different workflows. That cross-property exposure is genuinely hard to replicate in a stationary role.

The core leasing skills you'll sharpen here include giving tours that convert, managing your own pipeline of prospects through calls, texts, and emails, and closing on applications with confidence. You'll also work on renewals, reaching out ahead of lease expirations and making the case for residents to stay. On top of that, Redstone expects this person to bring a creative side, producing social media content and contributing marketing ideas that drive traffic to the properties you're supporting.

Skills This Role Requires (And Rewards)

  • Sales instinct and comfort asking for the application or the lease directly
  • Strong self-management, since you'll often be the one setting your own daily leasing targets and tracking your own progress
  • Adaptability across team cultures and property types within the same metro
  • Comfort with social media content creation, specifically Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, and Canva
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office and the ability to pick up Entrata quickly
  • Reliable transportation throughout the Salt Lake City area
  • Prior experience in leasing, sales, hospitality, or customer service (preferred, not required)

Where This Role Leads at Redstone

Redstone manages more than 38,000 beds across 20 states as one of the largest third-party student housing operators in the country, and their conventional portfolio is growing alongside that. Size matters here because it means internal mobility is real. A strong Traveling Leasing Manager who demonstrates consistent occupancy performance and the ability to work across teams is positioned well to step into a permanent Leasing Manager role, and from there into Assistant Community Manager work. The traveling structure itself signals what the company values: people who can read a new environment quickly, identify where to focus, and execute without waiting to be managed closely.

What separates candidates who thrive in this role from those who struggle is self-direction. You won't have a single manager watching your daily numbers at every property. The expectation is that you show up, assess what the community needs most, and move. If you've worked in leasing before and found yourself bored once a property stabilized, this structure solves that problem. The work changes before the repetition sets in.

Compensation is $22.00 per hour. Benefits include health, vision, and dental insurance, 15 days of PTO, 10 paid holidays, paid parental leave, a 401(k) with up to 6% matching, short-term disability, and a continued education program.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager, Jefferson Arbors at Broadlands
job.description:
Skills This Role Runs On

The Assistant Community Manager position at Jefferson Arbors at Broadlands calls on a specific blend of financial discipline, relationship management, and operational awareness. This isn't a leasing-only role. The bookkeeping responsibilities sit at the center of the job: tracking collections, keeping bad debt below budgeted thresholds, and managing the financial side of day-to-day operations. If you're comfortable reading delinquency reports and acting on them before they become a problem, that skillset transfers directly here.

On the resident side, the work is equally demanding. Renewal management requires reading your residents before they're already gone. Strong candidates in this type of role treat renewals the way a leasing team treats traffic: proactively, with a system, not just a response to a notice-to-vacate. Jefferson Arbors is a 240-unit garden-style community in Ashburn, and Loudoun County's rental market has historically maintained solid occupancy due to the area's tech and federal contractor employment base. That context matters because residents here often have choices. Retention strategy at a community like this needs to be genuine, not just automated renewal offers.

What You'll Be Responsible For

Day to day, you'll support the Community Manager across all phases of on-site operations while owning specific functions outright. Collections follow-through, renewal outreach, resident communication, and property inspections all fall within your scope. You'll also manage the property's social media presence across platforms including Facebook and Twitter, handle escalated resident concerns, and plan resident events within budget. RealPage/OneSite experience is preferred, which signals the property is already working within a structured platform environment. Familiarity with that system speeds up your contribution on the financial and leasing reporting side considerably.

  • Minimum two years of property management experience required
  • High school diploma required; college degree preferred
  • RealPage/OneSite experience preferred
  • Ability to lift up to 15 pounds occasionally; regular property walks required
  • In-office, on-site position

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

Jefferson Apartment Group operates across acquisition, development, and third-party management, which means there's genuine room to grow within the organization if you perform. The ACM role at a 240-unit community is a well-established stepping stone toward a Community Manager position, and companies structured like JAG tend to promote from within when they have capable people ready. What gets you there faster is being the person who closes the loop: on delinquency before month-end, on renewals before the 60-day window closes, on resident concerns before they hit Google reviews. The coordinative piece matters too. You'll lead the on-site team in the Community Manager's absence, which means the soft skill of keeping a small team aligned on leasing and operational goals is just as important as the bookkeeping precision.

Compensation for this role is in the $25 to $27 per hour range, with performance-based bonus potential and a full benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, and potential rental discounts for eligible employees.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
It's mid-month, the delinquency report is due, a prospective resident is waiting at the front desk, and the Community Manager just called out sick. That's Tuesday at a tax-credit community. If that scenario sounds manageable rather than alarming, this role is worth your attention.

What This Role Actually Covers

Avanath operates affordable workforce housing, and this Assistant Community Manager position in Gresham, Oregon supports the full operational load of a LIHTC community. That means rent collection, posting, and deposits alongside compliance file maintenance, delinquency follow-up, and lease enforcement. It also means handling leasing traffic, touring prospective residents, and running resident retention events. When the Community Manager is off-site, you run the property. That's not a stretch assignment; it's a regular expectation of the role.

Reporting is part of the daily rhythm here. You'll assist with monthly projection reporting, inspect vacancies, track make-ready status, and flag maintenance or policy issues during property walks. You'll also represent the property in eviction proceedings when required, so familiarity with proper notice requirements and landlord-tenant law isn't optional background knowledge.

What Avanath Is Looking For

  • At least two years of experience as an Assistant Community Manager
  • Working knowledge of LIHTC and tax credit compliance. This is a hard requirement, not a preferred qualification
  • Proficiency with Yardi Voyager
  • Solid bookkeeping and rent collection track record
  • Strong grasp of Fair Housing law and ADA requirements
  • Comfort with Word, Excel, and standard office communication tools
  • Interpersonal range: you'll deal with residents in crisis, vendors, social services contacts, and regulatory partners, sometimes all in the same afternoon

The compliance piece is worth emphasizing. Tax-credit communities carry a file maintenance burden that conventional Class A properties don't. Strong candidates know the difference between a complete file and a compliant one, and they don't need reminders to keep documentation current. Candidates who've only worked market-rate will face a real learning curve on the compliance side, even if their leasing and collections skills are solid.

Avanath positions this role as relationship-driven, and that's accurate for affordable housing in ways it isn't always true elsewhere. Residents often face financial instability, and the ACM here functions partly as a resource coordinator. Knowing how to connect a resident to rental assistance or social services, without stepping outside your lane, is a skill that comes up regularly and that you won't find described in most job postings for this title.

job.title: Community Manager, BTR
job.description:
BTR community management sits at the intersection of hospitality and operations. You're running a physical asset, yes, but residents in a single-family rental community chose that lifestyle for specific reasons, and they notice when the experience falls short. Evergreen Residential's 102-home gated community in Raleigh needs someone who can hold both of those things at once: the warmth of a great front-of-house and the discipline of someone who tracks traffic, conversion, and make-ready timelines without being reminded.

What This Role Actually Covers

You'll be the primary on-site contact, which means your day spans a wide range of interactions. A prospective resident calls about availability in the morning, a vendor needs sign-off on a punch list item by noon, and a current resident has a concern about a common area by end of day. That variety is real, and so is the accountability that comes with it.

On the leasing side, you'll guide prospects from first inquiry through application, move-in coordination, and early occupancy. This community is likely in or near lease-up, so hitting occupancy targets within timeline matters. You'll run tours, host open house events, track your own traffic and conversion metrics, and support outreach through local partnerships and digital marketing. You'll also monitor competing communities in the Raleigh market and relay relevant pricing intel to the revenue management team.

Day-to-day operations include vendor relationships, amenity upkeep, community appearance, and coordinating with centralized support teams on applications and move-ins. Evergreen operates as a platform, so you won't be doing everything solo. But you are the on-site leader, and residents will look to you first.

  • 1 to 3 years of leasing experience, including involvement in lease-up or new construction
  • Strong interpersonal skills and comfort managing competing priorities without constant oversight
  • Familiarity with Fair Housing regulations
  • Active North Carolina Real Estate License (the posting notes Arizona, but this role is based in Raleigh)
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • Background in hospitality or customer service is a genuine plus here, not just a box to check

The Raleigh BTR Market and What It Means for This Role

Raleigh has seen significant BTR development over the past few years, with several institutional operators now competing for the same renter profile: professionals and families who want the space and privacy of a single-family home without the burden of ownership. That means your competitive awareness matters. Knowing what a comparable community two miles away is offering in concessions or amenities gives you and the revenue team real information to work with.

Team Fit and Growth

Evergreen describes itself as transparent and collaborative, which tends to mean you'll have visibility into decisions that affect your community and a real voice when you flag issues. For someone who wants to grow in BTR or SFR operations specifically, this kind of platform role builds skills that carry: lease-up execution, resident retention in a non-traditional product type, and working within a centralized ops model. Community managers who perform well in BTR environments often move into regional or portfolio oversight as the asset class continues to scale.

If you're someone who takes genuine ownership of the place you manage, treats resident interactions as relationship-building rather than transaction management, and can stay organized when three things need your attention at once, this role has real substance to it.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do at Music City Flat

This role puts you at the center of everything happening at Music City Flat, a multifamily property in Nashville managed by Karya Property Management. Your day pulls in multiple directions: reviewing the rent roll for MTM exposure and upcoming expirations, checking delinquency and making collection decisions, running through the make-ready schedule with maintenance, and staying on top of leasing activity from lead to approved application. You're also the person your on-site staff looks to for direction, accountability, and coaching on renewals and resident retention.

The compliance side matters too. Karya expects you to submit HR paperwork accurately and on time, which means you're not just managing people but also managing the documentation that keeps the property running cleanly at the corporate level. Emergency calls rotate to you when they need to, so this is a role that asks for genuine availability, not just scheduled hours.

What You Bring

  • At least three years of community manager experience at a multifamily property
  • Hands-on familiarity with leasing, renewals, collections, and maintenance coordination
  • Experience with Onesite (required) and a CAM or CAPS designation (a strong plus)
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills, especially when situations get tense with residents or staff
  • High school diploma or equivalent required; a college degree is preferred
  • Comfort working evenings and weekends on a rotating schedule

Where This Role Can Take You

Community Manager is the role in multifamily where operational and financial accountability converge. You're watching NOI through the lens of occupancy, delinquency, and renewal rates, while also managing the people who keep the property in good physical condition. That combination of skills, financial oversight plus staff leadership, is exactly what regional and district manager roles require. Managers who come out of Onesite environments with clean rent roll habits and a track record of retention tend to move up faster because those skills transfer directly to multi-site oversight.

Nashville's multifamily market has stayed competitive, and operators here expect community managers to run tight ships on both the leasing and the expense side. If you've been in a strong lease-up or managed through a value-add renovation cycle elsewhere, that context will sharpen how you approach this property from day one.

job.title: Property Manager
job.description:
FLATS has built its reputation on a particular idea: that urban apartment living should feel intentional, not generic. The company operates lifestyle-driven communities where design, technology, and resident experience are treated as core product features, not afterthoughts. The Property Manager they're hiring in Chicago will be the person responsible for making that philosophy operational, on the ground, every day.

This is a lease-up role. If you've managed a stabilized asset, you know the rhythm of renewals, retention, and steady-state NOI management. Lease-up is a different discipline. You're building occupancy from scratch, which means pricing strategy, concessions decisions, and traffic conversion matter enormously in the early months. You'll work closely with leadership to set and adjust leasing strategy, communicate progress and risks to ownership, and keep the team executing at a pace that stabilized communities rarely require. The ability to read your T-3 and T-12 trends and translate them into action, quickly, is what separates strong candidates from those who struggle in this environment.

On the financial side, you'll own budget participation, expense control, and monthly financial review. You'll approve vendor invoices, coordinate with accounting, and monitor collections, deposits, and fees with attention to detail. Chicago's landlord-tenant regulatory environment adds a layer of complexity here: this role requires working knowledge of Illinois landlord-tenant law, Fair Housing requirements, ADA compliance, and FCRA standards. If those frameworks are already familiar to you, you'll spend your energy applying them, rather than learning them under pressure.

The operations side covers the full scope of a multifamily community: unit readiness, make-ready coordination, punch list completion, preventive maintenance schedules, and service request resolution. You'll also recruit, train, and manage your onsite team, which means performance management, coaching, and building a staff culture that aligns with what FLATS actually promises residents.

An Illinois Real Estate License is required. Prior lease-up or new construction experience is a firm expectation, and familiarity with Yardi Voyager or comparable property management software will matter from day one.

What this role requires vs. what it builds

  • Requires: lease-up experience, IL Real Estate License, working knowledge of Chicago landlord-tenant law, financial reporting literacy, team leadership, and property management software proficiency
  • Builds: deeper comfort with lease-up strategy at a brand-driven operator, owner-facing communication skills, and experience managing a community where design and resident experience are differentiated product features rather than table stakes

For a property manager looking to move toward a regional or portfolio-level role, a successful lease-up at a quality operator like FLATS is exactly the kind of credential that opens those doors. Bilingual Spanish is a plus given Chicago's resident demographics, though it's not a requirement. Compensation is $85,000 to $100,000 with a performance bonus, plus medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with employer match, and PTO.

job.title: Concierge (Full-Time) | Luxury High-Rise - Seaholm District
job.description:
The Modern Residences sits in Austin's Seaholm District, one of the city's more distinctive live-work-play corridors. The concierge desk is the first and most consistent point of contact residents interact with daily. Worth Ross Management Company is hiring a full-time Concierge to fill that role.

What You'll Actually Do

Your shift starts at the front desk. You greet residents by name, check in guests and vendors, and manage building access according to established protocols. Packages get logged in BuildingLink. Deliveries get tracked. Requests get routed to the right people. When a resident has a concern or an emergency situation surfaces, you handle it calmly and escalate when necessary.

A lot of this work is repetitive in the best way. Strong concierges build consistency. Residents learn they can count on you for accurate information, quick follow-through, and discretion. That last part matters more in luxury high-rise than most people expect. Residents in buildings like this often have high privacy expectations, and honoring those without being prompted is part of the job.

WRMC runs BuildingLink for activity and package logging, so comfort with property-level software is useful. The schedule requires flexibility to cover morning or afternoon shifts, including weekends and holidays.

What You Bring

  • Background in hospitality, luxury residential, or a high-touch customer service environment
  • Clear, professional communication with residents, vendors, and guests
  • Composure under pressure and a solution-first approach when issues arise
  • Attention to detail in logging, tracking, and following up on requests
  • High school diploma or equivalent; prior concierge or front-of-house experience preferred
  • Comfort with email and property or concierge management systems

Context Worth Knowing

Concierge roles at luxury high-rises are often a strong entry point into property management careers. People who excel here frequently move into leasing consultant or assistant community manager positions, particularly at companies like WRMC that promote from within. The skills you build, resident relations, vendor coordination, professional communication, and software fluency, transfer directly to nearly every other role in multifamily operations.

The benefit package includes medical, dental, and vision coverage, short and long-term disability, an employee assistance program, identity theft protection, pet insurance, retirement, and paid time off.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

Eastgrove is a 650-plus unit community that Peak Management recently acquired in Dallas, and they need technicians who can hit the ground running on a property of that scale. Your day runs from work orders to unit turns, HVAC diagnostics to appliance troubleshooting, with the kind of volume that keeps a good tech genuinely busy. You'll carry on-call rotation responsibility, which means nights and weekends come with the territory. That's not a footnote. It's a real part of the job, and Peak pays an on-call premium to reflect it.

The technical range here matters. This role calls for HVAC competency, electronic troubleshooting, and general equipment maintenance across a large garden-style footprint. At 650-plus units, even a modest work order backlog requires someone who can prioritize efficiently, communicate with residents clearly, and close tickets at a pace that keeps occupancy from slipping.

What You Bring

  • Hands-on maintenance experience with HVAC systems, including troubleshooting and repair
  • Electronic troubleshooting skills and comfort with general equipment maintenance
  • Physical capability: sustained standing and walking, climbing ladders, lifting up to 50 pounds, and working in confined or awkward spaces across varied weather conditions
  • Reliable personal transportation
  • Availability for on-call rotation
