  • A low-drama, get-it-done approach to the work

The Package and the Context

Peak offers medical, dental, and life insurance, PTO (including your birthday), a sign-on bonus, and a 401(k) with employer matching. The on-call premium pay is a genuine differentiator since many operators don't separate that compensation out.

One thing worth knowing about a newly acquired property at this size: the first 12 to 18 months post-acquisition typically surface deferred maintenance that wasn't fully captured in due diligence. That means a skilled technician joining now will see more variety in the work than they might at a stabilized asset, which is either a selling point or a caution depending on what you're looking for. For a tech who wants to build skills fast, a lease-up or newly acquired community generates real-world experience at a compressed pace.

Peak Management is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Maintenance work at a residential property is steady, physical, and sometimes unpredictable. You can plan your morning around three work orders and end up spending the afternoon chasing down a burst pipe or a tripped breaker that nobody can explain. If that kind of shift doesn't bother you, this role is worth a serious look.

CYM Living is a national property management firm with roots in Chicago and New York, and they're building out their maintenance team in Fort Wayne. Their model leans on data and technology at the portfolio level while keeping service hyperlocal at the property level. For a technician, that means organized work order tracking and a management team that's paying attention to how the properties perform, not just collecting rent.

The day-to-day covers the full range: plumbing repairs, electrical troubleshooting, HVAC service, carpentry, unit make-readies, and routine inspections to catch problems before they become expensive. You'll handle resident work orders, participate in preventative maintenance programs, and keep your records clean so the supervisor has an accurate picture of what's been done and what's pending. It's real work across all the trades, not a role where you're covering one narrow specialty.

The on-call rotation is real, and it's worth naming plainly. Emergency maintenance requests happen after hours. A water heater doesn't care that it's 10pm. You'll take turns in the rotation, and some weeks are quieter than others, but you should go in knowing that the phone can ring on your night.

What the role calls for

  • Prior experience as a maintenance technician in residential or a closely related setting
  • Working knowledge of plumbing, electrical, HVAC, and general carpentry
  • Attention to detail on inspections and work order documentation
  • Comfortable working both independently and alongside other maintenance staff
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • Clear communication with residents and property management

Strong candidates tend to be the ones who close work orders completely rather than patching things just enough to quiet a complaint. Residents notice the difference, and so does a supervisor reviewing callbacks. If you take pride in the punch list being actually done, that habit carries real weight here.

CYM Living offers competitive pay based on experience, health, dental, and vision coverage, a retirement plan with employer match, paid time off, and access to ongoing training and development. Fort Wayne's rental market has been growing steadily, and CYM's vertically integrated structure means there's room to move up as the portfolio expands.

job.title: Apartment Leasing Sales Consultant - Terrawood
job.description:
Leasing Consultant roles at large portfolio operators like AIR Communities run closer to structured sales positions than traditional apartment leasing jobs. There's a defined process to follow, targets to hit each month, and a commission structure that rewards closing well, not just closing often.

What You'll Be Doing

This role is based at Terrawood in Grapevine, TX. Day to day, you'll work inbound and outbound prospects, schedule and lead property tours, and follow AIR's sales process from first contact through signed lease. Prompt follow-up matters here. A prospect who doesn't hear back quickly moves on.

You'll carry monthly leasing goals and be expected to meet or beat them consistently. The commission structure has several layers: higher rent units, longer lease terms (18 months or more), and hitting monthly volume tiers all generate separate commission bumps. That's worth paying attention to if you're good at upselling.

You'll also support resident experience at every interaction, contribute to local marketing efforts, and provide leasing coverage to other AIR communities in the area as needed. Fair Housing compliance is required in every transaction.

What AIR Is Looking For

  • At least one year of sales or customer service experience where you had real goals to hit (property management, hospitality, retail, and restaurant backgrounds all apply)
  • A track record of following a sales process, not just winging it
  • Availability to work weekends and adjusted hours depending on season and community needs
  • Reliable transportation
  • Strong written and verbal English communication

Compensation and Benefits

Base pay runs $19.00 to $20.00 per hour, plus commissions. AIR also offers a 25% rent discount at any community in their portfolio, which is a real number if you're considering living onsite or nearby. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, a 401(k) with up to 6% employer match, paid parental leave up to 16 weeks, and tuition assistance with full reimbursement for job-related certifications.

One perk worth noting: after peak leasing season ends, AIR may offer extended unpaid time off over winter, while you retain your full benefits and rent discount. It's an unusual structure, and it appeals to people who want a real break rather than rolling straight into the slower months.

Strong candidates in this type of role tend to treat the tour as a sales conversation, not a property walkthrough. They ask qualifying questions, adjust their pitch based on what the prospect actually needs, and follow up without being pushed to do it. If you've sold on commission before and know how to work a pipeline, that background translates directly here.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Village Green manages communities where residents actually want to come home. That standard extends to the maintenance team, because nothing erodes trust with a resident faster than a work order that drags or a turn that looks rushed. If you take that seriously, this role in Woodbury, MN is worth your attention.

The day-to-day here covers the full range of what a capable technician handles: completing work orders on time, responding to service requests across plumbing, electrical, and appliances, and keeping up with turns that require real trade knowledge. A make-ready here means more than a quick clean. You're looking at drywall repair, painting, appliance inspection or swap-out, and anything else that needs to be right before a new resident walks in. The property's exterior condition is also part of your scope. Curb appeal maintenance, seasonal snow removal, and pool and spa upkeep (where applicable) are all on the table.

On-call availability comes with the role. Property managers lean on technicians who can be reached after hours and who respond without dragging their feet. That's the honest part of this job that doesn't always make it into postings. It's also where the quarterly bonus program starts to make more sense.

Pay runs $25 to $29 per hour depending on experience, with quarterly bonuses on top. Village Green also offers medical, dental, and vision coverage, and a 401(k) with a company match.

One thing that separates strong candidates here: residents are part of every service call. A technician who fixes the problem correctly but leaves a resident feeling dismissed will always create more friction than they resolve. The people who thrive in this kind of role combine real technical skill with basic interpersonal common sense. You don't have to be warm and fuzzy, but you do have to be professional and communicative.

What they're looking for

  • One to three years of experience in multifamily housing or hospitality maintenance
  • Strong working knowledge of plumbing, electrical, appliances, and painting
  • HVAC familiarity is expected; certifications in plumbing, contracting, or building trades are a plus
  • Comfortable with basic computer use for work order tracking
  • Available for on-call rotation and occasional weekend work

Village Green participates in E-Verify and requires pre-employment drug screening and background checks as part of the hiring process.

job.title: Regional Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
Third-party management companies face a structural challenge that in-house operators don't: maintenance quality varies site to site because each property runs its own team, often with minimal cross-property accountability. A Regional Maintenance Supervisor exists specifically to close that gap. At Asset Living, one of the larger third-party firms in the country (NMHC top 50, AMO-accredited), this role covers multiple properties across the Denver region and reports upward to a Director of Facilities.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Most of your time splits between site visits and the work those visits generate. You're walking properties to assess curb appeal, audit make-ready timelines, check inventory, and verify that preventative maintenance programs are running as designed. When you find deficiencies, you work directly with on-site maintenance managers and Regional Managers to correct them quickly. That's the cycle: inspect, identify, fix, follow up.

Beyond site visits, you're embedded in capital work. You'll help develop annual capex budgets, assist with scoping projects, and monitor vendor performance through completion. You'll also support due diligence and property transitions by doing inspections and staff assessments, which means you'll see new assets before the rest of the team does.

KPIs matter here. Make-ready completion times and work order close rates are the metrics you'll track across your portfolio. When numbers drift, you're the one who flags it and works with on-site staff to get them back on track.

Compliance is a real part of this role. You'll reinforce environmental safety programs covering asbestos, lead-based paint, and mold response across every property in your region. These aren't checkbox exercises. Regulatory exposure in multifamily is real, and keeping sites current is part of what this position protects against.

Who Fits This Role

  • Extensive background in maintenance management, with direct experience leading teams across multiple properties
  • EPA and CPO certifications required
  • Comfortable with capital project management from scope development through vendor selection and completion
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office (Word, Outlook, Excel at minimum)
  • Strong communicator between field maintenance staff and office/management teams
  • Able to work a flexible schedule, including hours outside the standard Monday through Friday window

The honest part: this role involves regular travel across the region, in-person attendance is required, and weeks over 40 hours are expected, not occasional. If you've managed single-site maintenance, the jump to multi-site regional oversight is a meaningful one. The administrative load is heavier, the stakeholder count is higher, and you're accountable for outcomes you don't always directly control. Candidates who do well in regional maintenance roles typically combine genuine technical depth with the patience to coach rather than just fix things themselves.

For someone ready for that scope, regional maintenance roles at third-party firms tend to be a direct path toward Director of Facilities or VP of Operations positions, especially at a company with a growing portfolio across multifamily, build-to-rent, affordable, and student housing segments.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Scion's Experience Team Member (ETM) role at Lark Huntsville is a front-line leasing and customer experience position at a student housing property in Huntsville, TX, home to Sam Houston State University. If you've spent time around collegiate living, you already know the pace: high traffic during lease-up season, a resident population that turns over almost entirely every 12 months, and a summer turn that demands real stamina and focus.

What You'll Actually Do

The day-to-day splits into three areas: sales and leasing, community engagement, and property administration. On the leasing side, you'll tour prospects, field objections, and report feedback to the management team so they can adjust pricing or concessions strategies. You'll also support social media content and local marketing outreach, which in a college market means staying current on what's happening on campus and positioning the property accordingly.

Administration work is real and steady. Package logging, maintenance request follow-ups, office upkeep, and occasional after-hours lockout coverage are all part of the job. During turn periods (the intensive move-out/move-in window between leases), expect the workload to spike significantly. Availability during summer and holidays is a firm requirement.

What You Bring

  • Strong interpersonal skills across a diverse resident base
  • Comfort in a role where priorities shift daily
  • Self-discipline and reliability without close supervision
  • Availability for on-call rotation and peak seasonal periods
  • Customer-first approach to every interaction, including difficult ones

Context Worth Knowing

Student housing operates on a compressed leasing calendar. Most of the year's traffic arrives in a tight window, and the ETM role sits directly in front of it. Candidates who do well here tend to build strong organizational habits early, because the volume during peak periods punishes disorganization quickly. This role also builds a transferable skill set: sales tracking, resident relations, marketing execution, and administrative systems knowledge all translate directly into assistant manager or leasing manager positions down the line. It's a genuine entry point into property management with real upward mobility for people who perform.

Scion is an established name in student housing with a national portfolio. Working at Lark Huntsville means learning student housing operations from a company with defined processes and clear standards, which tends to produce more structured training than smaller operators.

U.S. work authorization is required. Visa sponsorship is not available.

job.title: Community Specialist
job.description:
Evergreen Residential operates in the single-family rental and build-to-rent space, and this role sits right at the center of that work. As a Community Specialist based in Raleigh, you'll cover two BTR communities, The Point and Brier Creek, while also supporting a scattered SFR portfolio as needed. It's a field-based position where leasing and resident operations run together all day, every day.

The leasing side is real and consistent. You'll conduct tours, respond to inbound leads across phone, email, and walk-ins, track traffic and conversion data, and execute lease-up strategies to hit occupancy targets on schedule. You'll also assist with applications and coordinate move-in readiness, working alongside centralized teams that handle screening, documentation, and scheduling. Units need to be ready when residents arrive, and you're the on-site person making sure that happens.

Beyond leasing, you're the face of the communities day to day. That means community walks, vendor coordination, amenity oversight, and staying on top of property appearance. When residents have concerns, you're the first call. You'll also support retention efforts and local outreach, including events, social content, and partnerships with nearby businesses.

BTR lease-ups move differently than traditional multifamily. The asset class is still maturing, and Evergreen sits at the institutional end of that market. Strong candidates will already understand traffic-to-application conversion, know how to read what's happening with competitor pricing, and communicate that back to a revenue management team. If you've worked a lease-up before, you know how quickly the pace shifts from pipeline-building to move-in coordination. Both skills matter here.

What You'll Need

  • 1 to 3 years of leasing experience, preferably including a lease-up or new construction project
  • Active North Carolina Real Estate License
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation (you're covering multiple sites)
  • Working knowledge of Fair Housing regulations
  • Comfort operating independently with limited on-site supervision
  • Background in leasing, hospitality, or customer-facing service roles

Evergreen was founded in 2021 and is headquartered in Dallas, with offices in New York. The company's focus on data-driven operations and technology means the tools you use here will likely be more sophisticated than what you'd find at a smaller operator. If you want exposure to how institutional SFR platforms actually run at scale, this is a legitimate opportunity to build that experience.

job.title: Groundskeeper
job.description:
Eden Commons is a 196-unit community in Eden Prairie, and Bigos Management is looking for a Groundskeeper to keep it looking sharp from the parking lot to the pool deck. This is a Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. position, which makes it a steadier schedule than a lot of facilities roles out there.

The work spans both exterior grounds and interior common areas. On any given morning, that might mean watering and pruning flowerbeds, blowing leaves off walkways, checking light fixtures in the foyers, and cleaning laundry rooms before residents start their day. Minnesota winters add a real layer to this job: shoveling, sanding icy walkways, and keeping pedestrian areas safe during stretches of freeze-thaw cycles that can make paths genuinely hazardous. Summer means pool area upkeep, patio furniture setup and takedown, and staying on top of landscaping during growing season. The property changes what it asks of you depending on the month.

Beyond grounds work, you'll assist the maintenance team on turns and make-readies as needed, including paint touch-ups in vacant units and clearing out abandoned property. You'll also walk the property daily, which keeps you close to what's actually happening on the grounds and gives the team real-time eyes on conditions that could turn into bigger issues.

Bigos has been named a Star Tribune Top Workplace twelve times, which reflects something real about how they approach staffing and culture. Pay ranges from $17.00 to $19.00 per hour to start, with benefits beginning the first of the month after hire, ten paid holidays with no waiting period, and a 401(k) with employer match. There's also a rent discount and a Lifetime Fitness membership discount, which fit naturally with a physically active role like this one.

Candidates who do well in groundskeeping roles like this one tend to have a good eye for detail and a sense of ownership over their area. A property looks clean because someone notices the small things before they compound. Prior experience maintaining grounds at a larger residential property is a plus, and comfort with lawn care products and seasonal equipment matters. This role requires regular lifting of 20 or more pounds, with frequent lifts up to 80 pounds with assistance, so physical readiness for that kind of day is essential.

Qualifications:
  • At least 18 years of age
  • Prior grounds or facilities maintenance experience at a residential property preferred
  • Familiarity with lawn care, cleaning products, and seasonal equipment
  • Strong communication and time management skills
  • Ability to work safely in a physically demanding outdoor and indoor environment
  • Comfortable with daily property walks and direct resident interaction

job.title: Assistant General Manager- Sacramento, CA
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role sits at the center of daily HOA community operations. You'll work directly alongside the General Manager, handling the kind of tasks that keep a managed community running without friction: coordinating member services, fielding homeowner inquiries, and making sure the front desk and access control teams have the direction and training they need to perform well. You're the connective tissue between management decisions and resident experience.

In practice, that means your days shift between administrative detail and people-facing work. One hour you're reviewing community information to make sure it's accurate and current. The next you're training a front desk staff member on proper access control procedure or helping a homeowner understand association policy. The General Manager sets the direction; you help execute it and keep things moving when they're occupied elsewhere.

What You Bring

  • Prior experience in HOA management, residential property management, or a community-facing operations role
  • Comfort supervising and training support staff, with the patience to coach people through unfamiliar processes
  • Clear, professional communication with homeowners and board members, especially when conversations get tense
  • Organizational discipline to track open issues, follow up consistently, and close the loop without being reminded
  • Familiarity with access control systems and front desk operations is a genuine advantage here

The Craft of This Role

HOA management builds a specific kind of operational fluency that translates well across the industry. Working under a General Manager in a large association gives you exposure to governance, resident relations, vendor coordination, and staff supervision simultaneously. Those are exactly the skills that prepare someone to step into a General Manager role of their own. If you want to understand how a professionally managed community actually runs from the inside, this position delivers that education hands-on.

Action Property Management has operated in the HOA space since 1984 and now manages over 300 communities across nine offices, which means there's institutional knowledge here and real room to grow within a structured organization. The Sacramento market includes a mix of planned communities and high-density associations, so the complexity you'll encounter is genuine.

Strong candidates in this role tend to be people who already understand that homeowner satisfaction and operational consistency aren't in conflict. They know how to de-escalate a frustrated resident while still upholding community rules. That balance, between empathy and policy, is what separates a capable AGM from one who's just managing the inbox.

job.title: Maintenance Technician (59281)
job.description:
It's 8:15 a.m. on a Tuesday at a 196-unit senior community in Los Angeles. A resident called in a plumbing issue late yesterday, a work order came through this morning, and there's an apartment that vacated over the weekend sitting at day two of its five-day turn window. That's the rhythm this role runs on.

What This Role Covers

Cirrus Asset Management is hiring a Maintenance Technician for San Lucas Senior Apartments, a 196-unit property in Los Angeles. The schedule is Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., with on-call availability for after-hours emergencies. Pay runs $25 to $26 per hour.

The work spans a full range of building systems. You'll complete work orders within required timeframes, run make-readies on vacated units within five days of move-out, and conduct routine building surveys to catch mechanical issues before they become health or safety concerns. Day-to-day tasks include:

  • Electrical maintenance: replacing fixtures, sockets, and cleaning or repairing circuit breaker panels
  • Plumbing and HVAC component repairs
  • Interior and exterior painting, including prep and priming
  • Lock, door hardware, and closer repairs and replacements
  • Life safety documentation: fire extinguisher logs, suppression systems, alarm contacts, and related building systems
  • Manual repairs as needed, including window replacements and general fixes
  • Participation in ongoing safety, technical, and operational training programs
  • Accurate documentation of completed work and materials used

What You Bring and What You'll Build

The role requires at least one year of hands-on maintenance technician experience, a high school diploma, and solid working knowledge of general maintenance methods, tools, and common building systems. Manual dexterity, attention to detail, and strong time management matter here because the five-day turn clock doesn't pause, and a senior community means residents often have a lower tolerance for unresolved issues and longer waits.

Certifications like HVAC or CMRP aren't required but carry real weight in the review process. If you hold one, it's worth noting prominently. If you don't, this role builds toward that kind of credentialed expertise. Technicians who document work thoroughly and demonstrate consistent quality on turns and work orders tend to move into lead or facilities supervisor roles over time, and a senior community with nearly 200 units gives you regular exposure to the systems and resident communication skills that make that transition easier.

Cirrus offers health, dental, vision, and life insurance, a 401(k) plan, and paid holiday, sick, and vacation time, along with healthcare spending account options including HSAs, FSAs, and HRAs.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Commercial Maintenance in a Full-Service CRE Environment

Stream Realty Partners runs a large and varied portfolio across office, industrial, retail, healthcare, and multifamily assets. That breadth matters for a Maintenance Technician because the systems you work on change depending on the property: one building might have a central chiller plant and a complex BAS, another might lean heavily on rooftop HVAC units and simpler electrical. In Phoenix, where mechanical systems run hard against desert heat for most of the year, keeping equipment performing at spec directly ties to operating costs and NOI. A well-run preventive maintenance program is one of the cleaner ways to keep that number healthy.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Day-to-day, this role sits inside the building engineering function. You'll be working across mechanical, electrical, plumbing, and HVAC systems, handling both scheduled preventive maintenance and reactive work orders as they come in. That means pumps, air handling units, boilers, compressors, chillers, and the building fixtures and components that generate steady ticket volume. You'll also participate in water treatment chemical programs, maintain operation logs and central plant records, and develop familiarity with fire alarm and life safety systems at your assigned property.

Customer interaction is part of this position. Stream describes its service standard as concierge-level, which in commercial real estate typically means responsive, professional, and low-friction for tenants and internal partners alike. How you handle a work order follow-up or a tenant concern reflects directly on the property's reputation and retention.

Shifts can include early mornings, late evenings, weekends, and holidays, and overtime is a reality when building operations demand it. That's honest, and it's worth factoring in before you apply.

What Stream Is Looking For

  • 1 to 2 years of experience in commercial building operations, property management, or a closely related field (preferred)
  • Working knowledge of HVAC, electrical, plumbing, and hydraulic system fundamentals
  • Comfort with power tools: pneumatic, electric, drill motors, grinders, impact wrenches
  • EPA Universal Certification required within 90 days of hire
  • Ability to obtain city or state licenses as applicable (boiler operating permits, maintenance electrician licenses, etc.)
  • High school diploma, GED, or trade school credential preferred
  • Physical capability to lift 50 lbs. or more, access roofs and confined spaces, and work split between indoor and outdoor environments
  • Steady composure in emergency situations

The candidates who tend to stand out in commercial building tech roles aren't just mechanically capable. They log accurately, they flag issues before they escalate, and they communicate clearly with property management and tenants. A chiller that gets caught early in a PM cycle is far cheaper than a mid-summer emergency replacement. That operational awareness separates a strong technician from an average one.

Stream is headquartered in Dallas and operates in markets across the country, which means internal mobility is a realistic path for people who perform well. Building engineering roles like this one frequently lead to Chief Engineer or Facilities Manager positions as experience with complex systems grows.

job.title: Apartment Service Technician
job.description:
New Orleans is a city that tests buildings constantly. Humidity, heat, the occasional tropical storm, aging infrastructure in older garden-style communities. A maintenance technician here earns their keep differently than someone working a newer lease-up in a Sun Belt suburb. If you understand that going in, this role at Morguard is worth a serious look.

Morguard is a North American real estate company with a multifamily portfolio that spans the continent. Their onsite teams carry real responsibility for keeping communities running well, and this Service Technician position sits at the center of that daily operation. The work covers the full range of hands-on maintenance: HVAC diagnosis and repair, plumbing, electrical, appliances, drywall, flooring, carpentry, and exterior upkeep. You're also handling the make-ready process for vacant units, which means walking the pre-move-out inspection, building the punch list, coordinating vendors where needed, and confirming every item is done before a new resident moves in. Turns move fast when leasing demand is there, so attention to detail during make-readies matters more than it might seem from the outside.

Beyond the unit work, you'll be responding to resident service requests, supporting the grounds and common areas, and participating in the quarterly preventative maintenance program. There's also a rotating after-hours emergency on-call schedule, which is standard in residential property management but worth knowing before you apply. It affects your personal schedule in real ways, and the best candidates for this kind of role have already made peace with that.

Morguard expects technicians to think about cost control practically: fix rather than replace when it makes sense, track inventory accurately, and flag reorder needs to the maintenance supervisor or community manager before supplies run low. These habits keep NOI from eroding through small, avoidable waste, and they reflect well on the technician who builds them.

What the role requires

  • At least 2 years of residential maintenance experience, including work orders and make-ready turns
  • Basic to moderate skills across electrical, plumbing, HVAC, and appliance repair
  • EPA Universal certification (required)
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • Ability to pass a pre-employment drug test and background check

Morguard offers medical insurance options, a 401(k) with dollar-for-dollar matching and immediate vesting, paid time off including summer hours and holidays, and an education reimbursement program. There's also an employee housing discount within their portfolio, subject to availability, which is a benefit that carries real value depending on where you're at in life.

The candidates who stand out in this kind of role tend to be the ones who communicate well under pressure. When a resident's AC goes out in August in New Orleans, the technical fix matters, but so does how you interact with that person when you show up. Composure and basic people skills go further than most maintenance job postings let on.

job.title: Account Resolution Specialist
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role sits at the intersection of resident relations and loss mitigation for Mynd, Roofstock's property management platform serving single-family rental investors. Your core metric is delinquency. You'll monitor it daily, respond to it early, and work accounts through to resolution, whether that means a payment arrangement that actually sticks or initiating and tracking an eviction to completion. In the SFR space, where each home is its own asset on an investor's ledger, a delinquency that drags for 60 or 90 days hits NOI hard. Speed and accuracy matter.

On any given week, you might be negotiating a payment plan with a resident who's two months past due, coordinating with local legal counsel to file an unlawful detainer, preparing a delinquency summary for portfolio review, or appearing in court (in person or via Zoom) to represent a managed property. You'll also work cross-functionally with property management teams to flag patterns before they compound, and you'll help train those teams on prevention strategies that keep accounts from aging into eviction territory in the first place.

Record-keeping is a real part of this job. Accurate case documentation, payment tracking, and compliance with jurisdiction-specific notice timelines all fall on you. Dallas has its own procedural cadence for evictions, and staying current on Texas landlord-tenant law is not optional. Quarterly travel within your assigned territory is expected.

What You Bring

  • At least 3 years in property management or real estate, with hands-on exposure to delinquency workflows and eviction procedures in single-family or multifamily settings
  • Comfort de-escalating tense resident conversations while holding firm on timelines and legal requirements
  • Solid working knowledge of residential landlord-tenant law, particularly Texas regulations
  • Experience building financial reports and working in spreadsheets to track case status and payment trends
  • Proficiency with property management platforms (Yardi, AppFolio, MRI, Propertyware, or similar) is a strong plus
  • Ability to manage a high-volume caseload independently, without losing detail on individual accounts
  • Flexibility for occasional evenings, weekends, or travel when case timelines demand it

Why This Role Is Harder Than It Looks

SFR delinquency management is a different animal from multifamily. You're not working a centralized property where you can knock on a door down the hall. Each resident is at a separate address, often in different sub-markets, with different county court procedures and notice requirements. Strong candidates typically come in knowing how to read a delinquency aging report, prioritize accounts by risk, and communicate with residents in a way that recovers money without torching the relationship unnecessarily. The candidates who struggle tend to either move too slowly on legal timelines or escalate too fast before trying resolution. This role requires both patience and urgency, applied at the right moments. Compensation for this position runs $24 to $26 per hour, with total compensation including a benefits package that covers health, dental, vision, 401k, and paid parental leave.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Leasing consultant roles tend to attract people who like variety. No two days look quite the same when you're fielding prospect calls in the morning, walking tour routes at midday, and following up on applications before close. At Berkshire Residential Investments, this position carries that same rhythm, but within a company that puts some genuine thought into how its people experience the work, not just how the property performs.

What the Job Actually Involves

Your primary job is helping people find a home, and that means being useful at every point in their decision process. You'll handle inbound traffic, conduct tours, and close leases. Berkshire holds its leasing consultants to at least a 20% closing ratio, which means you'll need to know how to read where a prospect is in their process and respond accordingly, not just hand over a brochure and hope for the best.

Beyond the sales side, you'll keep a close eye on tour routes and model units, making sure everything looks the way it should before a prospective resident walks through. You'll communicate with current residents too, in writing and in person, and you'll flag anything worth noting to the property manager when it comes to local market shifts or ideas for improving resident satisfaction. The administrative piece is real here: accurate records and attention to detail matter in leasing, because small errors in paperwork can create larger problems downstream.

Who Fits Well Here

Berkshire describes their team culture with some enthusiasm, and that's worth taking at face value. This is a company that leans into personality alongside competence. They want someone who genuinely enjoys people and brings energy to interactions, not just someone who can check the process boxes. At the same time, the role has real performance expectations attached to it, so the enthusiasm needs to be backed by follow-through.

  • At least two years of customer-facing experience (property management experience is a plus, but transferable skills count)
  • Comfortable adapting to leasing software and new technologies
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Organized, detail-oriented, and able to manage multiple tasks without things slipping

The candidates who tend to do well in roles like this one aren't necessarily the loudest in the room. They're the ones who remember names, follow up when they say they will, and treat a prospect's questions with patience even on a busy Saturday. That consistency across interactions is what drives closing ratios over time.

Compensation and Growth

The base salary range for this role is $42,000 to $48,000, with placement within that range depending on experience and qualifications. The role also includes bonuses, retirement and health benefits, paid time off (including sick leave, parental leave, and vacation), and a 25% rent discount. Berkshire also mentions personal development plans, which signals that there's some intention around helping people grow internally, whether that leads toward an assistant manager track or a broader leasing career over time.

Leasing consultant experience is genuinely transferable. The combination of sales skills, resident relations, and market awareness you build here creates a foundation that applies across Class A, B, and C communities and across different management structures. It's a solid starting point for someone who wants to move into a senior leasing or property management role eventually.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Manager
job.description:
Fairstead operates as an integrated owner, operator, and developer across a portfolio of more than 30,000 affordable apartments in 28 states. At a company built around keeping development, construction, and property management under one platform, the Service Manager role sits at the center of daily operations. This position is responsible for the physical condition of the property, the performance of the maintenance team, and the standards that residents experience every day.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

On any given week, you're inspecting mechanical systems, reviewing repair work, walking the property for cleanliness and safety, and stepping in to perform skilled maintenance tasks yourself when the situation calls for it. You supervise other maintenance employees, which means setting standards, coordinating workflows, and taking the lead on special projects that fall outside routine upkeep. Routine repairs you'll handle independently. Complex projects may bring in additional support, but your role is to stay ahead of issues before they escalate.

Fairstead leans into technology and data-driven operations across its platform, so comfort with Yardi property management software will serve you well here. Microsoft Office proficiency is expected. The company's emphasis on digital systems means a Service Manager who can document work orders accurately and work within those platforms adds real operational value beyond what a wrench can fix.

What You Bring to This Role

  • At least three years of hands-on property maintenance experience
  • Depth in at least one skilled trade, paired with broad general maintenance knowledge
  • Familiarity with building and mechanical systems, tools, and trade terminology
  • Strong grasp of safety protocols and accident prevention
  • Ability to implement and refine maintenance policies and procedures
  • Organization skills that hold up under pressure when multiple systems need attention at once

The honest reality of this role: occasional overtime for emergencies or special projects is part of the job. Affordable housing communities run on tight operational margins, and residents depend on functional, safe units. When something goes wrong outside of business hours, you're often the person who resolves it.

Where This Role Can Take You

Service Managers who perform well in affordable housing portfolios at this scale tend to develop a breadth of skills that translates across all asset classes. You're managing people, coordinating capex-level projects, maintaining compliance with safety standards, and contributing to NOI by keeping maintenance costs predictable and controllable. Those skills carry weight whether you stay within affordable housing or move into conventional property management. At a company with Fairstead's footprint and growth trajectory, there's also room to move into regional maintenance oversight for candidates who demonstrate leadership and system-level thinking.

job.title: Leasing Professional - Solaris at Tucson
job.description:
Tucson's multifamily market has seen steady renter demand driven by University of Arizona enrollment, a growing tech and defense sector presence, and continued in-migration from California and Phoenix. For a leasing professional, that means a real mix of traffic: students, young professionals, and relocating renters, each with different priorities. Solaris at Tucson sits inside that demand current, and CloudTen Residential is looking for someone who can convert that traffic into signed leases.

What This Role Actually Involves

CloudTen's portfolio spans hotel-to-residential conversions, high-rise lease-ups, and value-add repositioning projects across the West. This position is grounded in day-to-day leasing and community administration at Solaris, a community that requires someone comfortable with volume and process. The role carries real lease-up expectations: prior experience at a 150-plus unit property is required, so candidates coming from small boutique communities may find the pace and paperwork load an adjustment.

Core responsibilities include:

  • Conducting tours, qualifying prospects, and tailoring your pitch to what each renter actually cares about
  • Handling all leasing paperwork accurately: applications, leases, addenda, and move-in packets
  • Collecting and processing deposits, rent payments, and resident fees
  • Running regular market surveys to track local competition, pricing, and trends
  • Inspecting vacant units before showings and flagging make-ready concerns to maintenance
  • Following up with prospects and managing resident relations throughout the lease lifecycle
  • Maintaining compliance with Fair Housing laws and ADA requirements in every interaction

Software proficiency matters here. CloudTen uses OneSite and considers Entrata experience a meaningful plus. These platforms handle everything from applications to accounting entries, and fluency with them reduces errors on the administrative side of the role.

What Sets Strong Candidates Apart

The baseline is two years of leasing or sales experience and a real working knowledge of property management software. But the candidates who perform well in roles like this tend to bring something more specific: they treat their follow-up pipeline like a sales professional treats a CRM. They remember what a prospect said on the tour, they send correspondence that doesn't feel templated, and they push for occupancy without losing the relationship. Leasing bonuses are part of the compensation structure here, which means your income has a direct connection to how well you close.

Pay runs from $21 to $23 an hour depending on experience, with leasing bonuses on top. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, an FSA, company-paid life insurance, and paid time off. CloudTen positions itself as a growth-oriented operator, and for a leasing professional who wants a path toward assistant management or community management, a company with an active and varied portfolio gives that progression real footing.

job.title: Housekeeping Specialist - The Lawrence at Wellen Park ~ North Port, FL - Brand New
job.description:
Cleanliness at a luxury apartment community is a measurable thing. Residents notice it in the first three seconds of walking through a door. At The Lawrence at Wellen Park, a brand-new Davis Development community in North Port, FL, the Housekeeping Specialist carries that standard every single day.

The Skills This Role Runs On

This position draws heavily on physical attention to detail, safe chemical handling, and the kind of consistent follow-through that keeps a Class A property looking like move-in day, every day. You'll be working an assigned area, covering vacuuming, wet mopping, damp dusting, spot cleaning, and proper waste disposal, including materials that may be hazardous or infectious. That last part matters: the role requires familiarity with aseptic technique and safety protocols, not as an afterthought, but as a core daily habit.

Tracking supplies and equipment is also part of this job. You flag shortages to the Maintenance Supervisor before they become a problem. That kind of proactive communication keeps the make-ready process from stalling when an upcoming move-in is on the calendar.

What You Bring to the Role

  • At least one year of housekeeping experience in a multifamily setting, preferred
  • A high school diploma or equivalent, preferred
  • Clear verbal and written communication skills across all channels
  • Comfort with general safety requirements and departmental protocols
  • Physical capability to lift approximately 30 lbs and work on ladders as needed

Strong candidates in this type of role tend to have a systems mindset. They clean the same way twice because they've figured out the most efficient sequence, and they don't leave a unit until it would pass a punch list review. Residents and their families will cross your path regularly, so a professional, courteous manner matters as much as the technical side of the work.

Why Davis Development, and Why Now

Davis Development has spent 25 years building and managing luxury multifamily communities with an in-house, owner-operator model. That means the management team running The Lawrence is the same group that built it. On-site staff aren't executing someone else's playbook handed down from a distant regional office. They're making real decisions, which gives every team member, including housekeeping, actual ownership over their work.

The Lawrence at Wellen Park is brand new, which means you're establishing the cleanliness standard from day one. Lease-up communities have higher traffic, more frequent unit turns, and tighter make-ready timelines than stabilized properties. The pace is real, and so is the visibility of your work. If you've worked a lease-up before, you already know what that means. If you haven't, it's a strong credential to add to your PM career history.

Benefits include health coverage starting the first of the month after 30 days, a 401(k) with a 4% employer match that vests immediately, company-paid life insurance, paid time off with a carryover provision, and access to a company apparel store allowance.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
It's 9 a.m. on a Tuesday. A resident stops by the office to explain why the rent is short this month. Down the hall, a leasing consultant is about to tour a prospective resident and has a question about qualifying criteria. Your Community Manager is out, and the regional is expecting a projection report by end of week. All of this lands on your desk at roughly the same time. That's the reality of this role.

The Work Itself

Avanath manages affordable housing communities, and this Assistant Community Manager position in Portland sits at the intersection of operations, compliance, and resident relationships. You'll support the Community Manager across rent collection, delinquency follow-up, leasing, and monthly reporting. When the Community Manager is away, you run the property. That means the leasing staff, the vendor interactions, the resident concerns, and the financial picture all report up through you.

The compliance piece here carries real weight. Avanath operates under LIHTC (Low-Income Housing Tax Credit) programs, so file accuracy and regulatory adherence aren't optional extras. You'll work alongside the Compliance department on file maintenance, and you'll need to already understand how tax credit programs work before your first day. This isn't a role where someone teaches you the basics of Section 42 over time.

On the resident side, your job is part problem-solver, part resource hub. A resident who can't make rent on time often needs more than a late fee conversation. Knowing what social services partnerships and support resources exist, and being willing to connect people to them, is a genuine part of this work at Avanath. That community-building function is intentional, not incidental.

What You Bring

  • At least two years of experience as an Assistant Community Manager
  • Working knowledge of LIHTC and tax credit compliance requirements
  • Solid bookkeeping and rent collection track record, including delinquency management
  • Familiarity with Yardi Voyager and standard office software
  • Clear understanding of Fair Housing laws and landlord/tenant regulations
  • Strong interpersonal range: you're as comfortable de-escalating a frustrated resident as you are presenting numbers to a regional manager
  • Organized enough to maintain confidential resident files accurately and consistently

The candidates who tend to thrive in affordable housing operations aren't just technically capable. They're people who can hold a professional boundary and a human conversation at the same time. Residents in workforce housing communities are often navigating tight margins, and how you handle those interactions matters as much as whether the ledger balances. Both things have to be true.

Portland's affordable housing environment also comes with regulatory scrutiny that's higher than in many markets. Familiarity with Oregon's landlord/tenant law and eviction notice requirements is a real advantage, since this role includes representing the property in eviction proceedings when necessary.

If you've been an assistant manager at a tax credit property and you're ready to take on more operational responsibility, this role offers a clear path toward stepping into a Community Manager seat. Avanath's portfolio gives you visibility into a range of community types, which builds the kind of experience that opens doors.

job.title: Director of Management
job.description:
Rise AMG runs a portfolio of Texas HOA communities with complex amenity infrastructure and a genuine focus on operational discipline. They use EOS (Entrepreneurial Operating System) to structure how the company runs, which matters for this role because the Director of Management sits inside that system, not above it. If you've never worked inside an EOS company, expect a learning curve around rocks, scorecard accountability, and level 10 meetings. That's not a warning, just context.

This is a people-management role at scale. You're not managing community managers directly in the field sense. You're managing the managers, building their capacity, and making sure the organizational layer between executive leadership and frontline staff actually functions. That means identifying where a manager is struggling before it becomes a client problem, building development plans that stick, and holding accountability conversations that don't wreck relationships. The job requires you to stay close enough to day-to-day operations to spot friction early, but strategic enough to address root causes rather than symptoms.

Rise AMG is in a growth phase, and that shapes the role considerably. Growth-phase companies tend to promote capable individual contributors into management before anyone's built the systems to support them. Part of what this director will do is build those systems: performance standards, communication rhythms, reporting structures, and succession planning. Scalability is the word that comes up repeatedly in how this company describes what it needs, and that's accurate to where they are.

The honest challenge here is that you're responsible for organizational performance while working through other people's decisions. When a department head misses a KPI or a team falls short on client outcomes, you're accountable for the coaching and structure that was supposed to prevent it. That kind of indirect accountability is uncomfortable for leaders who are used to owning outcomes directly. If you thrive in it, this role fits. If you need to be the one executing, it probably doesn't.

What Rise AMG Is Looking For

  • Seven or more years of progressive management experience, with direct experience managing other managers or leading multiple teams
  • Demonstrated ability to translate executive strategy into operational priorities that teams can actually execute against
  • Comfort building performance management frameworks from incomplete starting points, not just inheriting finished systems
  • Experience with organizational development, succession planning, or leadership pipeline work
  • Strong communication skills across levels, including the ability to deliver hard feedback constructively and without delay
  • A bachelor's degree in business administration, management, organizational leadership, or a related field is preferred
  • HOA or association management background is a plus, but the company has stated this is a leadership operations role first

Candidates who do well in this kind of role tend to be the ones who've already made the mental shift from "how do I get this done" to "how do I build a team that gets this done consistently." That shift is harder than it sounds, and organizations at Rise AMG's growth stage need leaders who've already made it.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Student housing maintenance runs at a different pace than conventional multifamily. Turns are concentrated, the resident pool turns over annually, and the volume of service requests after move-in can be relentless. PeakMade Real Estate manages off-campus student communities across the country, and this Maintenance Technician role in Reno sits at the center of keeping the physical asset performing the way it needs to.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Day to day, you're working through the service request queue, completing repairs thoroughly rather than just closing tickets fast. You'll work alongside the Maintenance Supervisor on preventative maintenance scheduling, inventory tracking, and keeping the community meeting company safety and operating standards. Curb appeal, common areas, breezeways, and grounds all fall within scope. Pool maintenance is part of the role, including chemical logs that need to stay accurate and current.

Turns are a significant piece of this position. Student housing communities typically flip a large percentage of units in a tight window each summer, so your ability to move through make-readies efficiently, complete punch lists cleanly, and coordinate with the broader team matters more here than it might at a conventional property with staggered lease expirations.

  • Service request completion and repair work across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliances
  • Preventative maintenance on equipment per manufacturer schedules
  • Grounds, exterior, and common area upkeep daily
  • Pool maintenance and chemical log documentation
  • Participation in on-call rotation for after-hours emergencies
  • Compliance with safety protocols and hazard communications programs

On-call is real. That's worth stating plainly. Rotating emergency coverage is part of this job, and the schedule includes weekends and holidays. If that's a dealbreaker, this probably isn't the right fit.

What You Bring

At minimum, a high school diploma and at least one year of maintenance experience, ideally in the apartment industry. EPA Type I and II certification is preferred. You'll need reliable transportation and must live within 30 miles of the property. The physical demands are real: lifting up to 50 pounds, working at height on ladders, and spending time outdoors in Reno's temperature extremes, both summer heat and winter cold. You're also expected to supply your own hand tools.

Strong candidates in this type of role know how to triage. When you're fielding a full queue and a HVAC call comes in during a turn week, the ability to prioritize without dropping the ball on residents already in their units is what separates solid technicians from ones who burn out or frustrate their supervisors. Mechanical aptitude matters, but so does basic communication with residents who may be filing their first-ever maintenance request.

Growth and Compensation

PeakMade offers a technical development path that includes HVAC certification and CPO training, which are credentials that carry real weight if you eventually want to move into a Maintenance Supervisor role. The company also runs a facilities leadership program for those interested in growing beyond the technician level. Pay range for this role is $19.00 to $22.00 per hour, with monthly renewal bonuses and additional recognition programs on top of base compensation. Benefits include a 401(k) match, paid parental leave, PTO, and what the company calls "Wellbeing Days."

job.title: Community Manager Manufactured Housing Community PLUS HOUSING
job.description:
A resident knocks on the office door at 8:15 on a Tuesday morning, frustrated about a neighbor dispute that's been simmering for weeks. By 9:00, you've documented the grievance, reviewed the lease provisions, and scheduled a follow-up. That rhythm, calm, methodical, people-first, is what this role runs on every day.

The Role at Rio Verde Mobile Estates

Investment Property Group, a private firm headquartered in Park City, Utah, that owns and operates over 150 properties across 13 states, is hiring a Community Manager for Rio Verde Mobile Estates, a 55+ manufactured housing community in Auburn, Washington. On-site housing is included: a two-bedroom, two-bath manufactured home with a carport and shed. Living on-site is required. The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 8 to 5, with occasional weekend availability expected.

This is a full operational leadership role. You'll oversee daily property functions, guide staff, manage the application and move-in process, enforce lease agreements and community rules, and serve as the primary point of contact for residents, vendors, local agencies, and law enforcement liaisons. Delinquency management is a real part of the job: you'll review accounts, oversee rent collection, and handle bi-monthly deposits. Budget performance matters here, and you'll be expected to identify operational gaps and recommend improvements that protect NOI and occupancy.

Working with a 55+ demographic adds a layer of relationship complexity that goes beyond standard multifamily community management. Residents here have often lived on-site for years. They know each other. They have expectations about how a community should feel and function. Your ability to hold firm on policy while remaining genuinely approachable will matter as much as your financial acumen.

What the Role Requires

  • At least one year managing a manufactured housing or multifamily community of 100 or more units
  • Hands-on experience with rent collection, delinquency tracking, and basic accounting systems
  • Comfort with property management software
  • Experience hiring, training, and evaluating on-site staff
  • Knowledge of Fair Housing regulations and manufactured housing compliance requirements
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills for resident interaction, vendor coordination, and agency reporting
  • Some marketing and sales aptitude to support lot or home occupancy when vacancies arise

Candidates who stand out tend to be proactive about identifying problems before residents escalate them, and they treat vendor relationships as ongoing partnerships rather than one-off transactions. In a senior community especially, consistency in how you show up matters. Residents notice when a manager is reactive versus when they're genuinely running the property with intention.

From a career standpoint, manufactured housing management builds skills that transfer directly into regional or district roles within MHC portfolios, and the on-site living experience develops the kind of operational instincts that corporate roles often can't replicate. IPG's scale across 13 states means internal mobility is a real possibility for managers who perform.

Compensation ranges from $34.00 to $38.00 per hour depending on experience and qualifications, with benefits that include medical, dental, and vision coverage, life insurance, an HSA, an employee assistance program, 401(k) with company match, and four weeks of accrued PTO.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Makowsky Ringel Greenberg has been a consistent presence in Memphis-area property management for decades, with a portfolio that spans both sides of the state line. This Leasing Consultant role covers two communities in DeSoto County, splitting time between Hernando and Southaven on a structured day-by-day schedule. You'll work one location per day, which keeps the role organized and lets you build genuine familiarity with each property's residents and traffic patterns rather than bouncing between sites mid-shift.

What You'll Actually Do

The core of this position is leasing: converting traffic into signed leases, following up with prospects, and maintaining the kind of resident relationships that support retention and reduce turnover costs. You'll handle the full leasing cycle from initial inquiry through application processing, and you'll represent the community's image in every interaction. Resident relations and administrative duties are part of the daily reality here, not secondary concerns. Saturday availability is required, which reflects the reality that weekend traffic is often when serious prospects show up.

DeSoto County has seen steady population growth driven by proximity to Memphis and relatively affordable cost of living compared to Shelby County. Southaven in particular draws renters who work in the metro but want suburban pricing and school access. That means traffic tends to skew toward practical, value-conscious renters who know the market and do their research. Strong product knowledge and clear communication about value will carry more weight here than high-pressure tactics.

What You Bring

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Two years of leasing or customer service experience preferred
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills
  • Reliable transportation, valid driver's license, and proof of insurance (required given the two-site structure)
  • Ability to pass credit, background, and drug screening

Candidates who tend to thrive in split-site leasing roles are organized and self-directed. When you're the primary leasing presence at a property for the day, you set the tone for how every prospect and resident experiences that community. Waiting for direction doesn't work well here. You need to come in ready to run your day.

Compensation and Benefits

MRG offers a competitive base salary with a commission and bonus program tied to leasing performance. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, short- and long-term disability, company-paid life insurance, and additional group-rate insurance options. The company also provides apartment discounts, paid holidays and PTO, and a 401(k) with a profit-sharing plan. That profit-sharing component is worth noting. It's not standard across all property management companies at this level and suggests the firm has a longer-term orientation toward its employees.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
It's 7:45 AM on a Tuesday. There are four open work orders from overnight, a vacant unit that turns on Friday, and someone just flagged a slow drain in 204. That's usually how this shift starts.

Flats LLC operates lifestyle-driven urban apartment communities in San Diego, and this Maintenance Technician role sits at the center of how their properties actually function day to day. The schedule runs Tuesday through Saturday, which works well for some and takes adjustment for others. Worth knowing going in.

What the Work Looks Like

Make-readies are a consistent part of this role. Vacant units need to hit company standards before a new resident moves in, and that means following a checklist, not approximating one. Beyond turns, you'll run through daily work orders, triaging by urgency and making sure nothing sits longer than it should. Plumbing and paint come up regularly. Exterior grounds, pool upkeep, and seasonal cleanup are part of the rotation too.

Property walk-throughs are on you. When something's off, you document it and move toward correction. Life safety and annual inspections (fire extinguishers, elevators, city-required systems) get scheduled and tracked under this role. When a repair needs an outside contractor, you coordinate that under direction from the Maintenance Supervisor or Property Manager.

On-call is real here. The rotation runs roughly one or two weeks on, one or two weeks off. If that's a dealbreaker, it's better to know now than after your first week.

What They're Looking For

  • At least one year of residential maintenance experience
  • HVAC experience required; certification is a plus
  • Pool maintenance background preferred; CPO certification is a plus
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Comfort with Microsoft Office products
  • Ability to lift up to 100 pounds and work in varying weather conditions
  • Safety-conscious mindset given exposure to mechanical parts, electrical systems, and airborne particles
  • Strong communication skills with residents and team members

Pay runs $28 to $30 per hour. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer match, paid time off, sick leave, and paid holidays.

The technicians who tend to stick and grow in roles like this are the ones who treat the punch list as a floor, not a ceiling. Residents notice when someone fixes the thing they called about and spots the thing they didn't. In a lifestyle-brand operation where resident experience is part of the product, maintenance quality shows up directly in retention numbers. That's not an abstract observation in multifamily. It's just how occupancy works.

job.title: Groundskeeper/Landscaper - Downtown Austin
job.description:
Groundskeeping at a luxury multifamily property calls on a specific mix of horticultural knowledge, mechanical aptitude, and resident-facing professionalism. This part-time role at a Worth Ross Management Company community in Austin's Market/Seaholm District draws on all three, and the balance matters: you're not just mowing and edging. You're maintaining the exterior presentation of a property where residents expect a high-end experience every time they walk through the common areas.

Skills This Role Puts to Work

The core of the job is hands-on landscaping: mowing, edging, mulching, fertilizing, weeding, and caring for flowers, shrubs, and trees. You'll need a real working knowledge of plant health, because identifying pest damage or irrigation issues early keeps small problems from becoming expensive ones. Speaking of irrigation, you'll be expected to monitor and troubleshoot the system, including minor repairs. That mechanical comfort with irrigation and low-voltage wiring separates candidates who can handle the full scope of the role from those who can only handle the visible, surface-level work.

Beyond the green spaces, you'll keep common areas clean and presentable: walkways, garage areas, amenity spaces, and dumpster zones. You'll also assist with light maintenance tasks like painting touch-ups and lighting checks. Residents will see you regularly, so professional, courteous interaction is part of the job, not a side requirement.

What You Bring to the Role

  • Prior groundskeeping or landscaping experience (required)
  • Working knowledge of plants, seasonal care, and gardening methods
  • Comfort with irrigation systems and basic troubleshooting
  • Reliability and a detail-oriented approach to keeping grounds in top condition
  • Strong communication skills with residents, vendors, and team members
  • A high school diploma or equivalent
  • Prior experience in residential facilities is a plus

What This Role Builds

If you're newer to luxury residential work, this position teaches you the standard that Class A communities operate at and what it takes to consistently maintain it. The combination of horticultural care, light maintenance exposure, and daily resident interaction gives you a cross-functional skill set that transfers well into a lead groundskeeper role or a broader maintenance technician track. Working within a company like WRMC, which manages luxury multifamily and HOA properties across multiple markets, also gives you exposure to professional property management processes and expectations that smaller operators often don't emphasize.

The schedule runs 16 to 24 hours per week with flexibility, and the pay range is $21 to $23 per hour. For someone who wants a part-time outdoor role with a professional employer and real craft expectations, this one is worth a close look.

job.title: Housekeeper - Downtown Austin - Market District
job.description:
Worth Ross Management Company runs luxury multifamily and HOA communities with a reputation built on service standards that most properties talk about but few consistently deliver. The Housekeeper role at their Downtown Austin Market District property sits at the center of that reputation. Every lobby presentation, every spotless amenity space, every orderly trash and recycling area either reinforces or undermines what residents paid for when they chose to live there. This position carries that weight directly.

The schedule is specific and worth understanding before you apply. Weekends are fixed: Saturday and Sunday, 7:00 AM to 3:00 PM. Three weekday shifts run midday through early evening, 11:00 AM to 7:00 PM. That midshift window means you're working through peak resident activity, which is different from an early-morning hotel housekeeping role where you're cleaning before guests emerge. You'll be visible, you'll interact with residents and guests regularly, and the quality of those interactions matters as much as the cleanliness of the spaces you're maintaining.

The core of the work covers interior and exterior common areas: lobbies, corridors, amenity spaces, outdoor areas, floors, carpets, and surfaces. You'll also stay alert to anything that needs reporting, whether a maintenance concern, a safety issue, or a cleanliness problem developing in a space you didn't directly clean. That proactive awareness is a skill this role requires from day one.

What the role builds is equally real. Working in a luxury multifamily environment trains your eye for presentation standards that carry directly into hospitality, high-end hotel operations, or senior living facilities. You learn to internalize a quality threshold rather than just follow a checklist, which is what separates housekeeping professionals from people who are just cleaning.

What You Bring

  • Prior housekeeping experience in a luxury residential, hotel, or hospitality setting
  • Attention to detail that holds up across a full shift, not just at the start of the day
  • A service-oriented presence when interacting with residents and guests
  • The ability to work independently and manage your area without constant direction
  • Reliability and consistency, because in a luxury property, one off day is noticeable
  • A high school diploma or equivalent is preferred

Pay runs $18 to $20 per hour. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, short and long-term disability, an employee assistance program, identity theft protection, pet insurance, paid time off, and a 401(k).

job.title: Property Manager
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role puts you in charge of Eagles Eyrie, an 85-plus unit community in Louisville. You'll carry full operational responsibility: budgets, leasing activity, staff supervision, financial reporting, and the day-to-day decisions that keep a property running at its best. Your mornings might start with a maintenance walk, shift into reviewing delinquency with your team, and end with a prospective resident tour. The work isn't siloed. You're the person who connects leasing performance to NOI, maintenance quality to retention, and staff accountability to occupancy outcomes.

Peak Management expects you to manage a team of at least two direct reports, so the leadership piece is real. You'll set the pace, coach performance, and make sure your staff has what they need to execute. Budget preparation and financial reporting are central to the role, not occasional tasks. You'll be expected to read your numbers, explain variances, and make operational decisions that reflect what the ledger is telling you.

What You Bring

  • Minimum five years of direct property management experience in a supervisory capacity
  • Demonstrated ability to lead a staff of two or more people
  • Solid working knowledge of budget preparation, financial reporting, and leasing fundamentals
  • Strong Fair Housing compliance knowledge, applied practically and consistently
  • A valid driver's license and reliable transportation for property-related travel
  • Comfort with physical demands: walking the property in varied weather, navigating stairs, and extended periods at a desk

What This Role Builds and Why It Matters

Candidates who thrive in roles like this one tend to have mastered the balance between people management and financial discipline. The skill that separates strong candidates from capable ones here is the ability to create and preserve value across different phases of a property's life cycle. That means you understand what a lease-up demands differently than a stabilized asset, and you adjust your approach accordingly. If your background is heavy on leasing but light on budgets, or strong on operations but thin on staff leadership, this role will expose those gaps quickly.

On the growth side, site-level property managers who demonstrate clean financial performance and low turnover tend to move into regional or multi-site oversight roles. Peak Management's benefit package includes medical, dental, and life insurance, PTO with a birthday day included, on-call premium pay, a 401(k) with employer matching, and a sign-on bonus for the right hire.

Louisville's rental market has stayed competitive, with Class B communities working harder on retention as newer inventory enters the metro. Strong property managers in this market know that concessions and traffic alone won't protect occupancy. Resident experience and consistent operations do. That's the mindset this role rewards.

job.title: Part Time Leasing Consultant
job.description:
A prospective resident walks in on a Tuesday afternoon having toured three communities that week already. They're comparing floor plans, weighing commute times, and still not sure what they actually want. Your job in that moment is to listen well enough to cut through the noise and match them to the right home.

Village Green is hiring a part-time Leasing Consultant for one of its apartment communities in Columbus, Ohio. The schedule runs two weekdays plus one Saturday each week, which makes this a realistic option for candidates who need flexibility without fully stepping away from a professional sales environment. The base rate is $17.38 per hour, with a commission structure on top of that tied to your leasing performance.

What the Role Involves

This is a resident-facing sales position. You'll handle incoming traffic from prospective residents, qualify their needs quickly, and guide them through the leasing process from initial inquiry to signed lease. Beyond new leases, you'll maintain relationships with current residents and deliver the kind of service that keeps renewals strong. Village Green places meaningful weight on customer experience, so the role carries both a sales expectation and a service standard.

  • Identify prospective residents' needs and match them to available homes
  • Manage follow-up with leads and guide prospects through the decision process
  • Build relationships with current residents to support retention
  • Participate in the commission program tied to leasing results
  • Represent the community professionally during weekend availability

What Village Green Is Looking For

One to two years of sales experience is the baseline. That experience can come from retail, hospitality, or multifamily leasing directly. Candidates with prior apartment leasing background will find the transition straightforward, but strong performers from customer-facing sales roles outside of multifamily often do well here too, since the core skill set transfers cleanly. Proficiency in Microsoft Office is expected. An undergraduate degree is preferred, though relevant experience carries real weight in the evaluation.

Strong verbal and written communication skills are non-negotiable. You'll be writing emails, handling phone inquiries, and having in-person conversations with prospects who are making a significant financial and lifestyle decision. The ability to listen, adjust your approach, and close without being pushy is what separates average leasing consultants from consistently high performers in this type of role.

Columbus is a competitive multifamily market, with steady demand driven by Ohio State, a growing tech and healthcare employment base, and continued in-migration from other Midwest metros. That demand creates real leasing opportunity, but it also means residents have options. Consultants who can articulate what makes a specific community worth choosing, rather than just showing units, tend to perform better here than those relying solely on price comparisons.
