Background check and pre-employment drug screening are required. Village Green participates in E-Verify. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, a bonus program, and a 401(k) with employer match, which is notable for a part-time position.

job.title: Administrative Coordinator - Facilities Operations & Construction
job.description:
This role runs on three skills above all others: systematic documentation, financial tracking discipline, and the ability to keep multiple stakeholders moving without owning the decisions yourself. If those three describe how you naturally work, read on.

What This Role Actually Does

Morguard is a fully integrated real estate company with multifamily assets across North America. This Administrative Coordinator position sits at the center of their facilities, maintenance, and construction operations, supporting a U.S. portfolio from Boynton Beach, FL. The role owns the administrative record for capital and construction projects: scope documents, contracts, purchase orders, change orders, RFIs, submittals, permits, closeout packages, and lien waivers. You're the person who makes sure nothing falls through the cracks between the project owner, accounting, vendors, and property teams.

Day to day, you'll manage project dashboards that flag overdue items, missing documentation, and budget variances. You'll coordinate bid-package logistics, track vendor compliance records (COIs, W-9s, licenses, service agreements), and serve as the administrative contact for national vendor partnerships. Invoice routing, purchase order workflows, and cost tracker reconciliation also land in this role. You won't approve budgets or sign off on change orders. The project owner holds that accountability. Your job is to make sure the right information reaches the right people on time, in a format they can act on.

The financial coordination piece is real. You'll set up and maintain job-cost trackers using approved budgets, commitments, and actuals pulled from company systems, then reconcile those trackers against accounting reports and escalate discrepancies. You'll also prepare recurring cost summaries and variance reports for leadership review. Comfort with numbers and an eye for inconsistency matter here.

Skills This Role Uses Constantly

  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft 365, particularly Excel for tracking and reporting
  • Experience with construction or facilities documentation (RFIs, submittals, closeout packages) is a genuine advantage
  • Accounts payable workflow familiarity, including invoice coding and routing
  • Vendor compliance management: COIs, W-9s, licensing, agreement renewals
  • Strong written communication for internal memos, leadership updates, and cross-department coordination
  • Calendar and travel management for senior facilities and construction leaders

What Sets This Role Apart at Morguard

The scope is portfolio-wide, not site-specific. You're coordinating across multiple properties, Area Service Managers, accounting, risk management, procurement, and construction teams simultaneously. That breadth makes this a strong role for someone who wants deep exposure to capex administration and facilities operations across a large multifamily organization. Coordinators who perform well here tend to develop the kind of cross-functional fluency that translates into senior operations or project management roles over time.

One honest note: this role requires comfort with ambiguity in terms of workload. Portfolio volume shifts, construction timelines slip, and priorities change. The measures of success here are largely about information quality and process discipline, meaning your work shows up in whether records are auditable, whether reports flag the right exceptions, and whether workflows move on schedule. The feedback loop is indirect. That suits some people well and frustrates others. Know which camp you're in before applying.

job.title: Assistant Maintenance Manager
job.description:
Maintenance management at a multifamily property is always a balancing act between reactive work and proactive stewardship. The reactive side gets the attention, but the properties that hold their value and keep residents renewing are the ones where someone is consistently running preventative maintenance programs, catching problems before they become costly, and building a team culture around pride of ownership. That's the environment this role operates in.

The Work Itself

As Assistant Maintenance Manager at a Bozzuto community in Baltimore, you'll carry a full technical load while also developing as a leader. The hands-on side covers the core trades: HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair, along with basic carpentry, drywall, and painting. You'll manage the make-ready and turn process directly, which means owning timeliness and punch list quality so apartments are leased-ready when the leasing team needs them. Beyond turns, you'll run preventative maintenance schedules, handle grounds upkeep, snow removal, and support the on-call emergency rotation on a shared basis.

The supervisory piece is equally real. You're not just completing tickets yourself. You're modeling the standard for how work gets done and how residents get treated, which means following up on service requests, checking completed work, and keeping the team focused on the details that protect the asset's value long-term. Bozzuto properties include complex mechanical systems (central plant, split systems, boilers, chillers), so comfort with those systems is a genuine plus, not just a credential line.

What the Role Requires vs. What It Builds

Coming in, you'll need:

  • 5 or more years in the trades, facilities, or residential building maintenance
  • Demonstrated proficiency across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair
  • An HVAC, EPA, or NAPE certification
  • Working knowledge of OSHA standards, risk management protocols, and MSDS
  • A safety-first mindset with genuine attention to detail
  • Supervisory experience or strong leadership aptitude
  • Physical capability to frequently exert 25 to 50 pounds of force, work at height, climb stairs, and operate in variable weather

What this role actively builds is the management side of the craft. Coordinating a team's daily workflow, prioritizing competing maintenance demands, and communicating clearly with residents and property leadership are skills that compound over time. Assistant Maintenance Managers who execute well at this level tend to move into Maintenance Manager roles and, at larger properties, into Regional Facilities positions where portfolio-wide asset oversight becomes the focus.

One honest note: on-call rotations are part of the job. Emergency calls happen outside business hours, and this role shares that responsibility. Candidates who thrive here treat on-call as a natural part of property stewardship rather than an inconvenience. That mindset, more than any single certification, tends to separate strong candidates from average ones at this level.

Compensation for this position ranges from $62,000 to $65,000 annually, with bonus eligibility. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
Lincoln Property Company runs one of the larger third-party commercial management platforms in the country, and this Assistant Property Manager role sits inside that machine at the property level in Dallas. At a firm managing north of 720 million square feet across office, retail, industrial, and beyond, the APM position is where you learn how institutional-grade management actually gets executed day to day.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

A good chunk of this role lives in the financial and administrative layer of commercial property management. You'll support the Property Manager on monthly reporting packages, help draft CAM reconciliations in coordination with accounting, and review vendor invoices against the management agreement and authorization thresholds. Lease administration is a real part of this job too: setting up leases in the system, processing changes, and keeping reporting accurate across platforms. On the operational side, you'll coordinate tenant move-ins and move-outs, participate in walk-throughs, and help maintain vendor relationships through bidding and procurement support. This position is 100% in-office and includes regular property inspections and travel to assigned sites.

Lincoln is also clear that this role carries some supervisory responsibility. If you have direct reports, you're expected to give real direction and manage performance, not just pass along tasks from above.

What Lincoln Is Looking For

  • Bachelor's degree preferred, or equivalent combination of education and experience; 1-2 years of relevant commercial property management experience
  • Comfortable with AP systems and CMMS platforms
  • Intermediate to advanced Microsoft Office skills
  • Ability to work through financial calculations: percentages, proration, basic analysis
  • Strong written and verbal communication, particularly with tenants and ownership
  • Organized enough to keep reporting deadlines and lease administration tasks from piling up
  • Must be authorized to work in the U.S. without sponsorship, now or in the future

Where This Role Tends to Lead

The APM seat at a firm like Lincoln is a known path to Property Manager. CAM rec experience, vendor management, and ownership reporting are the core skills that hiring managers look for when promoting into full PM responsibilities on commercial assets. Candidates who distinguish themselves here usually have two things in common: they understand the financials well enough to catch errors before the PM does, and they can handle tenant communication without escalating every issue. Institutional clients expect clean reporting and low friction. If you can deliver both, this role builds a resume that opens doors across commercial property types.

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k) with traditional and Roth options, flexible time off, paid sick leave, and company-paid life insurance and long-term disability.

job.title: Business Manager - Avenue 25
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

The Business Manager at Avenue 25 runs the property. That's the honest summary. You're accountable for financial performance, team development, occupancy, and the physical condition of the asset, all at once. On any given week, you might be reviewing T-12 financials with your Regional VP in the morning, walking units for make-ready inspections after lunch, and sitting across from a vendor to negotiate a service contract before the day ends. Resident retention programs, renewal strategies, leasing traffic, and marketing budgets all land on your desk. So do the people questions: coaching an office associate through a tough conversation, redirecting a maintenance tech who's cutting corners on a punch list, or jumping in personally when an after-hours situation needs a calm hand in charge.

You'll build the annual asset business plan and own the budget forecasts that come from it. Monthly, you'll analyze performance against projections and bring a point of view to those conversations with regional leadership, not just numbers, but context and strategy. Vendor bids, one-time project oversight, and ensuring the amenity spaces and common areas stay in market-ready condition are also part of your regular rhythm.

What You Bring

  • At least two years of hands-on property manager experience in multifamily. Luxury or Class A experience is genuinely preferred here, not just a nice-to-have.
  • Familiarity with RealPage, Knock, or Onesite. Avenue 25 moves fast and these tools are already embedded in daily operations.
  • Comfort reading and presenting financial reports. You don't need to be an accountant, but you do need to understand what the numbers are telling you.
  • Full-time availability Monday through Friday, with real flexibility for resident events and the occasional emergency outside business hours.
  • A steady presence under pressure. This role has a lot of moving parts, and the team needs a manager who stays organized when things pile up.

The Team and Culture Context

Olympus Property has been recognized by the National Apartment Association as a top employer three years running, which reflects something genuine about how they operate internally. The "family-oriented" language in their materials can read as corporate noise, but the structure here backs it up: there are dedicated leadership conferences, career pathing programs, and what they call Budget Camp, actual hands-on training for managers around financial planning. For a Business Manager who wants to grow toward a Regional Manager role, that kind of investment in skill-building matters more than the phrase on the website.

One honest note: this role carries real authority and real accountability simultaneously. You're managing a team while also being managed to specific asset goals. The candidates who do well here tend to be people who genuinely enjoy mentoring others and who don't compartmentalize "people work" as separate from "performance work." At a Class A property in Phoenix's competitive multifamily market, resident experience directly affects renewals, and renewals directly affect NOI. Strong Business Managers here understand that connection intuitively and build their teams around it.

Compensation ranges from $72,000 to $76,000 annually, with monthly commissions and quarterly and annual bonus eligibility on top of that base.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Skills This Role Runs On

This position at The Bowery at Southside runs on communication, sales follow-through, and the ability to shift gears fast. You'll spend a large part of your day talking to people: prospective residents touring units, current residents with concerns, and teammates coordinating the day's priorities. Strong verbal and written communication aren't just nice to have here. They're the engine of the job.

Weinstein Properties is straightforward about what they want: someone without leasing experience is fine, but someone without drive isn't. The team is specifically seeking a candidate with some leadership or management background who can move toward Assistant Manager level. If you've supervised people, run a shift, managed a team, or owned outcomes in a service environment, that background applies here more directly than you might expect.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

The days have a rhythm, but interruptions are part of that rhythm. You'll greet walk-ins, take calls, process applications, inspect units, and respond to resident questions, sometimes all before lunch. The administrative side of the role is real: paperwork, follow-ups, and keeping files accurate matter as much as closing a lease.

This isn't a role where you sit at a desk and wait for leads. You'll walk the property, check on unit readiness, and pitch in on tasks outside your core responsibilities when the team needs it. Weinstein operates with a hands-on culture from the top down, and that expectation extends to everyone on site. Resident events and occasional off-schedule hours come with the territory.

Schedule runs weekdays 9 to 6, Saturdays 9 to 5 on a rotating basis with your team, and Sundays off. Starting pay is $19 per hour with quarterly bonuses on top.

Why This Role at Weinstein

Weinstein Properties has been family-owned for over 70 years, with a portfolio of more than 60 communities across Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia. That ownership structure tends to produce more consistency in culture and training than you'd find at a larger institutional operator. They've built a reputation for promoting from within, and this posting is a direct signal of that: they're looking for someone with growth potential, not just someone to fill a leasing seat.

The skills you build here transfer well. Leasing consultants who move up in property management typically develop the resident relations experience needed for Assistant Manager roles, where the work shifts toward collections, delinquency oversight, and light financial reporting. Starting in leasing and being explicitly positioned for upward movement is a practical entry point into a full property management career.

  • Starting pay: $19/hour, increasing with experience
  • Quarterly bonus structure
  • Rotating Saturday schedule (not every week)
  • Training program provided, prior leasing experience not required
  • Management experience and career ambition are the real differentiators here

job.title: HOA General Manager - Houston, TX
job.description:
The board meeting wrapped at 8:45 PM. By 9:00, you're walking the lobby with the engineering lead, reviewing the punch list from last week's elevator modernization. By 9:15, you've drafted a follow-up to the homeowners about the timeline. That's the rhythm of high-rise HOA management, and it's exactly what this role demands.

The Role

Action Property Management, founded in 1984 and now the largest privately owned HOA management company in the West, is hiring an onsite General Manager for a high-rise community in Houston. With over 300 communities and nine regional offices, Action operates at a scale where process and culture both matter. This GM position sits at the center of daily operations: staff leadership, vendor oversight, budget management, and direct service to homeowners.

You'll own the full operational picture. That means managing the annual budget cycle from draft through board approval, tracking actuals against projections, and understanding reserve study outputs well enough to explain them clearly to a board that may not have a finance background. Audit preparation, bidding processes, and governing document compliance are part of the core work, not the occasional exception.

Leadership here is real. You'll hire, train, and hold accountable an onsite team. In a high-rise, that team typically spans front desk, maintenance, and concierge-adjacent functions. Staff turnover in high-rises is one of the most visible operational failures a GM can have, because residents notice it immediately. Retention starts with how you hire and how you train.

What You Bring

  • Two to five years of onsite HOA high-rise General Manager experience
  • CMCA certification, or the ability to obtain it within six months of hire
  • Solid understanding of HOA budgets, reserve studies, audits, and the vendor bidding process
  • Familiarity with association governing documents (CC&Rs, bylaws, rules and regulations)
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present to boards confidently
  • Independent time management: this role requires you to prioritize without being told what matters first
  • A track record of following through on homeowner and board issues without letting things fall

The CMCA requirement is worth noting for candidates coming from conventional multifamily backgrounds. HOA governance operates under a different legal and operational framework than apartment management. Board dynamics, voting thresholds, assessment collection rules, and fiduciary responsibilities to homeowners all create a distinct environment. Candidates with strong multifamily ops experience who lack direct HOA exposure should plan for a steeper ramp-up than the title might suggest.

Action offers a full benefits package including medical, dental, vision, pet insurance, a 401(k) with company match, life and disability coverage, and paid time off including vacation, sick time, and company holidays, all for qualifying team members.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
Managing a Manufactured Home Community in Northern Colorado

Manufactured housing has moved to the center of the affordable housing conversation, and operators like Havenpark Communities are growing fast to meet demand. With 100+ communities and 30,000+ homesites across the country, Havenpark runs a national operation, but the real work happens at the community level. In Berthoud, a small town on the northern Front Range that sits between Longmont and Fort Collins, this 134-home community needs someone who can own every part of that operation day to day.

This is genuinely a general management role. You'll carry the budget, drive collections and delinquency, manage leasing and occupancy, oversee vendors, and lead a small on-site team. The decisions that shape resident experience, community appearance, and financial performance all flow through you. You don't hand things up the chain and wait. You own the outcome.

What This Role Actually Requires

Havenpark values five things internally: Respect, Grit, Collaboration, Stewardship, and Boldness. The Community Manager position is where those values get tested every day, not stated in a meeting. A few specifics on what competence looks like here:

  • Budget ownership and financial accountability across a 134-homesite community
  • Collections management, including working delinquency with empathy and firmness
  • Leasing and occupancy, keeping the community full and moving vacant homes quickly
  • Vendor coordination for maintenance, landscaping, and capital work
  • On-site team leadership and day-to-day operational decisions
  • Resident relations across a diverse, working-class community

Strong candidates here understand that manufactured home communities operate differently from conventional apartment assets. Residents typically own their homes and lease the land beneath them. That shapes every conversation you'll have about rent, rules, and rights. The manager who thrives in this environment reads their community the way a small-town mayor reads a neighborhood: by being present, being consistent, and being reachable.

Berthoud has grown quickly as housing pressure from the Denver metro has pushed renters and buyers north. Manufactured housing in this part of Colorado serves families who can't access the conventional market, which means the work here carries real social weight. Managers who treat that lightly don't last. Managers who take it seriously build communities that retain residents year after year, and that's what Havenpark is building toward.

job.title: International Community Ambassador
job.description:
A new international student arrives in August, jet-lagged and unsure where to pay rent or how to get a bus pass. You're the first person they talk to who actually understands both what they're asking and why it's hard to ask.

The International Community Ambassador role at The Carmin in Tempe sits at the intersection of student housing operations and cross-cultural community building. PeakMade Real Estate manages off-campus student communities across the country, and The Carmin serves a significant international student population at Arizona State University. This position is the connective tissue between that population and the broader community: part leasing support, part programming coordinator, part resident advocate.

What This Role Actually Covers

Day to day, you'll communicate with residents and prospects in both Mandarin and English, explaining lease terms, rent obligations, and community policies accurately in both languages. That precision matters. Misunderstood lease terms drive delinquency and dissatisfaction; clear communication up front prevents both. You'll support the leasing team by attracting and converting international student prospects, working leads in person, by phone, and online.

Beyond leasing, you'll plan and execute weekly and monthly cultural programming, onsite and in the surrounding Tempe community. You'll coordinate welcome efforts for the major August and January move-ins and manage farewell logistics during the December and May/July turns. You'll also build relationships with ASU offices and student organizations, including International Student and Scholar Services, the Chinese Students and Scholars Association, and the Indian Students Association, partnering on events and keeping a presence where international students already gather.

What You'll Need Coming In

  • Fluency in Mandarin and English (speaking, reading, and writing) is required, not preferred
  • Current full-time enrollment in a degree program, or a completed bachelor's degree
  • Prior leadership experience: student organizations, resident life, peer mentoring, or comparable roles
  • Strong organizational and interpersonal skills, with a genuine ability to engage diverse populations
  • Cultural awareness and experience in multicultural or international settings
  • Availability for evenings and weekends, particularly around major move-in and move-out periods
  • Familiarity with fair housing standards, or the ability to learn them quickly

The skills this role builds are worth naming directly. You'll develop real leasing experience alongside the community management and programming skills that carry well into Resident Services Manager or Assistant Community Manager positions. Bilingual leasing professionals with cultural programming backgrounds are genuinely scarce in student housing, and the experience here translates directly to those next steps.

Strong candidates will bring more than language fluency. The students who thrive in this role tend to understand the specific friction points of being a first-year international student at a large American university, because they've lived some version of it themselves. That lived context shapes programming that actually draws residents, and conversations that build real trust.

job.title: Property Manager
job.description:
Peak Management is adding a Property Manager to lead a soon-to-be-acquired community in Milwaukee, and the timing matters. Taking over a new acquisition means setting the operational tone early: stabilizing occupancy, building resident relationships from scratch, and making sure the property performs the way underwriting expects it to. That's a different challenge than stepping into a turnkey asset, and it suits a certain kind of operator.

This is a 400-plus unit community, so the scale requires someone comfortable managing a small staff while also staying close to the numbers. Budget prep, financial reporting, leasing performance, and delinquency management all need to live in your head at the same time. Peak is looking for a minimum of five years in a property manager seat, with direct experience supervising at least two people. Fair Housing fluency is a baseline expectation, not a bonus.

Milwaukee's rental market has stayed relatively affordable compared to Midwestern peers like Minneapolis or Chicago, but that doesn't mean operators have had an easy run. Renter demand has been uneven across submarkets, and class B and C properties have faced real pressure on collections and concession management over the past few years. Someone who has managed through that kind of environment, kept occupancy steady, and still delivered NOI results will translate well here.

What separates strong candidates for an acquisition lease-up or stabilization role like this is the ability to read a T-12 critically and identify where the previous ownership left money on the table, whether through deferred maintenance, weak renewal pricing, or bloated vendor contracts. Candidates who bring that analytical lens alongside people skills tend to hit the ground faster and earn the confidence of ownership earlier.

What Peak is Looking For

  • Five or more years managing a multifamily property at scale
  • Demonstrated experience supervising leasing or maintenance staff
  • Hands-on budget preparation and financial reporting experience
  • Solid working knowledge of Fair Housing regulations
  • Strong leasing and operations fundamentals
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation

Peak Management offers medical, dental, and life insurance, PTO including your birthday, on-call premium pay, a 401(k) with employer matching, and a sign-on bonus. The company's core values lean hard into accountability and optimism, so if you tend toward drama or blame-shifting, this culture probably isn't the right fit. If you're the kind of manager who walks in on day one ready to assess, prioritize, and build, this role has real runway.

job.title: Regional Property Manager - Multi-Family Properties
job.description:
Regional Oversight With Real Operational Weight

Regional roles in multi-family management tend to fall into two categories: glorified troubleshooters who spend their days putting out fires, and genuine portfolio stewards who drive NOI with intention. CYM Living is building toward the latter. This is a vertically integrated firm headquartered in Chicago with deep roots in real estate investment, and they want a Regional Property Manager in Indianapolis who can own the full picture across a portfolio of multi-family communities.

The scope here is what you'd expect from a serious regional position. You'll be accountable for occupancy, revenue, and NOI performance across multiple properties, with regular site inspections, financial reviews, and variance analysis built into your rhythm. Budget ownership is real: you'll develop annual operating budgets, track month-over-month performance against those budgets, and bring a point of view on where expenses can be tightened without sacrificing asset condition. Delinquency and bad debt are yours to monitor and manage. Capital projects, renovations, and property transitions fall under your coordination as well.

On the people side, you'll recruit and develop Community Managers and support staff, run performance evaluations, and contribute to succession planning. CYM's stated emphasis on internal growth means the expectation is that you're building a bench, not just filling slots. Escalated resident issues and compliance matters, from fair housing to local landlord-tenant law, land on your desk when site teams need backup.

What the Role Actually Requires

  • 5 to 7+ years of progressive multi-family property management experience, with at least 3 years in a multi-site or regional capacity
  • Demonstrated track record managing budgets and hitting NOI targets
  • Working knowledge of fair housing regulations and applicable landlord-tenant law
  • Proficiency with property management software (Yardi, AppFolio, RealPage, Entrata, OneSite, or comparable platforms)
  • Valid driver's license and comfort with regular regional travel between properties
  • Bachelor's degree in a related field, or equivalent professional experience

What Separates Strong Candidates

The candidates who perform well in regional roles like this one have usually spent real time on-site before moving up. They know what a well-run make-ready program looks like, they can read a T-12 without needing someone to walk them through it, and they've personally coached a struggling Community Manager back to competency instead of just replacing them. Financial fluency matters here, but so does the credibility that comes from having actually managed a lease-up or worked through a difficult occupancy recovery. Indianapolis has a competitive mid-market multi-family environment with a mix of garden-style and mid-rise product, so familiarity with that asset class and price point will serve you well.

CYM Living's model combines data-driven decision making with what they describe as hyperlocal customer service, which in practice means the Regional Manager needs to be comfortable pulling performance reports and interpreting traffic trends, while also staying connected enough to individual communities that resident satisfaction doesn't slip through the cracks. It's a balance that takes experience to hold well.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance- Royal Oaks Apartments
job.description:
Banyan Living runs Royal Oaks as a luxury apartment community in North Royalton, Ohio. This Maintenance Technician position covers the full scope of day-to-day property upkeep: service requests, preventative maintenance, make-readies on vacant units, and building system repairs.

What the Work Looks Like

Your days split between scheduled work and reactive work. On the scheduled side, you're running preventative maintenance on building systems, inspecting equipment, and prepping turns so units are ready for incoming residents. On the reactive side, you're handling resident service requests across plumbing, electrical, and appliances, and you need to move on them promptly. Documentation matters here too. You'll track completed work and manage supply inventory so nothing falls through the cracks.

You'll work directly with the property management team. When an issue escalates or needs coordination, they need someone who communicates clearly and doesn't leave problems open longer than necessary.

What You Need

  • At least one year of maintenance or related hands-on experience
  • Working knowledge of plumbing, electrical systems, and general repairs
  • Strong troubleshooting skills and a customer-service mindset when dealing with residents
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • Ability to lift up to 50 pounds and handle physical work throughout the shift
  • Availability for on-call and emergency coverage
  • High school diploma or equivalent; technical certifications are a plus

Compensation and Benefits

Pay is bi-weekly. Benefits include medical, vision, dental, short and long-term disability, life insurance, and an employee assistance program. You also get paid holidays, PTO, and a 401(k). If you live on-site, there's a 35% rent discount.

One thing worth knowing: make-ready quality directly shapes the first impression a new resident gets. Technicians who treat turns with the same attention they give emergency calls tend to build stronger reputations within the property team, and that visibility often leads to lead tech or facilities coordinator roles as a company grows its portfolio.

job.title: Maintenance Service Manager
job.description:
Condominium maintenance management sits in its own category. You're not running a leasing operation, you're running a building, and the residents who own their units have high expectations and a direct financial stake in how well systems are maintained. When the boiler goes down in January or the fire suppression system throws a fault, the property manager's first call goes to the Maintenance Service Manager.

Taylor Management Company is hiring for that role at a condominium property in Summit, New Jersey. A valid New Jersey Black Seal Boiler Operator License is required before you apply. That's non-negotiable here, and it narrows the candidate pool considerably.

What the Job Actually Covers

This is a full-scope building systems role with a supervisory layer on top. Day-to-day, you're overseeing HVAC, boilers, plumbing, electrical, fire protection, and life safety systems, coordinating both reactive repairs and a structured preventive maintenance program. You'll also manage and schedule the maintenance staff, which means you're accountable for their work quality, their training, and how they interact with residents.

Resident-facing communication matters here. Condo owners are not renters, and they'll let you know it. Responding to service requests and emergencies with professionalism and follow-through is part of the job as much as any mechanical skill. You'll maintain records, track compliance, and handle the administrative side with basic proficiency in Microsoft Office and whatever maintenance management technology the property uses.

On-call coverage is real. Nights, weekends, holidays when systems don't care about your schedule.

What You Need Coming In

  • Valid New Jersey Black Seal Boiler Operator License
  • At least five years of commercial or residential building maintenance experience
  • Minimum three years in a supervisory capacity
  • Working knowledge of HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and life safety systems
  • Familiarity with OSHA standards and safe work practices
  • Basic carpentry, drywall, and painting skills (useful for unit turns and punch list items)
  • Valid driver's license with a clean record
  • Ability to lift 50 pounds, work on ladders, and handle outdoor work in all weather
  • High school diploma or equivalent; trade or technical school background preferred

The candidates who stand out in roles like this are the ones who can troubleshoot a mechanical problem and then clearly explain what happened and what was done to fix it, to both their staff and to a condo owner who's standing in the hallway asking questions. Technical skill gets you in the door; communication keeps the property running smoothly. Additional bonus opportunities are available beyond base compensation.

job.title: Make Ready Technician/Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Lynco Properties is hiring full-time maintenance and make-ready technicians for their apartment communities in Lawton, Oklahoma. Pay runs $18 to $21 per hour depending on what you bring to the table, and the role comes with health, dental, and vision insurance, 401(k), and paid time off.

The work is split between two lanes: make-readys and general maintenance. On the make-ready side, you're turning vacant units for move-in. That means painting, swapping out fixtures, replacing appliances, addressing plumbing, and working through the punch list until the apartment is genuinely ready to lease. You'll pull from the make-ready board and coordinate with the property manager on priorities and timing.

Day-to-day maintenance covers work orders in occupied units, grounds upkeep, common areas, and amenities. You'll also handle scheduled preventive tasks on a weekly, monthly, and quarterly basis. Material and supply orders go through the property manager for approval, so you'll need to communicate proactively when inventory is running low.

On-call rotation is part of the job. Weekend availability is required. If that's a dealbreaker, this role isn't the right fit.

One thing that separates solid candidates here: the ability to self-manage across both types of work without needing constant direction. Make-readys have a rhythm, but occupied-unit repairs are unpredictable. The techs who perform well can switch gears, work cleanly inside residents' homes, and keep a unit's timeline on track without letting work orders stack up.

What you'll need

  • At least one year of property maintenance experience
  • Your own tools
  • Reliable transportation
  • Working knowledge of painting, basic plumbing, appliance repair, and fixture replacement
  • Ability to work on-call and weekends
  • Dependable, team-oriented, and motivated to work without close supervision

Experience with HVAC, electrical, or other skilled trades will likely put you at the higher end of the pay range. Apply with a clear picture of your hands-on background.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Manager - Farrington Midtown
job.description:
It's 7:30 on a Tuesday morning at Farrington Midtown and you've already got two work orders from overnight, a vendor running late on a make-ready, and a resident calling about a water heater. That's a normal Tuesday.

AIR Communities is hiring a Maintenance Manager for Farrington Midtown, a mid-rise apartment community in Atlanta's Midtown submarket. The compensation sits between $85,000 and $90,000 annually, with a 15% target bonus and quarterly customer service bonuses that can add up to $250 per month when resident satisfaction scores reflect it. An on-site apartment discount is also available for the right candidate.

What the Role Covers

This is a working leadership position. You'll oversee a maintenance team while staying involved in the day-to-day yourself. The scope includes apartment turns and make-readies, resident service requests, preventative maintenance scheduling, vendor coordination, and Environmental Health and Safety compliance. You'll also track capital needs and communicate them up to property leadership, and you'll manage your portion of the maintenance budget with an eye on both cost control and quality. AIR uses technology-forward maintenance systems, so comfort adapting to digital work order platforms matters here.

On-call responsibility is real in this role. Expect at least one week per month on rotation, plus occasional evenings and weekends based on community needs and seasonal demand. That's worth knowing upfront.

What AIR Is Looking For

  • At least 3 years of hands-on technical maintenance and facilities experience in residential property management
  • 1 to 3 years leading a maintenance or customer service team
  • Strong mechanical aptitude with a practical, solution-focused approach to problems
  • Ability to handle physical demands of the job, including moving heavy equipment
  • Reliable transportation
  • Flexibility for evenings, weekends, and on-call shifts
  • English proficiency (read, write, speak)

The candidates who tend to do well in roles like this aren't just technically skilled. They know how to prioritize a full punch list when everything feels urgent, keep a team's morale steady during a heavy turn season, and still make individual residents feel like their service request matters. That combination is harder to find than it sounds.

AIR Communities offers a full benefits package including medical, dental, vision, and life insurance, company-paid short and long-term disability, a 401(k) with up to 6% employer match, up to 16 weeks of paid parental leave, tuition assistance, and 100% reimbursement for job-related certifications and licenses. The certification coverage is worth noting for anyone working toward HVAC, EPA 608, or similar credentials.

Applications are accepted through October 15, 2026, with earlier submissions reviewed first. Pre-employment screening includes reference checks, a four-panel drug screen (marijuana excluded), employment verification, and a background check.

job.title: Lead Maintenance Technician (Villages)
job.description:
What This Role Covers at Prometheus

Prometheus Real Estate Group operates a substantial portfolio of communities across the Bay Area, and their Cupertino properties sit in one of the most competitive rental markets in California. The Lead Maintenance Technician role here carries more operational weight than a standard tech position. You're responsible for the full scope of unit turns and make-readies, troubleshooting major mechanical systems, and keeping the day-to-day maintenance rhythm moving across the community. You also help coordinate vendor scheduling, track maintenance-related costs, and handle administrative work tied to those activities. Yardi proficiency matters here because work order management is part of the job, not an afterthought.

The "Lead" designation means you're mentoring and directing a team, setting the standard on how work gets done and how residents get treated. That combination, technical execution plus team leadership, is what separates this from a senior tech position. You're expected to already know plumbing, electrical, carpentry, painting, and appliance repairs at a working level and to carry at least one year of supervisory experience. Prometheus prefers two or more years in that lead capacity.

What the Day Actually Looks Like

Mornings likely involve reviewing open work orders, triaging what the team handles in-house versus what needs a vendor, and checking the punch list on any units in turn. A good chunk of your week will shift depending on vacancy levels: when occupancy dips and turns pile up, the make-ready pipeline becomes your priority. When the property runs tight, resident service calls and preventive work move to the front. On-call rotation is part of this position, including weekends, so the role asks for real availability, not theoretical flexibility.

Compensation runs $38.00 to $39.25 per hour, with standby and on-call premium pay on top of that base. Prometheus also offers a discretionary semi-annual bonus plan, referral bonuses, a renovation bonus, and a lease-up bonus when applicable. Benefits include 100% company-paid medical, vision, and dental coverage for eligible employees and dependents, 401(k) with employer matching, and tenure-based housing discounts, which carries real value in a market like Cupertino.

Where This Role Can Take You

Leads who build strong track records here tend to move toward Maintenance Supervisor and eventually Maintenance Manager roles as portfolios scale. The skill set you sharpen here, budget accountability, vendor coordination, team development, and technical breadth, transfers directly into those positions. Prometheus also offers tuition reimbursement and educational assistance, which means you can pursue additional certifications while working. If your goal is to move into a property-wide or regional maintenance leadership role over the next few years, a lead position at a company with an established portfolio is one of the cleaner paths to get there.

  • High school diploma or GED required, plus a minimum of three maintenance-related certificates (BOMA, IREM, or vocational equivalents)
  • Three to four years of apartment maintenance experience
  • At least one year of supervisory experience (two or more preferred)
  • Working knowledge of Yardi or comparable work order platforms
  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs. and work in both indoor and outdoor conditions
  • On-call and weekend availability required

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
Community managers at stabilized conventional properties carry a deceptively broad mandate. Occupancy, NOI, team culture, resident retention, vendor oversight, and ownership reporting all land on the same desk. At a company the size of Hawthorne Residential Partners, one of the larger Southeast-based multifamily operators in the country, the expectation is that the person running a community functions as a general manager, not just a leasing lead with an elevated title.

Meridian at North Hills sits in one of Raleigh's most competitive submarkets. North Hills has absorbed significant Class A and B supply over the past several years, which means renewal strategy and resident retention carry real weight here. Strong occupancy at this location requires more than traffic. It requires a manager who understands pricing, concessions, and what keeps a resident from going MTM or not renewing at all.

What the Role Actually Covers

Hawthorne describes this as a coach, culture ambassador, and business strategist position, and that framing is accurate. You'll own budget management, delinquency tracking, deposit accounting, and financial reporting. You'll run leasing alongside your team, including tours and lead follow-up, while also driving renewal conversion and monitoring occupancy targets. Vendor relationships, work order oversight with maintenance, and regular property inspections are part of the weekly rhythm. Resident escalations, online review responses, and resident event planning round out the community-facing side of the role. Yardi and Knock are the primary platforms in use.

Team leadership here means hiring, training, and holding accountability for both office and maintenance staff. Weekly team meetings, performance coaching, and connecting individual development to Hawthorne's internal career path program are all expectations of the role.

  • Two years of property management experience required, including time as a Leasing Consultant and Assistant Community Manager
  • Six months of community manager experience in multifamily, highly preferred
  • Yardi, Knock, and Microsoft Office familiarity preferred
  • CAM, CAPS, real estate license, or property management license preferred
  • Valid driver's license required
  • High school diploma or GED required

What Separates Strong Candidates

The managers who perform well in roles like this read a T-12 the same way they read a punch list. They spot delinquency trends before they compound, and they understand how a single bad renewal month affects NOI at the end of the quarter. Financial fluency isn't a bonus here. It's woven into the day-to-day. The other differentiator is genuine investment in team development. In a market like Raleigh, where leasing talent turns frequently, a manager who builds a team people want to stay on creates a compounding retention advantage. Hawthorne's internal career path program, which maps a trajectory from Community Manager toward Regional Manager, signals that the company rewards managers who develop their people rather than simply covering for turnover.

Office hours run Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, and Saturday 10 AM to 4 PM, with one weekday off to keep the schedule at 40 hours. Some evenings and weekends may come up for resident events. Compensation includes base salary plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, paid time off, paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, and company-paid life insurance.

job.title: Affordable Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Maintenance technicians who build their careers at affordable housing properties tend to develop a range of skills that specialists in other sectors simply don't get. At Brockton Commons, you'll touch electrical, mechanical, cosmetic, and life-safety work on a regular basis. That breadth is worth something, both now and down the road.

The Skills This Role Puts to Work

John M. Corcoran and Company has been operating New England residential communities since 1951, and the maintenance function at their Brockton Commons property reflects that institutional depth. Day to day, this role calls on a wide technical range: appliance repairs, smoke detector installations, light fixture work, door hardware, tile, locks, handrails, window replacements, and painting. That last category matters more than it sounds. Cosmetic readiness directly affects resident satisfaction and, in affordable housing, regulatory compliance during inspections. Technicians who treat make-ready quality as seriously as mechanical repairs tend to stand out quickly.

You'll also coordinate with outside contractors and track paperwork tied to your work orders. That combination of hands-on repair and basic administrative accountability is where a lot of technicians start building the habits that lead to lead tech or facilities supervisor roles.

What the Day Actually Looks Like

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., with an on-call rotation for emergencies. In practice, that means your core hours are structured, but you need to stay mentally ready for flood response, urgent safety calls, or back-to-back move-ins that compress your punch list. Affordable properties carry full occupancy pressure, so turns need to happen efficiently without cutting corners on habitability standards.

The position requires at least six months of trade or building maintenance experience, and a background in plumbing, electrical, HVAC, or roofing will strengthen your candidacy. The pay range runs from $29 to $33 per hour depending on experience, and JMC is offering a $2,500 sign-on bonus for this opening.

What This Role Builds Toward

Technicians who come up through affordable housing learn to manage high unit counts, navigate contractor relationships, and maintain documentation under HUD or state agency scrutiny. Those skills transfer directly into lead maintenance, facilities management, or property operations roles. JMC's track record of long-tenured employees suggests the company tends to promote from within rather than hire externally for senior positions, which makes early investment in relationships and reputation worth the effort.

  • Minimum six months of trade or building maintenance experience
  • Working knowledge of electrical and mechanical systems
  • Comfort identifying and correcting safety hazards
  • Specialized trade experience (plumbing, electrical, HVAC, or roofing) is a plus
  • Willingness to participate in on-call rotation

Benefits include medical, dental, vision, and life insurance, paid time off, holidays, and a 401(k) with company match.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Manager
job.description:
Maintenance managers at affordable housing portfolios wear a lot of hats. On any given day, you might be walking units to build a punch list, coordinating a vendor for a boiler repair, or coaching a technician through a task they haven't handled before. At Fairstead, this role sits at the center of all of that, and the expectation is that you can lead from the front, not just direct from an office.

What This Role Actually Involves

Fairstead's Champaign property needs someone who can supervise a maintenance team while still getting hands-on when the situation calls for it. You'll oversee the repair and upkeep of building systems, electrical equipment, and mechanical components, making sure inspections happen on schedule and that the property stays clean, safe, and code-compliant. Special projects will pull you into a leadership position, and some of them will require overtime. That's worth naming honestly up front.

Day-to-day, you'll balance reactive work (emergencies happen in any residential setting) with planned maintenance, and you'll need the organizational discipline to keep both tracks moving without letting one swallow the other. Yardi experience is a plus here, and Fairstead does lean into tech and data tools more than a typical affordable housing operator, so comfort with systems matters.

Core qualifications include:

  • At least three years of property maintenance experience, with depth in at least one trade
  • Solid working knowledge of building and mechanical systems, tools, and safety protocols
  • Experience supervising or mentoring other maintenance staff
  • The ability to implement and refine maintenance policies and procedures
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite; Yardi knowledge is a plus

The People Side of This Job

A maintenance manager in affordable housing interacts with a wider range of people than many comparable roles. Residents often have fewer options and higher stakes when something goes wrong in their unit. That context shapes how good managers in this space communicate, follow through, and prioritize. The best candidates here aren't just technically sharp. They're consistent, calm under pressure, and clear with both their team and the residents they serve.

You'll also work alongside a property management team and, periodically, with Fairstead's broader platform, which spans development and construction as well as operations. That integrated structure means decisions get made with more context than they would at a purely third-party management shop, and it tends to give on-site leaders a clearer line of sight into why things are being done the way they are.

Compensation and Benefits

The salary range for this position runs from $27 to $29 per hour, depending on skills, experience, and location. Fairstead offers a benefits package that includes medical coverage through Meritain Health with a generous employer contribution, employer-paid vision and life insurance, a 401(k) with company matching (100% on the first 3%, 50% on the next 2%), 15 days of PTO, 7 sick days, 12 or more paid holidays, and a flexible spending account. Pet insurance, disability coverage, and employee discount programs round out the package.

For someone with a strong trade background who's ready to step into or grow within a supervisory role, this is a solid place to build. Fairstead's scale across 28 states means internal mobility is a real possibility for people who perform well and want to take on more.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Delaware Pines - Part-time
job.description:
Skills This Role Puts to Work Daily

Part-time maintenance work at a residential community in Huntington Beach demands more technical range than most people expect. At Delaware Pines, managed by Sunrise Management, a part-time technician touches plumbing, basic electrical, HVAC, appliance repair, carpentry, pool maintenance, and custodial upkeep, sometimes all in a single shift. The breadth isn't a list of edge cases. It's the actual daily scope, and it rewards people who've built genuine hands-on experience across trades rather than deep expertise in just one.

The pay range for this role sits at $25 to $26 per hour depending on experience. The position is part-time and not eligible for company benefit plans.

What the Work Actually Involves

A strong portion of the role centers on keeping units rent-ready and common areas in good shape. The standard for vacant unit turns is 3 to 5 days, so your ability to assess a punch list quickly and work through it efficiently matters. Service requests carry a 24-hour resolution expectation, and when parts or outside factors create delays, clear communication with both the Community Manager and the resident is part of the job, not an afterthought.

Beyond unit work, you'll manage preventive maintenance on a scheduled basis: checking lighting, fire safety equipment, pool and spa systems, and life-safety signage. Knowing the location of gas, water, irrigation, and electrical shutoffs is a baseline expectation. You'll assist with move-in and move-out inspections, track vacant unit status, and maintain accurate inventory of tools and supplies. On-call emergency availability is required, including evenings and weekends.

  • 1 to 2 years of hands-on maintenance experience across plumbing, electrical, HVAC, carpentry, and painting
  • Comfort using a mobile device for work orders and communication
  • Ability to work a flexible schedule including evenings, weekends, and holidays
  • Self-directed work style, you'll often operate without direct supervision
  • Strong attention to detail and a methodical approach to problem-solving
  • Resident-facing composure, including the ability to handle difficult situations professionally

What This Role Builds

Technicians who start in part-time roles like this one often develop something that's harder to teach than any specific trade skill: the discipline to prioritize across competing demands on a compressed schedule. When your hours are limited, your sequencing decisions matter. You learn to distinguish between what's urgent and what's scheduled, and that instinct carries into every maintenance role that follows, including lead tech and supervisor positions.

Sunrise Management operates with a resident-hospitality orientation, which means the soft skills this role sharpens, clear communication, professional presentation, handling difficult interactions with composure, are treated as part of the craft, not separate from it. For a technician building a career in residential property management, that framing tends to stick.

job.title: Leasing Specialist
job.description:
Some leasing roles are mostly paperwork and portal updates. This one asks for something different: the ability to build real relationships with people who are navigating real financial constraints, and to do it with consistency, warmth, and professionalism every single day.

Skills at the Center of This Role

Avanath operates affordable housing communities that serve the workforce, and the Leasing Specialist position reflects that mission in every interaction. The skills this role draws on most heavily are active listening, community-building, and cross-functional communication. You'll work with prospects and residents, yes, but also with vendors, social service partners, regulatory contacts, and your own management and maintenance teams. The ability to hold all of those relationships well, while still moving traffic through the leasing process, is what makes someone genuinely effective here.

On the leasing side, you'll qualify prospects, conduct tours, explain features and benefits in ways that connect to what the person actually needs, and guide them through the application and deposit process in compliance with Fair Housing requirements. You'll track all visits and follow-ups, process applications in Yardi Voyager, prepare files, and make sure units are move-in ready on agreed dates. When a prospect doesn't lease, you follow up. When you can't serve them here, you refer them to a sister community. Nothing falls through the cracks.

Resident retention lives here too. That means fielding calls and in-person visits, coordinating with the maintenance team on service requests, following up until issues are actually resolved, and participating in community events. It's a full-cycle relationship, from the first phone inquiry through the renewal conversation.

Administrative Accuracy Matters as Much as Personality

Strong leasing consultants know that the relationship skills and the paperwork skills have to coexist. At Avanath, that means accurate, timely Yardi data entry, proper lease execution before move-in, compliance file maintenance under the guidance of the Compliance department, and keeping your own commission records current for bonus purposes. Affordable housing communities carry regulatory requirements that don't leave room for sloppy documentation, particularly around LIHTC compliance. Experience in that space is a real advantage here.

What This Role Looks Like at Avanath Specifically

Avanath's communities serve workforce residents, and that shapes the culture of the leasing office. Residents often have complex situations. They may need more explanation, more patience, or more connection to outside resources. The Leasing Specialist here is expected to go beyond transactional service and genuinely advocate for people finding stable housing. That's a meaningful distinction.

Bilingual ability in English and Spanish is highly desired, which reflects the communities Avanath serves in the Los Angeles market. If you have that fluency, it will matter here in a way it might not at a Class A luxury lease-up.

  • 2 or more years of sales or customer relations experience
  • LIHTC or affordable housing experience is a strong plus
  • Bilingual English and Spanish preferred
  • Yardi Voyager familiarity preferred
  • Comfort with a flexible schedule, including evenings and weekends
  • Proficiency in Word, Excel, and standard office technology

For someone who wants a leasing role where the mission is genuine and the people you serve are genuinely counting on you, Avanath is worth a serious look.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Waypoint Management Services runs a high-end luxury community in Jacksonville and needs a Maintenance Technician who can keep things running cleanly, respond fast, and treat residents well. The property is growing, and they want someone who takes ownership of their work rather than waiting to be told what to do next.

What You'll Actually Do

Your day centers on service work and preventive care. You'll diagnose and repair problems across plumbing, HVAC, carpentry, and general building systems. Make-readies are a real part of the job: you'll inspect units before move-in, coordinate with contractors on punch list items, and make sure turns are completed to a high standard. Priority work orders get a 24-hour resolution target, which means you need to be organized and efficient, not just technically capable.

Beyond the unit-level work, you'll run routine preventive maintenance on HVAC equipment and community systems, service the pool (including chemical readings), maintain the trash compactor, and confirm that gate and security equipment stays operational. Grounds upkeep falls into your scope too. At a luxury community, the physical condition of the property directly shapes resident perception, so the bar for presentation is higher than average.

You'll be on an on-call rotation, so after-hours emergency response comes with the role. That's a consistent reality here, not a rare exception.

What You Bring

  • EPA Section 608 Type I and II certification (required)
  • Hands-on experience with building repairs across multiple trade areas
  • Working knowledge of OSHA safety standards
  • Ability to handle make-ready inspections and coordinate with outside contractors
  • Strong service orientation and a professional, resident-facing presence
  • CPO certification is a plus
  • High school diploma or equivalent, plus relevant field experience

Why This Role Is Worth a Hard Look

Waypoint offers medical, dental, and vision coverage starting day one, a 401k with matching, an employee referral program, and an onsite housing discount. For someone who wants to live close to where they work, that discount can meaningfully offset cost of living in Jacksonville.

Technicians at luxury communities tend to develop sharper skills faster than peers at Class C or value-add properties, simply because the expectation for quality is higher and the equipment is newer. If you're building toward a lead or maintenance supervisor role, a stint at a high-end community like this carries real weight on a resume. Owners and operators notice the difference between someone who can fix things and someone who can maintain a premium product at a consistent standard.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Rover technicians occupy a specific and underrated niche in multifamily maintenance. You're not tied to one property, which means you see more failure modes, more building types, and more management styles in a single year than a site-based tech might encounter in three. For someone building a career in maintenance, that breadth compounds fast.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Property Management Associates runs a large residential portfolio across Beverly Hills and the greater Los Angeles area. In this rover role, you'll move between communities based on where support is needed, so your schedule has real variety. Most days involve a mix of work orders and make-ready work: plumbing calls, drywall patches, appliance repairs, electrical fixes, and getting units punch-list ready for incoming residents. You'll also do routine inspections, catching deferred issues before they turn into expensive problems. Parts and inventory management falls to you as well, which means staying organized and thinking ahead, not just reacting.

You'll coordinate directly with property managers at each site, which requires solid communication. Residents interact with maintenance staff more personally than with almost anyone else at a property, so professionalism on service calls matters as much as technical skill.

What You Bring

  • At least three years of hands-on maintenance experience, ideally in multifamily residential settings
  • Solid working knowledge of plumbing, electrical, drywall, and appliance repair
  • Experience completing apartment turns and make-readies efficiently
  • Strong troubleshooting instincts and the judgment to prioritize competing demands
  • Comfort working independently across multiple sites with minimal supervision
  • A valid driver's license and proof of auto insurance (an auto allowance is included)
  • Physical capability to lift 25 to 50 pounds and stay active throughout a full workday
  • High school diploma or GED

Where This Role Can Take You

Rover technicians who perform well tend to be strong candidates for Lead Technician or Maintenance Supervisor roles, because they've already proven they can operate across a portfolio without constant direction. Exposure to multiple property types and management teams also builds the kind of institutional knowledge that makes someone valuable in a regional maintenance capacity down the line. PMA has been operating in Southern California for over 30 years with a portfolio of thousands of residential units, so internal advancement is a realistic path rather than a talking point.

Compensation runs $24 to $26 per hour with a $300 monthly auto allowance, a $25 monthly cell phone allowance, and a benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, life insurance, 401(k) with discretionary company contribution after one year, disability coverage, and paid time off.

job.title: Community Manager - Affordable Housing
job.description:
Affordable housing management runs on a different set of rules than conventional multifamily. The compliance layer is thick, the regulatory calendar never really lets up, and residents depend on the property in ways that go well beyond month-to-month convenience. That's the environment this Community Manager role operates in, at a Fairstead property in Boaz, Alabama.

What This Role Actually Involves

The core of the job is keeping a HUD-regulated property running on every dimension at once: occupancy, compliance, finances, and physical condition. On the compliance side, you'll own the full cycle of certifications, annual and interim recertifications included, and you'll need to know the HUD 4350.3 Handbook well enough to write responses to regulatory agencies and work alongside the Compliance Department when residents fall out of lease or program requirements. REAC inspections, Management and Occupancy Reviews, LIHTC reviews, and investor site visits all land on your desk to prepare for and coordinate.

Financially, you're watching delinquency closely, pursuing collections through the appropriate legal channels, monitoring bad-debt write-offs, and attending monthly budget reviews with your regional team. On the maintenance side, you'll coordinate preventive and emergency work with your Building Superintendent, manage vendor bids and contractor quotes, document unit inspections, and stay in close contact with the construction team if any renovation work is active on site.

Resident-facing responsibilities are woven into every week. Move-in and move-out coordination, lease violation documentation, eviction processing when necessary, and handling the steady stream of questions and requests that residents bring to the office all require consistency and a calm, organized approach.

What Qualifications You'll Need

  • At least three years of management experience that included supervising a team (property management background preferred, though hospitality, retail, or restaurant management is considered)
  • COS or CPO certification is required
  • TCS certification if the property carries a tax credit component
  • Hands-on experience with EIV, and familiarity with Yardi or RealPage
  • Affordable housing program knowledge, particularly HUD-regulated occupancy
  • A bachelor's degree is preferred but not required

Where Strong Candidates Stand Out

The compliance requirements here are specific and consequential. A candidate who has personally prepared for or sat through a MOR or REAC inspection carries a real advantage over someone who has only worked conventional multifamily. So does someone who understands how EIV discrepancies get resolved, or who has written a response to a regulatory finding. The technical side of affordable housing occupancy is learnable, but coming in with that foundation means you're contributing from the first month rather than spending it getting up to speed on program rules.

Fairstead operates as an integrated owner and manager with a portfolio across 28 states, which means community managers here have access to centralized compliance and construction resources that smaller operators can't offer. For someone looking to grow in affordable housing management, that organizational infrastructure tends to create clearer paths toward regional or portfolio-level roles over time.

job.title: Grounds Specialist - Botanic Miramar Beach ~ Destin, FL
job.description:
Beachside luxury communities like Botanic Miramar Beach carry a visual standard that residents pay a premium to live inside. A single neglected breezeway or a cloudy pool can undercut everything the leasing team works to sell. The Grounds Specialist role exists to make sure that never happens.

This is a daily-presence, eyes-on-the-property position at Davis Development's Destin community. You're walking the grounds throughout each shift, pulling litter, debris, and pet waste from breezeways, pool decks, and common areas before residents notice them. Trash and recyclables get handled on schedule. Pool chemistry gets checked and logged every day, with a full vacuum cycle weekly. Grills get cleaned and their timers and knobs inspected regularly to keep things safe. You'll also pitch in on general labor tasks supporting the Maintenance Supervisor and Property Manager as needs come up.

Davis Development operates as an owner-operator from the inside out. Their on-site teams aren't executing orders from a distant regional office; they're making real decisions daily. For a grounds role, that means your judgment about what the property needs matters. You notice the things others walk past.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of general labor experience; multifamily background is a plus
  • High school diploma or equivalent (preferred)
  • Certified Pool Operator (CPO) certification preferred
  • Comfortable with hand tools, cleaning equipment, and related supplies
  • Able to lift approximately 50 lbs regularly
  • Strong time management and communication skills across all channels
  • Availability to work over 40 hours per week when the property needs it

What Davis Development Offers

Benefits begin on the first of the month after 30 days of employment and include medical, dental, vision, and behavioral health coverage. The 401(k) plan includes a 4% employer match that vests immediately. Company-paid life insurance at one times base salary, a PTO package with carryover, a company apparel store allowance, and ongoing training and career development round out the package.

One practical note for candidates: Destin's Gulf Coast climate means this role runs outdoors year-round, through humid summers and variable winters. Pace and physical stamina matter here more than they might at an inland Class B community. CPO certification, even if you don't have it yet, is worth pursuing early. Pool compliance is taken seriously at luxury communities, and holding that credential opens up maintenance career paths that pure groundskeeping doesn't.

job.title: Property Manager
job.description:
Skills That Drive This Role

Property management at this level runs on a specific blend of financial literacy, team leadership, and operational awareness. At The Whit and Ridgewood Arches, a combined 164-unit portfolio in Minneapolis, the Property Manager keeps occupancy healthy, delinquency low, and the physical asset in good shape while developing a site team that actually performs. Bigos Management has earned Star Tribune Top Workplace recognition eleven times, which tells you something about how the company treats its people internally. That culture runs both directions: toward employees and toward residents.

The financial side of this role is real. You're managing rent collection, tracking delinquent accounts, working evictions when necessary, and submitting accurate reports to your Regional Manager. You'll do market research using public-facing sources to inform pricing recommendations. If you've ever prepared a T-12 or watched NOI move based on concession decisions, that mindset applies here. You're not just executing tasks. You're thinking about what the numbers mean for the property's overall health.

What You're Actually Managing Day to Day

On the leasing side, you're overseeing activity to keep occupancy maximized. That means watching traffic, understanding what's driving or limiting conversions, and making sure the site is positioned correctly in the market. On the maintenance side, you're building the turn schedule, coordinating make-ready inspections, managing the punch list process, and working with the roving maintenance team on anything beyond routine upkeep. You'll also monitor preventative maintenance programs and regularly walk the property to assess its condition and appearance.

The leadership piece is direct. You supervise site employees, handle coaching and development, and maintain a team environment consistent with Bigos' core values around relationships, quality, and accountability. Fair housing compliance and workplace safety are non-negotiable components of how you operate.

  • 3 to 5 years of management experience, with property management preferred
  • 1 to 2 years in a Property Manager or supervisory role preferred
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office; Yardi experience is a strong plus
  • CRM designation preferred
  • High school diploma or GED required; degree in property management preferred
  • Active real estate licenses are not permitted in this role
  • Solid grasp of federal fair housing law and applicable local provisions

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

Minneapolis has a competitive multifamily market with a wide range of product types. Managing two named communities under one umbrella means you're balancing distinct resident profiles and operational rhythms simultaneously. Managers who excel here tend to be detail-oriented on the financial side without losing sight of the resident experience. They know how to coach a team through a high-turn period without letting quality slip. They read delinquency reports early in the month, not at the end. And they document unit conditions thoroughly because it protects the property and keeps the make-ready process efficient.

The pay range runs $65,000 to $75,000. Bigos offers a competitive benefits package that includes 401(k) with employer match, HSA with employer contribution active from the first of the month after hire, ten paid holidays with no waiting period, PTO with rollover, volunteer time off, life insurance, short and long-term disability, educational assistance, an employee assistance program, a rent discount, and a Life Time Fitness membership discount.

job.title: Lobby Ambassador (Full-Time)- Century Plaza North Tower
job.description:
A resident steps off the elevator at 6 PM carrying dry cleaning and a pizza box, expecting the front desk to hold a package that arrived three hours ago. You already know the package is there. You hand it over before they ask. That's the job.

Action Property Management, one of the largest privately held HOA management companies in the western U.S., is hiring a full-time Lobby Ambassador for Century Plaza North Tower in Century City. This is an evening shift role: Monday through Friday, 3:00 PM to 11:30 PM, paying $22.00 to $23.00 per hour.

Daily Responsibilities

You're the face of the building during the hours when most residents are actually home. The role covers front desk operations, access control, and lobby presentation. You'll log activity in a daily report, field incoming calls, receive and distribute resident parcels, and handle guest and visitor inquiries. Keeping the lobby, front desk area, and main elevators presentable is part of every shift, not just when someone's watching.

You'll also need a working understanding of the association's governing documents. Residents ask about rules, guest policies, and building procedures. You need to answer accurately, not guess.

What the Right Candidate Looks Like

  • At least one year of customer service experience, required
  • Background in hospitality, luxury retail, or fine dining is a real advantage here
  • Hospitality Management students or recent graduates are a strong fit
  • Professional appearance and demeanor, consistently
  • Calm under pressure, solutions-focused, and proactive rather than reactive
  • Must be 18 or older and clear a pre-employment background check and drug screening

The candidate who stands out doesn't wait for a resident to flag a problem.
