Compensation runs from $31.00 to $32.25 per hour, with a discretionary semi-annual bonus and additional incentives including referral, renovation, and lease-up bonuses where applicable. Benefits include fully company-paid medical, dental, and vision plans covering eligible dependents, a 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, and tenure-based housing discounts. Prometheus also offers 12 paid holidays, including your birthday, which is an unusual and concrete acknowledgment that they've thought about their people beyond the standard package.

job.title: Leasing Manager
job.description:
Vero Beach sits in a stretch of Florida's Treasure Coast that draws a genuinely mixed renter profile: retirees, seasonal residents, young professionals, and working families all share the same leasing office waiting room. That variety shapes what this role actually demands day to day. A Leasing Manager here can't run a single script. You read the room, adjust your approach, and still close.

Waypoint Management Services is hiring for that position now. The core of the job is converting prospect interest into signed leases, then supporting those residents through move-in and into their tenancy. That sounds straightforward, but the full cycle is genuinely involved. You're fielding inquiries, running tours, preparing lease files, calculating prorations, and managing applicant qualification, all while keeping the leasing office and model units presentable and tour-ready. Renewals and waitlist management fall into the mix too, because occupancy goals don't pause between new lease cycles.

The follow-up piece deserves honest attention. Prospects who go quiet don't always stay that way, and the difference between a missed lease and a signed one is often one well-timed call or email. If you enjoy that part of sales, not just the tour but the patient, persistent follow-through, this role fits naturally. If you've come from hospitality or retail sales and you're moving into multifamily for the first time, that background translates well here. The human dynamics of leasing aren't far removed from managing guest experience or closing a service sale.

Spanish language skills are preferred, which reflects the community's demographics and gives the right candidate a real edge in building trust with prospective residents who may feel more comfortable in their first language. Yardi and CRM familiarity will help you get up to speed faster, though neither is a hard requirement. Fair Housing knowledge is expected at some level of fluency before you step into the role.

Weekend availability is part of the schedule rotation. That's consistent with almost every leasing role, but it's worth stating plainly: Saturday and Sunday are often the highest-traffic days, and a leasing manager who shows up present and energized on those days carries a lot of weight for the team.

What you'll bring

  • At least two years in leasing, sales, or hospitality, with a track record of converting interest into commitments
  • Comfortable handling the full leasing cycle: inquiry to move-in, including lease preparation and financial calculations
  • Familiarity with Fair Housing regulations
  • Bilingual English/Spanish, preferred
  • Experience with Yardi or comparable property management software, a plus
  • High school diploma or equivalent; valid driver's license required

Waypoint offers monthly leasing and renewal bonuses, a leaser-of-the-month monetary recognition, an employee housing discount, medical/dental/vision coverage starting day one, 401(k) with company match, 120 hours of PTO in year one, and additional floating days. For someone who wants a clear connection between their daily performance and their paycheck, the bonus structure here gives that feedback loop in a real way.

job.title: Porter
job.description:
Porter roles at student housing and build-to-rent communities are ground-level in title but foundational in function. The condition of common areas, make-ready units, and amenity spaces shapes how residents feel about where they live, and that perception drives renewals and referrals. At PeakMade Real Estate, this position sits inside a portfolio that spans off-campus student housing, traditional multifamily, and build-to-rent communities across the country, all managed out of Atlanta.

Day-to-Day Responsibilities

The core of this role is keeping the property clean, safe, and presentable. That means daily attention to the leasing office, amenity areas, laundry facilities, and other common spaces, on whatever schedule the property manager sets. When units turn, you'll help prepare them for incoming residents, which in student housing often means tight timelines and high volume during summer turns. You'll track supplies and equipment, respond to resident and management requests with professionalism, and flag anything unusual about the property or residents to the appropriate person. OSHA compliance and safe handling of cleaning chemicals aren't optional here; they're part of the daily routine.

The physical demands are real. This role involves frequent lifting up to 75 pounds, regular bending and stooping, and hands-on work with machinery and equipment. If you've worked in facilities, hospitality, or groundskeeping before, you'll recognize the rhythm quickly.

What This Role Builds

Porters who pay attention to how a property operates, not just their task list, tend to move into maintenance technician roles over time. You start to understand the relationship between unit condition and occupancy, between clean amenities and resident satisfaction scores, between a well-logged punch list and a smooth make-ready. Those are the instincts that property managers notice when they're filling maintenance tech openings. Student housing in particular moves fast during lease-up season, and people who can work under that pressure and still maintain standards get remembered.

PeakMade's company values center on accountability, resident experience, and continuous improvement, which maps well to someone who wants to grow rather than just clock in. The benefits package includes paid parental leave with a year of diapers provided, 17 days of paid time off including two wellbeing days, a 401(k) match, wellness programming, and employee resource groups. There's also a ten-year anniversary trip for long-tenure employees, which signals something about how the company thinks about retention.

  • High school diploma or equivalent required
  • Basic reading, written communication, and number recognition needed for daily tasks
  • Safe handling of cleaning fluids and equipment is a must
  • Physical stamina for lifting, bending, and equipment operation throughout the shift

If you're looking for a place to start building a maintenance career inside a company that manages a diverse portfolio, PeakMade's size and variety of community types gives you more exposure than a single-site operator would.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
It's a Tuesday morning, and before 9 a.m. you've already fielded a tenant call about an HVAC issue, flagged a vendor invoice that doesn't match the approved scope, and pulled a lease abstract to confirm CAM exclusions ahead of an operating expense reconciliation deadline. That's the rhythm of this role at Lincoln Property Company.

What This Role Actually Covers

Lincoln is one of the largest private real estate firms in the country, and this Atlanta-based position sits within their commercial portfolio, which spans office, retail, and industrial assets. As an Assistant Property Manager, you'll work directly alongside the Property Manager to keep day-to-day operations running accurately and on schedule.

A significant portion of your time will involve financial work: reviewing vendor invoices for compliance with the management agreement, supporting monthly report and budget package preparation, and managing the data collection behind CAM and operating expense reconciliations. These aren't cursory tasks. CAM rec errors surface quickly during audit season, and the discipline you build here transfers directly to senior property management responsibilities later.

Lease administration is another core area. You'll handle lease setups, process lease changes across applicable systems, and coordinate tenant move-ins and move-outs including participation in walk-throughs with tenants, the Property Manager, and tenant improvement teams. On the operations side, you'll respond to tenant needs, support vendor sourcing and bid coordination, help prepare emergency response plans, and provide direction to direct reports as appropriate.

This is a fully in-office position based in Atlanta. Property inspections are conducted monthly or more frequently, and travel to assigned properties is part of the job.

What You Bring and What You'll Build

This role requires a working foundation in commercial property fundamentals. Specific requirements include:

  • A bachelor's degree preferred, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience (1 to 2 years minimum)
  • Intermediate to advanced proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite
  • Familiarity with accounts payable and CMMS platforms
  • Ability to work through financial calculations including percentages, discounts, and basic financial analysis
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills suited to both tenant relationships and internal reporting
  • Experience with commercial office, retail, or industrial properties is preferred

What the role builds is equally worth naming. Candidates who come in with basic financial literacy will leave this position understanding how to read a T-12, how operating expense reconciliations connect to lease language, and how to manage vendor relationships through a full contract cycle. Those skills position you well for a Property Manager role, particularly in commercial fee management environments where financial accuracy and client reporting carry significant weight.

Strong candidates here tend to be detail-driven without being slow. The ability to keep lease data clean, catch invoice discrepancies before they become problems, and communicate clearly across tenants, vendors, and internal teams is what separates someone who handles the job from someone who advances through it.

job.title: Maintenance Technician I
job.description:
Grounds awareness, hands-on repair instincts, and a service mindset are the core skills this role draws on every single day. Hawthorne Residential Partners is hiring a Maintenance Technician I at Overlook Morganton Park in Southern Pines, NC, and the work is grounded in the fundamentals that keep a residential community running well: clean common spaces, make-ready support, and the kind of consistent presence residents notice.

Skills This Role Builds On (and Develops)

This is an entry-level position, and Hawthorne treats it that way in the best sense. A background in yardwork, general facility upkeep, or basic repair work translates directly. Some HVAC or maintenance experience is a plus, but the role is structured to teach. What matters more than credentials is a track record of showing up reliably and taking ownership of physical space.

On the grounds side, the work involves daily debris pickup, pressure washing breezeways and sidewalks, and keeping common areas like the pool deck, fitness room, clubhouse, and mailroom clean and presentable. On the repair side, you'll assist with make-ready turns on vacant units: light painting, lock changes, fixture replacements, and bulb checks. These tasks sound routine, but they directly affect occupancy. A unit that isn't make-ready on time costs the property a lease.

The role also includes pool maintenance support and on-call rotation for after-hours emergencies. That on-call component is worth understanding clearly before you apply. It's manageable, but it does mean your schedule isn't always 8-to-5, even if that's the standard Monday through Friday baseline.

Where This Role Leads

Hawthorne's internal career path program is a genuine differentiator here. The progression from Technician I to Technician II is structured, not vague, and their learning and development team is actively involved. For someone early in a maintenance career, the combination of on-the-job training across HVAC basics, plumbing, electrical, and turn work creates a skill base that carries across any multifamily property type. Technicians who move up at Hawthorne or elsewhere typically do so because they build diagnostic instincts, not just task completion habits. This role is the starting point for that.

What to Know About This Property and Company

Overlook Morganton Park sits in Southern Pines, part of Moore County's stable residential market anchored by the Pinehurst area. The region draws steady demand from military-adjacent households near Fort Liberty (formerly Bragg), retirees, and golf-industry workers, which tends to produce consistent occupancy and lower turnover volatility than high-growth urban corridors. For a maintenance tech, that context matters: you're likely supporting a community with a relatively stable resident base rather than constant lease-up churn.

Hawthorne Residential Partners manages a regional portfolio across the Southeast and is known in the multifamily space for investing in their site-level teams. The monthly renewal bonus program available at this level is a concrete signal of how the company ties compensation to community performance.

  • High school diploma or GED required
  • Valid driver's license required
  • One year of maintenance, repair, or HVAC experience preferred, not required
  • Familiarity with general yardwork and facility upkeep
  • Ability to participate in an on-call rotation for after-hours emergencies

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) match, paid time off (including your birthday), pet insurance, paid parental and adoption leave, telehealth access, and company-paid life insurance.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Maintenance work at a residential property splits into two modes: reactive and preventive. This role runs both at the same time. You're closing out resident work orders while also keeping up with scheduled inspections, make-ready turns, and grounds upkeep. The skill this job uses most is mechanical troubleshooting. You need to walk into a unit, diagnose what's wrong, and fix it correctly the first time.

What the Work Looks Like

Day-to-day, you're handling resident repair requests, conducting inspections, and prepping vacant apartments for incoming residents. Make-readies require a sharp eye for punch list items. You're also tracking parts, managing inventory, and coordinating with vendors when work requires outside support. Documentation matters here. Work orders, materials used, safety incidents: all of it needs to be logged accurately.

This position runs on a rotating on-call schedule, so evenings and weekends are part of the job. If that's a dealbreaker, this one isn't the right fit.

Skills This Role Depends On

  • Mechanical diagnosis and repair across building systems and common areas
  • Preventive maintenance planning and execution
  • Pre-move-out inspections and unit turn preparation
  • Vendor coordination and supply management
  • Safety compliance and OSHA protocol adherence
  • Clear communication with residents, management, and contractors
  • Ability to read technical manuals, schematics, and blueprints
  • EPA Type I and II or Universal certification (or willingness to obtain it)
  • Valid driver's license (required for golf cart operation on property)

Physical demands are real: regular lifting up to 50 lbs, climbing ladders, working outdoors in heat and cold, and spending time in confined or noisy spaces. You need solid manual dexterity and comfort operating both hand tools and power tools.

Working at Hillpointe

Hillpointe builds and manages market-rate workforce housing across the Sun Belt, and they handle the full development cycle in-house, from land acquisition through construction and asset management. That structure means the maintenance team operates within a company that understands properties from the ground up, literally. Decisions move faster, and there's direct accountability from ownership down to site operations.

Okatie, SC sits in the Bluffton area, just outside Hilton Head Island. The region has seen steady population growth driven by coastal relocation trends, which keeps demand for workforce housing strong and occupancy pressure real. For a maintenance tech, that means consistent volume and a property that stays active.

Strong candidates for this type of role tend to have a mix of HVAC, plumbing, and electrical knowledge rather than depth in just one trade. The ability to troubleshoot across systems, without waiting on a specialist for every call, is what separates technicians who advance from those who plateau. EPA certification is a clear differentiator if you already hold it.

job.title: Community Assistant Manager - Redfield Ridge
job.description:
CloudTen Residential manages a genuinely varied multifamily portfolio across the West, from hotel-to-residential conversions to high-rise lease-ups to value-add repositioning plays. That range matters for this role because it means the skills you build here go well beyond any single asset type. Redfield Ridge is one piece of a growing Nevada-anchored operation, and the assistant manager position there is structured deliberately as a training ground for the community manager seat.

The day-to-day splits across four areas: financials, leasing, team support, and resident relations. On the financial side, you'll handle rent collection, posting, daily deposits, bank reconciliation, and invoice processing. You'll also own delinquency follow-through, including serving non-payment notices and coordinating eviction proceedings when the community manager requires backup. Weekly and monthly reporting is part of the cadence, so comfort with property management software and a clean understanding of basic accounting isn't optional here.

Leasing responsibilities include responding to inquiries, conducting tours, and keeping all lease documents current and Fair Housing compliant. You'll also help track comp properties and market conditions, which feeds into pricing and marketing recommendations. Move-in and move-out administration rounds out the operational scope, including apartment inspections and security deposit dispositions handled within state-mandated timelines.

When the community manager is off-site, you step into full operational responsibility. That's worth taking seriously during the interview process. This isn't a role where management coverage is theoretical.

Reno's multifamily market has seen real pressure over the past few years, with significant new supply delivering across the metro while rent growth has moderated from its post-pandemic peaks. That context makes delinquency management and resident retention more consequential than they might be in a tighter market. Candidates who've worked through a softer occupancy environment and understand how concessions and renewal strategy interact will stand out.

The pay range runs $22 to $24 per hour depending on experience. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, an FSA, company-paid life insurance, and paid time off.

What the role requires

  • At least two years in property management, leasing, or a closely related field
  • Working knowledge of landlord-tenant law, Fair Housing regulations, and local compliance standards
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and at least one property management platform
  • Strong written and verbal communication, plus the organizational discipline to manage multiple priorities without dropping anything
  • Foundational accounting knowledge sufficient to handle daily financial tasks accurately

Candidates who come in with a genuine interest in advancing to a community manager role will fit CloudTen's intent for this position. The company's growth trajectory across the West means that path isn't abstract.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Residential maintenance work builds a skill set that compounds quickly. Every service request answered, every turn completed, every HVAC system diagnosed adds to a practical knowledge base that transfers directly into lead tech roles, maintenance supervisor positions, and eventually facilities or regional maintenance management. At Karya Property Management, a Maintenance Technician role in Baytown, Texas gives you the day-to-day volume and variety that accelerates that growth.

The Technical Core

This position touches the full range of residential systems. Plumbing, electrical, HVAC, carpentry, and paint work all fall within scope, which means you're not narrowing your expertise by taking this role. You'll respond to resident work orders, run unit turns and make-readies, and conduct property inspections to catch deferred maintenance before it becomes a larger repair. Tool and inventory management is part of the job too. Knowing what's on the shelf and keeping it stocked keeps your response times tight and your costs predictable.

On-call availability is required, so this isn't a strictly scheduled position. That's honest. After-hours work is part of residential maintenance, and if you've done this before, you already know that emergency calls during peak summer months in the Houston area are real. Baytown's heat and humidity put HVAC systems under consistent stress, which means that comfort with diagnostics and preventive maintenance on those systems is genuinely useful here, not just a checkbox on a job posting.

What Separates Strong Candidates

The basics are a high school diploma or GED and prior maintenance or handyman experience. But the technicians who stand out in a role like this share a few specific habits. They communicate with residents like professionals, not just fix the problem and leave. They anticipate what's likely to fail based on what they're already seeing during inspections. And they work efficiently during turns, because a slow make-ready delays occupancy and puts pressure on the whole team.

  • Hands-on experience with residential plumbing, electrical, HVAC, and carpentry
  • Comfortable working independently and prioritizing tasks without constant direction
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • Availability for on-call and flexible scheduling
  • Genuine attention to safety standards and quality workmanship

What This Role Builds at Karya

Karya Property Management offers health and wellness benefits, strong PTO, and maternity and paternity leave. But the longer-term value of a role like this is what you build in your own career. Technicians who learn to read a property's maintenance patterns, document their work clearly, and collaborate well with the management team are the ones who move into lead or supervisor roles. This position puts you inside those daily operations, working directly alongside property management to triage and prioritize, which gives you visibility into how maintenance decisions affect NOI and resident retention. That context matters when you're ready for the next step.

job.title: Maintenance Technician II at The Marq Highland Park Apartments
job.description:
A resident puts in a request at 7 a.m.: no hot water. By 8, you've already diagnosed the water heater, sourced the part, and updated the work order. That's the rhythm of this role.

The Work

Cottonwood Residential is hiring a Maintenance Technician II for The Marq Highland Park Apartments in Westchase, Florida. This is an intermediate-level position, which means you're expected to work independently on most repairs without needing the supervisor to walk you through it. You'll handle the full range of service requests: HVAC diagnosis and repair, plumbing, electrical fixtures, appliances, and carpentry. You'll also contribute to the make-ready process, getting vacant units turned and ready for incoming residents.

Beyond service requests, the role includes preventative maintenance on building systems, regular property walks to keep grounds and common areas in good condition, and support for pool and spa upkeep. You'll document completed work in the property management system and stay in communication with the Maintenance Supervisor on anything that needs escalation or additional resources.

On-call rotation is part of the job. After-hours emergencies happen, and you'll be expected to respond when it's your turn. The supervisor provides backup, but residents count on the team to show up.

What Qualifies You

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • 2 or more years of multifamily maintenance experience
  • EPA Type II or Universal certification (required)
  • Solid hands-on knowledge of HVAC, plumbing, electrical, appliances, and pool/spa systems
  • CPO certification (preferred)
  • Ability to lift up to 75 lbs. regularly; weights over 50 lbs. should be handled with assistance
  • Availability for evenings, weekends, and on-call shifts
  • Basic tools required; HVAC gauges required if EPA certified

The candidates who stand out here aren't necessarily the ones with the longest resume. They're the ones who can walk into an unfamiliar problem, think through it systematically, and fix it right the first time. Multifamily maintenance moves fast, and units that sit down cost money and frustrate residents. Technicians who close work orders cleanly, communicate clearly, and leave the work area better than they found it are the ones who earn trust on a team like this.

Cottonwood Residential operates a national multifamily portfolio, so there's genuine room to grow within the organization for technicians who perform well and build their skills over time.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Museum District, Houston, TX
job.description:
Maintenance techs at apartment communities wear a lot of hats. At Plaza Museum District, a Berkshire Residential property in Houston's Museum District, you're not just fixing things. You're the person residents see when something's wrong, which means your attitude matters as much as your tool belt.

What the Work Looks Like Day to Day

Your time splits between completing work orders, supporting make-readies, and keeping the property's physical condition where it needs to be. Curb appeal and common areas fall under your watch. You'll help manage shop inventory, equipment upkeep, and key security, which sounds routine until something's missing at the wrong moment. You'll also back up the management team on enforcing safety standards and community policies, and you'll be expected to document and communicate clearly, both in writing and in person.

The role calls for working knowledge across appliances, plumbing, electrical, carpentry, and general building systems. You don't need to be a licensed specialist in every trade, but you do need enough hands-on experience to diagnose problems quickly and know when something's beyond your scope. A minimum of one year working maintenance in a residential community is expected.

What's Honest About the Job

Maintenance work at an apartment community is physical, repetitive on some days, and genuinely unpredictable on others. Residents don't always report issues at convenient times, and the punch list before a unit turn rarely shrinks on its own. The Museum District location means you're working near a dense, active part of Houston, which brings its own pace. If you prefer a job where the problems are always straightforward and the hours are always predictable, this one will test you.

That said, this is also a role where strong techs build real credibility fast. You see the whole property. You learn what breaks, how often, and why. That operational knowledge is exactly what carries into lead tech or service manager roles over time.

What Berkshire Offers

Berkshire owns and manages its own properties rather than operating as a third-party manager, which tends to create more consistency in how decisions get made at the site level. Benefits include three weeks of vacation, personal development planning, health insurance, and a 25% rent discount for employees.

  • At least one year of residential maintenance experience
  • Hands-on knowledge of plumbing, electrical, appliances, carpentry, and general building systems
  • Proficiency in written and spoken English
  • Comfort using computers and property management-related software
  • Reliable, detail-oriented, and resident-focused approach to the work

Berkshire is an equal opportunity employer committed to fair treatment across race, color, creed, national origin, age, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, and all other protected categories.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Champion Hills at Windyke is a residential community in Memphis, and Makowsky Ringel Greenberg needs a maintenance technician who can carry real responsibility from day one. This is a full trade role, not a helper position. You'll work independently across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, appliance repair, and lock work, and you'll be expected to handle those systems with confidence rather than escalate most things to a supervisor.

What You'll Actually Do

A typical week moves between reactive repairs and scheduled work. Make-readies keep the turns moving between residents, and preventive maintenance keeps the systems from failing in the first place. You'll handle lock re-keying and installation, respond to plumbing and electrical calls, and document your work daily. Rotating weekend on-call is part of the schedule, so after-hours calls do happen. That's just honest.

The role carries a fuel allowance because you'll use your own vehicle to get to and from the property and service calls. MRG also includes a $1,000 sign-on bonus, an annual bonus structure, paid time off, holidays, and a full benefits package covering medical, dental, vision, disability, life insurance, AFLAC options, and a 401(k) with profit sharing.

What You Bring

  • HVAC certification is required. Universal certification is preferred and will matter in the hiring conversation.
  • At least two years of apartment maintenance experience, meaning you've handled the full range of residential repair work, not just one trade.
  • Solid working knowledge of common tools, appliances, and mechanical systems.
  • Familiarity with applicable building codes and OSHA safety practices. Documentation is part of the job, so you need to be comfortable with that side of it too.
  • A reliable vehicle, valid driver's license, and proof of insurance.
  • Ability to pass background, credit, and drug screenings.

Strong candidates also bring organization and time management. When you've got three open work orders, a make-ready punch list, and a resident waiting on a callback, the techs who stay steady are the ones who prioritize well and communicate clearly. Customer service matters here because residents notice how you show up in their home, not just whether the repair got done.

Context Worth Knowing

Makowsky Ringel Greenberg has been managing properties in the Memphis market for decades. Working for an established local operator tends to mean clearer processes, institutional knowledge on the maintenance side, and a management team that understands the market. For a technician who wants stability and a legitimate path toward a lead or facilities management role, that kind of operator tends to offer more runway than a smaller shop or a national REIT where the local team is thin. If you've got the HVAC cert and the hands-on background, this is a role worth taking seriously.

job.title: Maintance Supervisor
job.description:
CommonPlace puts a real emphasis on the idea that a home is more than just an apartment unit. That framing matters for this role because a Maintenance Supervisor here isn't just keeping equipment running. The condition of every hallway, every make-ready, every courtyard reflects directly on whether residents feel like they actually belong somewhere. That's the standard you're working to.

Day to day, this job is split between leading people and doing physical work yourself. You'll schedule and supervise your team, review their work, and step in alongside them when needed. Vendor oversight is part of it too. When a contractor is on site, you're the one accountable for the quality of what they deliver. You'll manage parts inventory, keep MSDS logs current, and make sure the shop stays organized enough that the next person who needs a tool can actually find it. Turns (make-readies) are a core part of the rhythm here. Units need to be genuinely move-in ready, and that punch list responsibility lands with you.

The on-call piece is worth being direct about. Emergencies don't follow business hours, and you'll be in the rotation. That's a real part of the job. The same goes for being the person who handles lock changes after evictions or responds when something breaks down on a weekend. If you've worked in property maintenance before, none of this is a surprise. But if it's new information, it should factor into your decision.

CommonPlace is also looking for someone who communicates clearly with the Property Manager, flags unusual findings early, and keeps OSHA and company safety policies in place consistently, not just during inspections. That last part separates supervisors who actually build team habits from ones who just check boxes.

What CommonPlace Is Looking For

  • 3 to 5 years of hands-on maintenance experience, ideally in residential property management
  • 1 to 3 years in a supervisory role
  • Working knowledge of plumbing, electrical, HVAC, PTAC units, appliances, and general construction
  • Comfortable with hand tools, power tools, and motorized or electrical equipment
  • Able to regularly lift, carry, or maneuver up to 50 lbs independently
  • Valid driver's license with proof of automobile liability insurance
  • Availability for on-call rotation and a flexible schedule

Pay runs $26 to $28 per hour, with medical, dental, and 401(k) benefits, plus paid vacation, sick time, and volunteer time.

One thing worth noting for candidates considering the supervisory side of this role: the strongest applicants tend to be people who've already had to hold a team accountable to a quality standard, not just complete work orders themselves. Training a newer tech to do a turn correctly takes different skills than doing the turn yourself. If that part of the job genuinely interests you, this is a role where it's a significant part of the work.

job.title: Onsite Project Manager
job.description:
This role lives at the intersection of construction knowledge and field coordination. The Onsite Project Manager at Asset Living's Omaha location needs to read plans, hold subcontractors accountable, and keep a renovation schedule moving, all at the same time. If those three things feel natural to you, read on.

What This Role Calls On Daily

The core skills here are schedule management, vendor coordination, and quality control. You'll interpret project plans and specifications, track construction progress against contract documents, and compile submittals for the Senior Construction Project Manager's review. You're not just walking the site, you're the person who catches deviations before they become expensive problems.

Subcontractor management takes up a meaningful chunk of your time. That means reviewing proposals, confirming contract compliance, and coordinating work sequencing so trades aren't stacking on top of each other. Strong written and verbal communication is non-negotiable since you're the daily point of contact between the field and the broader project team.

Multifamily renovation experience is a genuine advantage here. Understanding how an occupied or recently vacated unit moves through a make-ready or full rehab cycle, and what quality benchmarks matter at each stage, lets you set expectations with subs rather than just report on what they did.

Qualifications Worth Highlighting

  • High school diploma or equivalent required
  • Certified Apartment Manager (CAM) or Accredited Resident Manager (ARM) designation preferred
  • Previous multifamily renovation supervision experience strongly preferred
  • Ability to read and interpret project plans and specifications
  • Comfortable with independent judgment and real-time problem solving on-site
  • Basic computer skills and familiarity with project or property management software
  • Willingness to travel and flexibility with hours when deadlines require it
  • Ability to lift up to 25 pounds; regular standing, walking, and physical presence on the job site

Why This Role at Asset Living

Asset Living is a third-party management firm ranked in the NMHC top 50, with a portfolio spanning multifamily, build-to-rent, affordable housing, and student housing. The Onsite Project Manager reports directly to a Senior Construction Project Manager, which means you get structure and a clear escalation path, but you're expected to own the day-to-day without hand-holding.

One thing candidates often underestimate about this type of role: the documentation discipline matters as much as the field presence. Submittals, schedule updates, and quality control records are how you demonstrate that work conforms to contract. Candidates who treat paperwork as secondary to "getting things done" tend to struggle. The ones who thrive treat both as the same job.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
Skills This Role Runs On

Student housing operates on a different clock than conventional multifamily. The entire community turns over in a compressed window once a year, delinquency pressure is constant because you're collecting from 18-to-22-year-olds with inconsistent income, and the leasing cycle runs against an academic calendar rather than market demand. The Assistant Community Manager role at Alight Laramie asks you to carry skills across three distinct areas simultaneously: financial controls, turn execution, and customer experience management. If any one of those wobbles, the whole property feels it.

On the financial side, you'll manage accounts receivable, enforce NSF and late fee policies, keep delinquency below 2% at month end, and assist with monthly close. The Entrata proficiency requirement matters here. Knowing your way around the ledger in a PMS isn't optional at this level. You're also posting damage charges from quarterly inspections and handling dispute resolution when residents push back, which they will.

The customer-facing work runs parallel. Weekly market surveys, managing concession budgets, monitoring Yelp and Google reviews, and working with the centralized sales team on occupancy goals. Laramie is a university town tied entirely to UW enrollment cycles, so traffic patterns and lease-up timelines are predictable but unforgiving if you miss the window.

The Turn Is Its Own Season

Annual turnover in student housing is a full operational sprint. This role takes an active hand in it, including physical tasks like moving furniture, assisting facilities with punch lists, and cleaning units. Scion uses Turnable to track the electronic turn board, and you'll be responsible for ensuring progress stays on pace, damage assessments are completed accurately, and final billing goes out correctly. Move-in, room assignments, transfers, and move-outs all process in a tight window. The General Manager leads this effort, and you're the second in command executing it.

It's worth noting that this role also requires you to step into the General Manager position when they're absent. That's a real expectation, not a formality buried in the job description.

What Makes This Role Work at Alight Laramie

Scion is a student housing operator with a clearly defined internal stack: Entrata, ClickUp, Lattice, Greenhouse, Qualtrics. Candidates who've worked across a purpose-built tech stack in student or conventional housing will move faster here than those learning the category from scratch. The one year of property management experience requirement is a floor, not a ceiling. Strong candidates typically bring familiarity with lease audits, resident account management, and at least one major turn season behind them.

The position includes a discretionary annual bonus, 401k matching, paid parental leave, and learning reimbursement. On-call responsibility is part of the schedule. That's standard for any community this size, but worth knowing before you apply.

  • 1+ year in property management or a residential living community
  • Proficiency in a property management system, Entrata preferred
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Comfort with accounts receivable, delinquency tracking, and resident billing
  • Ability to cover General Manager responsibilities as needed
  • Eligible to work in the United States without visa sponsorship

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Aubrey, TX
job.description:
Maintenance technician roles at vertically integrated ownership groups tend to run differently than third-party fee management shops. When the same company owns and manages the asset, there's more accountability attached to every work order, every turn, and every curb appeal walk. Berkshire Residential Investments operates that way at Park 3Eighty in Aubrey, TX, and this technician position sits in the middle of that day-to-day physical operation.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

You're covering the full range of hands-on maintenance: plumbing, electrical, appliance repair, carpentry, and general building upkeep. Beyond work orders, you'll help maintain the shop, manage inventory, and keep equipment and key security organized. Curb appeal is treated as a real priority here, not an afterthought. You'll be expected to inspect the property regularly and flag issues before residents do. Supporting the management team on safety compliance and community standards is part of the job, as is delivering consistent, professional service to both current residents and prospects walking the property.

One year of residential maintenance experience is the baseline. You need a working knowledge across the trades, not necessarily a license in every one, but you can't be starting from scratch on appliances or basic plumbing when a resident's unit is down.

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

The technicians who do well in roles like this are the ones who treat a make-ready punch list the same way they treat an emergency call. Consistency matters more than occasional heroics. If you're the type who takes pride in a clean shop, tracks your parts inventory without being reminded, and communicates clearly with the office team without drama, you'll fit the culture. Berkshire puts weight on people skills alongside technical ability. Residents notice whether the tech who showed up was professional. That matters here.

The Bigger Picture

Berkshire Residential is a nationally operating ownership and management company, so technicians who grow into lead or make-ready roles have a real path toward maintenance supervisor and eventually service manager positions within the same organization. For someone early in their maintenance career, there's value in working for an owner-operator where your work has direct visibility to asset performance. Benefits include three weeks of vacation, a 25% rent discount, and personal development plans.

Aubrey sits in the north DFW growth corridor, and the submarket has seen significant new construction over the past few years. That means residents in the area generally have options, and the quality of maintenance service plays a real role in retention. It's not background noise. It shows up in renewal rates.

job.title: Maintenance Technician (Summer Oaks)
job.description:
What This Role Actually Demands

Maintenance work at an affordable housing community calls on a wider skill set than most job titles suggest. At Summer Oaks in Sonoma, you'll draw on genuine multi-trade competency every single day: electrical troubleshooting on appliances, circuits, and fixtures; plumbing repairs to water and sewage systems; rough and finish carpentry; and landscape and irrigation upkeep. These aren't siloed tasks handed off to specialists. You're expected to move across all of them, assess what's needed, and get it done to standard.

The role also carries a mentorship component. You'll coach and provide day-to-day oversight to Maintenance Groundskeeper staff, which means your communication skills matter almost as much as your technical ones. Clear, direct guidance to junior team members isn't a bonus trait here. It's a core part of the job.

On-call rotation is real and worth understanding upfront. You'll carry 24/7 emergency coverage for seven consecutive days at a time, including evenings, weekends, and holidays. If that kind of schedule disrupts your household, it's worth thinking through before you apply. If you're someone who handles that well and takes pride in being the person residents can count on at midnight, this structure suits you.

Day-to-Day Scope

A typical week will include some combination of the following:

  • Unit turns: painting, flooring, fixture installation, appliance hookups, and anything else needed to get a vacant unit rent-ready within established timeframes
  • Preventive maintenance rounds and work order documentation in the property management system
  • Landscape and irrigation checks to keep common areas clean, functional, and up to MidPen's standards
  • Contractor coordination: helping with bid processes, scheduling vendor work, and confirming it's completed correctly
  • Support for Community Manager on move-ins, move-outs, and annual inspections
  • Inventory management for tools, equipment, and supplies

The paperwork side of this role is real. Work orders, inspection logs, and procurement documentation all require accurate records. Basic computer proficiency isn't optional.

Doing This Work at MidPen

MidPen has operated affordable housing across Northern California since 1970 and manages more than 142 properties serving working families, seniors, and residents with special needs. That context shapes the culture of maintenance work here in a specific way: the people living in these units depend on well-maintained housing in ways that go beyond convenience. A leaking pipe or broken heater in an affordable community carries a different weight than it might at a market-rate property, and most MidPen maintenance staff will tell you they feel that difference.

What separates strong candidates from average ones in this role is the combination of trade depth and interpersonal steadiness. You can have excellent plumbing skills and still struggle here if you can't communicate calmly with a frustrated resident or give clear direction to a groundskeeper who's still learning. MidPen looks for technicians who bring both, and who are comfortable taking ownership without needing constant oversight from the Community Manager.

The pay range for this position runs $25.00 to $28.13 per hour based on experience, and the benefits package includes health, dental, vision, life and disability insurance, a 403(b) retirement plan, paid parental leave, education reimbursement, and an EAP, among others.

job.title: Part Time Groundskeeper Manufactured Housing Community
job.description:
Part-time groundskeeper roles at manufactured housing communities tend to get overlooked, but they carry real weight. An 81-home community lives and dies by its curb appeal and the condition of its common areas. At Mountain View Estates in Longmont, this is a 10-hour-per-week position, so the work is focused and the expectations are clear: show up, keep the property looking sharp, and flag problems before they become work orders.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Most of your time will split between grounds maintenance and common area upkeep. That means operating mowers, trimmers, and blowers; inspecting and adjusting irrigation systems; and doing a morning walkthrough to catch anything that needs attention before residents notice it. The role also includes chainsaw work for larger limbs or debris, pool maintenance during season, and trash-out duties when abandoned items or bulk waste accumulate. You'll also handle interior common spaces: sweeping, scrubbing, disinfecting, keeping the leasing office and community rooms presentable. None of this is glamorous, but it's the kind of work that makes a manufactured housing community feel well-managed rather than neglected.

You'll operate with minimal supervision, which means you're expected to prioritize your time well within a short shift window. You'll report maintenance and safety issues to the on-site team rather than being responsible for repairs, but solid eyes matter here. Catching a leaking sprinkler valve or a parking lot hazard early keeps small problems from turning into capex headaches.

What IPG Is Looking For

  • At least one year of groundskeeping or maintenance experience at a manufactured housing or multifamily community of 100 or more units
  • Comfortable and safe with power tools and mechanical equipment
  • Physically able to walk, lift, bend, and stay on your feet throughout a shift
  • Professional when interacting with residents and staff
  • Basic landscaping and light general maintenance knowledge is a plus

About Investment Property Group

IPG is a private investment and management firm based in Park City, Utah, with a portfolio that spans 150 properties across 13 states, covering multifamily, manufactured housing, and RV communities. The company puts weight on employee development and internal culture, and given the size of their operation, part-time roles like this one have a track record of becoming full-time when the right person is in them. The pay range for this position runs $20 to $24 per hour depending on experience and qualifications.

One honest note: manufactured housing communities have a different rhythm than conventional apartment properties. Residents often own their homes and have long tenure on-site, so the relationship between staff and community members tends to be more personal. Being consistent and approachable matters as much as the quality of the grounds work itself.

job.title: Maintenance Custodian
job.description:
It's 8:15 on a Tuesday morning. Someone tracked mud through the laundry room overnight, a light fixture in Hallway C is out, and the groundskeeper flagged a broken gate latch on the way in. That's a normal start. By afternoon, you've handled all three and moved on to the next punch list.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Paragon Properties is hiring a Maintenance Custodian for their Clinton Township community. This is a Monday through Friday, 8am to 5pm position. No nights, no weekends, no on-call rotation. That's worth saying plainly, because a lot of maintenance roles come with after-hours obligations baked in. This one doesn't.

Day to day, you're keeping the property clean, safe, and functional. That means common area cleaning, trash removal, basic repairs, and light groundskeeping work as needed. You'll use hand and power tools, handle cleaning chemicals correctly, and stay on top of whatever the property throws at you without needing someone to tell you what to do next. Self-direction matters here. The property doesn't stop generating work, and the expectation is that you'll manage your time and tasks without constant supervision.

Pay runs up to $20 per hour depending on experience. Paragon also offers paid time off, nine company-paid holidays, medical, dental, and vision insurance with a short waiting period, company-paid life and disability coverage, a 401(k) with employer contribution, quarterly profit sharing, a rent discount, and an employee referral program. They run a hands-on training facility with weekly education courses, so if you're newer to property maintenance, there's a real structure in place to develop your skills.

What You Bring

  • Experience with cleaning and light maintenance tasks
  • Familiarity with cleaning chemicals, equipment, and proper handling
  • Comfort using basic hand tools and power tools
  • Reliable attendance and dependable transportation. A valid driver's license is recommended
  • Ability to work independently and stay productive without close supervision

Pre-employment requirements include a background check, drug screening, and a physical.

One thing that separates the people who do well in custodial and maintenance roles from those who burn out quickly: the willingness to take ownership of the small stuff. A scuff on the lobby wall or a full trash can by the mailboxes might seem minor, but residents notice them. The candidates who build a real career in property maintenance are the ones who see those details before anyone has to point them out. Paragon's investment in training and profit sharing suggests they're looking for people who want to grow in the work, not just punch a clock.

job.title: Community Assistant Manager - Metro on Main
job.description:
The Assistant Community Manager role at Metro on Main, a CloudTen Residential property in Mesa, AZ, sits at a specific and valuable crossroads in a multifamily career: you're operational enough to run the day-to-day, but still close enough to a working Community Manager to absorb how decisions get made at the property level. CloudTen is explicit that this position is designed to prepare you for a CM seat. That's not boilerplate. The company manages a genuinely varied portfolio across the West, including hotel-to-residential conversions, high-rise lease-ups, and value-add repositioning projects, so the growth path here has real breadth behind it.

What You'll Actually Do

Most of your days will involve the financial and administrative engine of the property. That means collecting and posting rent, reconciling bank accounts, preparing deposits, processing invoices, and generating weekly and monthly reports. You'll be the person who keeps the numbers clean and the records accurate in the property management system. On the leasing side, you'll handle inquiries, conduct tours, and support lease renewals and resident retention programs. You'll also conduct inspections of units, common areas, and grounds, manage move-in and move-out administration, and prepare security deposit dispositions in line with Arizona landlord-tenant law.

When the Community Manager is out, you step into that role. That's not ceremonial. It means you need to know delinquency procedures, how to serve non-payment notices, and when to initiate eviction coordination. You'll also support the on-site team in day-to-day challenges and help model the operational standards CloudTen holds across its portfolio.

What You Bring

  • At least two years of multifamily experience, ideally at a community of 300 or more units
  • Solid command of property management software and Microsoft Office
  • Working knowledge of Fair Housing regulations and Arizona landlord-tenant law
  • Comfort with basic accounting principles and financial reporting cycles
  • Strong organizational habits and the ability to reprioritize when the day shifts
  • Communication skills that hold up across residents, vendors, and team members

Where This Role Takes You

The skills that compound fastest in an assistant manager role are the financial ones. Leasing coordinators learn traffic and closing ratios. Maintenance coordinators learn work order flow. But the AM who can read a T-12, track NOI trends, manage delinquency, and explain variances to ownership is the one who gets promoted to Community Manager with real confidence. This role gives you structured exposure to all of that, inside a company that manages complex assets across multiple markets. For someone two or three years into a multifamily career who wants to run their own property, this is a logical and well-supported next step. Pay runs $23 to $26 per hour depending on experience, and CloudTen offers health benefits, FSA, company-paid life insurance, and paid time off.

job.title: Regional Service Manager
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role sits above the property level but stays close to the work. You'll spend real time in the field: walking communities, reviewing make-ready quality, inspecting service team output, and coaching Service Managers across a Southern California portfolio. Monthly feedback to Operations Managers and the VP of Maintenance Services keeps you accountable to what you find.

On the capital side, you'll review scope, track timelines, approve progress payments, and sign off on completed projects. That requires staying in close contact with Community Managers and Service Managers so nothing stalls without a clear reason.

Vendor and contract management is a meaningful part of this job. You'll define scope, set service standards, and negotiate pricing with outside contractors. The goal is to reduce contractor reliance where your in-house teams can handle the work, and to control cost per unit across maintenance parts, supplies, turns, and exterior maintenance.

You'll also build the operational infrastructure: preventative maintenance programs, QAR standards, procurement processes, and a training calendar that hits each service team at least quarterly. Service Managers under your oversight will participate in 30-60-90 day forecasting with their Community Managers, and you'll set the standard for how that happens.

What You Bring

  • At least 3 years of multi-family housing experience, with a track record that includes managing maintenance operations across multiple sites
  • EPA Universal certification (or Type I and II) for refrigerant recycling, required before or at start
  • CPO certification and any other state or local credentials required for California operations
  • Hands-on technical ability in plumbing, electrical, and appliances. You need to troubleshoot alongside your teams, not just direct from a distance
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Office, and comfort with tools like Bluebeam for blueprint review or Smartsheet for project tracking
  • Strong communication skills. You'll be translating field-level problems into actionable information for operations leadership, and vice versa
  • Willingness to travel across the portfolio as the work requires

Context Worth Knowing

Griffis Residential operates a multi-community portfolio, and this position covers properties in the Anaheim and San Diego markets. Southern California's labor and contractor costs run high, which makes the cost-per-unit focus on this role genuinely consequential. A strong candidate here brings a track record of reducing vendor spend by building internal capability rather than just re-negotiating contracts. The difference between average and strong in this role often comes down to how well you can develop Service Managers. You're being asked to build competency across multiple teams simultaneously, so your ability to coach, identify skill gaps, and run effective field training matters as much as your own technical knowledge.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This Leasing Consultant role at Logan Property Management puts you at the front door of Peachtree, a residential community at 901 F Street in San Diego's East Village neighborhood. East Village has matured considerably over the past decade, shifting from a transitional corridor into one of downtown San Diego's more active rental submarkets. Foot traffic is real here, and so is competition from newer mid-rise product nearby. Your job is to convert that traffic into signed leases.

Day to day, that means touring prospective residents, following up on leads with purpose, and helping applicants move through the screening and approval process without losing momentum. You'll track your own numbers, understand where prospects drop off, and adjust accordingly. Beyond leasing, you'll stay close to current residents during their tenancy, handling renewal conversations and keeping occupancy where it needs to be. Good leasing consultants at conventional properties like this one also develop a feel for concessions, know when to offer them and when to hold firm, and understand how unit availability and traffic patterns shift week to week.

What You Bring

  • Prior experience in residential leasing or a customer-facing sales role
  • Comfort working with property management software for tracking leads and processing applications
  • Strong written and verbal communication, including timely follow-up
  • Ability to manage multiple prospects at different stages of the leasing funnel simultaneously
  • Weekend availability, since that's when most tours happen in any urban submarket

Who Logan Property Management Is

Logan was founded in 2002 and is woman and Latina-led, which is still uncommon in this industry and reflects a deliberate organizational identity. The company started in affordable housing and has since expanded into luxury and conventional properties across California, Colorado, Nevada, and Arizona, managing more than 3,500 units. That breadth matters: staff who grow with Logan often find opportunities to move between markets or property types, including affordable housing, which carries its own compliance and regulatory demands that can be genuinely career-building knowledge.

For a leasing consultant aiming to advance, this kind of multi-vertical operator offers a clearer path than a single-property owner would. Strong performers who build fluency in occupancy metrics, lead conversion, and resident retention are well-positioned to step into assistant manager or property manager roles. In a market like San Diego, where operating costs are high and owner expectations for NOI are tight, leasing performance gets noticed quickly.

job.title: Administrative Assistant
job.description:
It's 9:05 AM and someone in the department just realized the conference room wasn't booked for the 10 o'clock. You fix it before they finish explaining the problem. That's the job.

What This Role Covers

Lincoln Property Company is hiring an Administrative Assistant to support a team in their Dallas office. This is a fully in-office, five-days-a-week position. The work is operational: keeping calendars organized, handling correspondence, maintaining filing systems, processing expense reports and invoices, ordering supplies, and making sure meetings actually happen without friction.

You'll also enter and maintain data in company systems, coordinate onboarding logistics for new team members, and draft or proofread memos and reports. Nothing on this list is glamorous. All of it matters. Lincoln operates one of the largest private commercial real estate portfolios in the country, and the administrative function is what keeps the department's day-to-day moving.

What You Bring

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • At least two years of administrative or clerical experience (commercial real estate background is a plus)
  • Solid command of Microsoft Office, specifically Word, Excel, and Outlook
  • Good written communication skills and attention to detail
  • The ability to manage several tasks at once without being prompted on priorities
  • Current authorization to work in the U.S. (no visa sponsorship available)

The candidates who do well in this kind of role tend to be the ones who treat follow-through as non-negotiable. Drafting a memo is straightforward. Making sure it reaches the right people, in the right format, on time, every time, is where the work actually lives. If you come from a background where you supported multiple people with competing deadlines and figured out the order yourself, that experience translates directly here.

Lincoln offers medical, dental, and vision insurance, a 401(k) with traditional and Roth options, paid time off, company-paid life insurance and long-term disability, and an employee assistance program. Benefits eligibility and coverage details are provided during the hiring process.

job.title: Customer Experience Specialist at The Melrose Apartments
job.description:
Leasing velocity in Nashville's multifamily market has tightened considerably, and properties that convert traffic efficiently are the ones hitting their occupancy targets. The Customer Experience Specialist at The Melrose Apartments is the frontline role that makes that conversion happen. Every prospect who walks in, calls, or texts is a potential lease, and how that interaction goes determines whether the community closes or loses that opportunity.

What the Role Actually Looks Like Day to Day

This is a full-time leasing position with a schedule that includes evenings and weekends, which is standard for any community that wants to capture weekend traffic. You'll greet prospects, residents, and vendors when they enter the office, handle inbound inquiries across phone, email, and text, and maintain detailed records on every interaction. You'll also own the readiness of the tour path, which means daily walks through the vacant units, amenity spaces, and common areas to confirm everything meets Cottonwood's standards before a prospect sees it. A unit that shows poorly is a lease that doesn't close. That connection between physical product and leasing outcome is something you'll feel quickly in this role.

Cottonwood has been an early adopter of Self-Guided Tours, so prospects may arrive having already toured on their own. Your job in those cases shifts toward follow-up, answering pricing questions, and moving them toward a decision. Knowing current availability, pricing, and any applicable concessions cold is essential. You can't convert a prospect who called three hours ago if you have to dig for that information.

Beyond leasing, you'll support community events and social media marketing, manage the package room daily, and maintain vendor communications. These tasks are real parts of the job, not afterthoughts.

What Cottonwood Is Looking For

  • Clear, prompt communication across phone, email, and text with zero dropped inquiries
  • A natural ability to build rapport quickly with prospects and residents at every interaction
  • Attention to the physical details that affect the showing experience and move-in quality
  • Comfort with technology, particularly self-guided tour platforms and digital communication tools
  • Flexibility to work a schedule that includes weekends and some evenings
  • An interest in growing toward a management track over time

Candidates who stand out in this kind of role tend to be the ones who treat follow-up as a reflex, not a task. Responding to a prospect inquiry within minutes versus hours can be the difference between a signed lease and a lost unit. If you've worked in hospitality, retail, or any high-volume customer-facing environment and you've tracked your own performance metrics, that background translates well here.

The compensation package includes a competitive base plus a quarterly bonus structure, full health, vision, dental, life, and disability benefits available within the first 30 days, generous 401k and HSA company matching, three weeks of paid time off in the first year, and 10.5 paid holidays.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Maintenance Technicians at residential communities carry a lot more than a tool belt. They carry the daily experience of every resident who opens a leaky faucet, trips a breaker, or puts in a work order at 8 a.m. hoping someone actually shows up. At Trellis House, that person is you.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Berkshire Group owns and manages its own properties, which means decisions get made closer to the ground than they do at third-party management shops. As a Maintenance Technician here, you're not waiting on a chain of approvals to fix something. You're expected to take ownership of the property's physical condition and keep it there.

Day to day, that means working through service requests across plumbing, electrical, appliances, and carpentry, helping with make-readies between residents, keeping the shop organized, tracking inventory, and making sure the community looks sharp from the curb in. You'll also be a point of contact for residents when things go wrong, which means your customer service instincts matter just as much as your technical ones. The management team leans on maintenance staff heavily, and this role reflects that. You're supporting community standards, enforcing safety protocols, and contributing to how the property is perceived by people who live there and people considering it.

What You Bring to the Team

  • At least one year of hands-on maintenance experience in a residential or similar community setting
  • Working knowledge across the core trades: appliances, plumbing, electrical, carpentry, and general building upkeep
  • Comfort with computers and work order systems
  • Strong written and spoken English communication skills
  • The ability to shift between tasks without losing focus on quality or resident experience

The candidates who tend to stand out in roles like this aren't necessarily the ones with the longest resume. They're the ones who treat a unit turn the same way they treat an emergency call: with attention and follow-through. A willingness to own your punch list, not just close it, makes a noticeable difference on a team like this one.

The Team and the Culture

Berkshire describes itself as people-first, and that framing extends to how they treat staff, not just residents. They offer three weeks of vacation, a 25% rent discount, personal development plans, and solid insurance. The culture leans toward high performance without losing a sense of personality. That combination suits people who take their craft seriously but don't take themselves too seriously.

If you're looking to grow into a lead technician or maintenance supervisor role over time, the in-house ownership model gives you real exposure to how a well-run community operates. You'll learn how physical asset preservation connects to NOI, how curb appeal affects traffic, and how fast maintenance response affects renewal rates. That kind of context is harder to come by than most job postings let on.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Maintenance technicians at affordable housing communities carry a different kind of weight than their counterparts at Class A lease-ups. Residents depend on their homes in a deeper way, and the person who shows up to fix a leaking pipe or a faulty breaker isn't just a service vendor. They're part of why the community functions. Fairstead understands that, and it shapes how they operate their portfolio of more than 30,000 apartments across 28 states.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

This is a full-scope technician role at a Fairstead property in Mobile, Alabama. Your day will move between scheduled work and the unexpected. Preventative maintenance inspections, make-ready prep on vacated units, electrical checks, safety system walkthroughs, and inventory management fill the structured parts of your week. The less predictable parts come from residents: an HVAC issue in August heat, a tripped breaker, a safety concern that can't wait. You'll be part of the on-call rotation, which means some calls come after hours. That's the honest reality of this work, and it's worth knowing upfront.

Fairstead runs an integrated platform where development, construction, and property management sit under one roof. That structure matters for technicians because decisions move faster and the maintenance team isn't an afterthought. You're working within a system that treats physical asset quality as a core part of the mission, not a cost center to minimize.

What You Bring

  • Prior experience as a maintenance or service technician in a residential or similar setting
  • Working knowledge of electrical systems, enough to diagnose problems and handle minor repairs safely
  • General mechanical skills covering plumbing, appliances, fixtures, and building systems
  • HVAC certification, CMRP, or equivalent credential (preferred but not a hard stop)
  • Ability to lift up to 70 pounds unassisted and stay on your feet for extended shifts
  • Clear communication, both with residents who may be frustrated and with a team that depends on accurate handoffs

Attention to detail separates solid technicians from great ones in affordable housing specifically. A punch list item skipped during a make-ready creates problems for a new resident on day one. A missed safety check creates liability. The candidates who do well here are methodical, not just skilled.

The Team and the Bigger Picture

Fairstead describes itself as purpose-driven, and the affordable housing space does attract people who care about more than square footage and cap rates. That doesn't mean the work is easy or the pace is slow. It means the stakes feel real. Residents in these communities aren't choosing to live elsewhere for lifestyle reasons. Keeping their homes functional and safe is straightforward mission-critical work.

Benefits include employer-contributed medical through Meritain Health, employer-paid vision and life insurance, a 401(k) with company matching (100% on the first 3%, 50% on the next 2%), 15 days of PTO, 7 sick days, and 12 or more paid holidays. There's also a flexible spending account, disability coverage, pet insurance, and employee discount programs.

For a technician who wants room to grow, Fairstead's scale means there's a real path toward senior technician, maintenance supervisor, or facilities management roles across a large multi-state portfolio. The company's tech-forward approach also means exposure to digital work order systems and data-driven operations that build skills transferable well beyond any single property.

job.title: Full-Time Concierge (Mon-Fri 4pm-12am)
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is an evening shift role, Monday through Friday, 4pm to midnight, at a Class A residential community in Rockville managed by Comstock. The hours matter: you're the face of the building during the time residents are actually home. That means handling a steady stream of arriving residents, guests, and deliveries, coordinating amenity reservations, managing the loading dock and elevator scheduling, and keeping the lobby looking the part throughout the night. You'll field phone calls, respond to resident concerns, and make judgment calls about building access every single shift.

Daily building walks are part of the rhythm. You're flagging maintenance items, straightening common areas, and doing the small things that keep a Class A property feeling like one. The work is more active than a typical front desk job, and the pace picks up around dinner hours when foot traffic peaks.

What You Bring

  • High school diploma or GED
  • At least one year in a concierge or high-end customer service role, preferably in residential property, hospitality, or a similarly guest-facing environment
  • Comfortable working with Microsoft Office, particularly Outlook, Word, and Excel
  • Ability to work holidays and pick up additional shifts when the schedule requires it
  • Strong communication skills, both written and verbal, and the instinct to handle difficult situations with composure
  • Trustworthy and accountable, two qualities that matter especially when you're working largely unsupervised on an evening shift

Context Worth Knowing

Rockville's mixed-use residential market has grown considerably with Comstock's development around the Shady Grove and Rockville Pike corridors. Residents in these communities tend to have high expectations and many options. The concierge position at this tier of property carries real weight: a confident, polished evening presence directly influences how residents feel about where they live, which connects to renewals and retention in ways that don't always show up on a punch list but absolutely show up in NOI over time.

For candidates with hospitality backgrounds looking to move into property management, this role builds the resident relations instincts that carry well into leasing or property management coordinator positions. Comstock's expanding portfolio also means internal mobility is a realistic path, not just a line in a job posting.

Compensation ranges from $18 to $21 per hour, with bonus potential and a benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, 401(k) match, housing discount, commuter benefits, free parking with EV charging, and parental leave.

job.title: Sr. Regional Real Estate Manager - Pacific Northwest Region
job.description:
Where This Role Lives in the Organization

Regional property management at this level is fundamentally a relationship-management discipline dressed in operational clothing. The financials matter, the inspections matter, the compliance matters. But what separates a strong senior regional manager from a capable one is how well they hold together a web of people: site teams spread across a market, clients with real money and real expectations, and a corporate leadership team that needs accurate information to make good decisions. CloudTen Residential is looking for someone who understands that dynamic and thrives inside it.

CloudTen manages a genuinely varied multifamily portfolio across the West, and their Portland metro group reflects that variety. Hotel-to-residential conversions, high-rise lease-ups, value-add repositioning plays. Each of those asset types carries different operational rhythms, different resident profiles, and different client expectations around performance. The person in this role needs to be comfortable context-switching between a lease-up where traffic and concessions dominate the weekly conversation and a stabilized asset where NOI discipline and delinquency management take center stage.

What the Work Actually Involves

This is a senior leadership position overseeing multiple properties and the managers who run them day-to-day. You're not the person solving a broken HVAC unit at 7am. You're the person who built the team that handles it, coached the manager who escalates it correctly, and reviews the capex line to know whether that unit should be repaired or replaced. The work is a mix of people development, financial oversight, client communication, and strategic planning, and all four have to move together.

Day-to-day, you'll be reviewing monthly financials across the portfolio, preparing and monitoring budgets, and catching variances before they become problems. You'll conduct property inspections with an eye toward operational consistency, not just curb appeal. You'll carry relationships with existing clients and help develop new ones, which means being fluent in how a T-12 tells a story and how to present a repositioning plan that earns trust.

On the people side, you'll provide direct mentorship and oversight to regional managers, assistant regional managers, district and area managers, and property administrators. That's a meaningful leadership span. Performance evaluations, sensitive personnel situations, recruitment, team culture. It all lands here.

Key qualifications CloudTen is looking for:

  • At least five years of directly relevant multifamily experience, ideally at the regional or multi-site level
  • Strong financial acumen, specifically around property financial reports, budget preparation, and income and expense analysis
  • An active real estate license (preferred)
